01
Before the first verse · Vol. 2, p. 537

Opening of the surah

Vol. 2, p. 537
Sūrat Ibrāhīm (Meccan, [except verses 28 and 29, which are Medinan]; its verses are 52 [revealed after Sūrat Nūḥ]). In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة إبراهيم (مكية، [إلا آيتي 28 و 29 فمدنيتان] وآياتها 52 [نزلت بعد سورة نوح] ) بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 14:1–3 · Vol. 2, pp. 537–538

Verses 1 to 3

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. "Alif, Lām, Rā. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you [O Muḥammad] that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light, by permission of their Lord, to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy," (1) "God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment," (2) "those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and avert [people] from the way of God and seek to make it [seem] deviant. Those are in extreme error." (3)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الر كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلى صِراطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ (1) اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَوَيْلٌ لِلْكافِرِينَ مِنْ عَذابٍ شَدِيدٍ (2) الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً أُولئِكَ فِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ (3)
Vol. 2, p. 537
"A Book": it is a book, meaning the sūra. It has also been read li-yukhrija al-nās. "The darknesses" and "the light" are two metaphors for error and guidance. "By permission of their Lord": by His easing and facilitating, borrowed from the permission (idhn) that is an easing of the veil; and that is what He grants them of kindness and success. "To the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy" is a substitute for His saying "to the light," by repetition of the governing particle, as in His saying "for those who were oppressed, for those of them who believed." It is also possible that it is a fresh start, as though it were said: "to what light?" and it was said: "to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy." His saying "God" is an explanatory apposition to "the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy," because it has the status of proper names by its predominance and its specificity to the One worshipped who is deserving of worship, just as "the Star" came to predominate for the Pleiades. It has also been read in the nominative, on "He is God." Al-wayl is the opposite of al-waʾl, which is deliverance; it is a noun of meaning, like "destruction," except that no verb is derived from it; one says only waylan lahu, in the accusative like verbal nouns, and then in the nominative like them to convey the sense of permanence, so one says waylun lahu, like "salāmun ʿalayka." When He mentioned those who come out from the darknesses of unbelief to the light of faith, He threatened the unbelievers with woe.
كِتابٌ هو كتاب، يعنى السورة. وقرئ: ليخرج الناس. والظلمات والنور: استعارتان للضلال والهدى بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ بتسهيله وتيسيره، مستعار من الإذن الذي هو تسهيل للحجاب، وذلك ما يمنحهم من اللطف والتوفيق إِلى صِراطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ بدل من قوله إلى النور بتكرير العامل، كقوله لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ ويجوز أن يكون على وجه الاستئناف، كأنه قيل: إلى أى نور؟ فقيل: إلى صراط العزيز الحميد. وقوله اللَّهِ عطف بيان للعزيز الحميد، لأنه جرى مجرى الأسماء الأعلام لغلبته واختصاصه بالمعبود الذي تحق له العبادة كما غلب النجم في الثريا. وقرئ بالرفع على: هو الله. الويل: نقيض الوأل، وهو النجاة اسم معنى، كالهلاك، إلا أنه لا يشتق منه فعل، إنما يقال: ويلا له، فينصب نصب المصادر، ثم يرفع رفعها لإفادة معنى الثبات، فيقال: ويل له، كقوله سلام عليك. ولما ذكر الخارجين من ظلمات الكفر إلى نور الإيمان توعد الكافرين بالويل.
Question
If you ask: what is the connection of His saying "from a severe punishment" with "woe"?
فإن قلت: ما وجه اتصال قوله مِنْ عَذابٍ شَدِيدٍ بالويل؟
Answer
I say: because the meaning is that they wail from a severe punishment and cry out from it and say "Woe to us!", as in His saying "they will cry out there for destruction." "Those who prefer" is a subject whose predicate is "those are in extreme error." It is also possible that it is in the genitive, as a description of "the disbelievers," or in the accusative in the sense of censure, or in the nominative by an implied "I mean those who prefer" or "they are those who prefer." Al-istiḥbāb is preferring and choosing; it is a form istifʿāl from "love" (maḥabba), because the one who prefers
قلت: لأنّ المعنى أنهم يولولون من عذاب شديد، ويضجون منه، ويقولون: يا ويلاه، كقوله دَعَوْا هُنالِكَ ثُبُوراً الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ مبتدأ خبره: أولئك في ضلال بعيد ويجوز أن يكون مجروراً صفة للكافرين، ومنصوبا على الذمّ، أو مرفوعا على أعنى الذين يستحبون أو هم الذين يستحبون. والاستحباب: الإيثار والاختيار، وهو استفعال من المحبة، لأنّ المؤثر
Vol. 2, p. 538
one thing over another is as though he asks himself that it be more beloved to it and better in its estimation than the other. Al-Ḥasan read yuṣiddūna, with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a kasra on the ṣād. One says ṣaddahu ʿan kadhā and aṣaddahu. [The poet] said: "People who turned people away from them with the sword (1)." The hamza in it enters upon ṣadda, ṣudūdan, to transfer it from the intransitive to the transitive; as for ṣaddahu, it is set up on transitivity like manaʿahu, and it is not eloquent like awqafahu, because the eloquent contented themselves with ṣaddahu and waqafahu rather than going to the trouble of making them transitive by the hamza. "And seek to make it [seem] deviant": they seek for the way of God swerving and crookedness, and to show people that it is a path turning aside from the truth and not straight; the original is "and they seek for it," so the preposition was dropped and the verb made to reach [its object directly]. "In extreme error": they have strayed from the path of the truth and stopped far short of it by many stages.
للشيء على غيره كأنه يطلب من نفسه أن يكون أحبّ إليها وأفضل عندها من الآخر. وقرأ الحسن: ويصدّون، بضم الياء وكسر الصاد. يقال: صدّه عن كذا، وأصدّه. قال: أُنَاسٌ اصَدُّوا النَّاسَ بِالسَّيْفِ عَنْهُمُ «1» والهمزة فيه داخلة على صدّ صدوداً، لتنقله من غير التعدّى إلى التعدّى. وأما صدّه، فموضوع على التعدية كمنعه، وليست بفصيحة كأوقفه، لأنّ الفصحاء استغنوا بصدّه ووقفه عن تكلف التعدية بالهمزة وَيَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً ويطلبون لسبيل الله زيغاً واعوجاجاً، وأن يدلوا الناس على أنها سبيل ناكبة عن الحق غير مستوية، والأصل: ويبغون لها، فحذف الجار وأوصل الفعل فِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ أى ضلوا عن طريق الحق، ووقفوا دونه بمراحل.
Question
If you ask: what is the meaning of describing error as remote?
فإن قلت: فما معنى وصف الضلال بالبعد.
Answer
I say: it is a figurative ascription; the remoteness truly belongs to the one in error, because he is the one who goes far from the path, so his act was described with it, as you say "his earnestness was earnest." It is also possible that the meaning is "in error possessing distance," or "in which there is distance," because the one in error may stray from the road to a near place or a far one.
قلت: هو من الإسناد المجازى، والبعد في الحقيقة للضالّ، لأنه هو الذي يتباعد عن الطريق، فوصف به فعله، كما تقول: جدّ جدّه. ويجوز أن يراد: في ضلال ذى بعد. أو فيه بعد، لأنّ الضالّ قد يضلّ عن الطريق مكاناً قريباً وبعيداً.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 538
1. (1). "People who turned people away from them with the sword / with the repelling of the sawāfī against the noses of the thirsty camels (ḥawāyim)." By Dhū al-Rumma; al-Farrāʾ recited it from him. One says ṣaddahu ʿan kadhā, and in the dialect of Kalb: aṣaddahu ʿanhu when he prevented him, so ṣudūd was put in the place of iṣdād. Al-sawāfī (with fāʾ) are the winds, because they scatter dust. It is also said that it is with qāf, the plural of sāq or sāqiya, which is a channel above the stream. Al-ḥawāyim are thirsty camels, because they circle (taḥūmu) around water; plural of ḥāʾim; it is also applied to a bird which, when its thirst is intense, circles around the water, and when it reaches it its feathers fall and it drowns in it; its plural too is ḥawāyim. It may also be meant here [the camels], or the mountains, because by their height they look out from afar as though circling, or because the birds circle above them, so the ascription of the act to them is figurative because they are its locus. He says: a people who kept people off from themselves with the sword, like the winds' prevention and their striking at the noses of the camels, or at the tops of the mountains; or like watering-men preventing the camels of others from [reaching] their own camels at the drinking; or like the rivers, by the distance of their water, preventing the thirsty camels or the thirsty birds from drinking, because the birds fear drowning in it. It is also related as "ʿan unūf al-ḥawāyim." In it is a comparison of the enemies to the thirsty, and of the swordsmen, or the swords, to the winds, by implication.
2. . Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "That is, so that they understand from him what he calls them to, so that they have no argument..." etc. Aḥmad said: The whole section is satisfactory, but in this ending there is a point for consideration, because it contains an intimation that the inimitability of the Qurʾān, in respect of the Arabic language in particular, falls short of its [full] inimitability, had it been supposed to be sent down in every tongue, such that if it had been sent down in all languages it would have reached such clarity that it would almost be compulsion to believe in it. This is open to question, and holding it is not necessary, because the miracle gives knowledge of the truthfulness of the one at whose hand it appears, and whenever knowledge has been attained, there is no disparity or preferability between one knowledge and another; so if the Qurʾān had been sent down in all languages, the knowledge arising from it, [compared with] its having been sent down in a single language, is [the same] knowledge; and were it sent down in all of them, there is no disparity or preferability between the two knowledges. This is the verification, and God knows best. Al-Zamakhsharī builds, in much of his discourse, on the view that knowledges differ and divide into the clear and the clearer, which is far from the truth, and only a faction of the Ẓāhirīs thought that. And God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . أناس أصدوا الناس بالسيف عنهم
…. صدود السواني في أنوف الحوايم لذي الرمة، أنشده عنه الفراء، يقال: صده عن كذا، ولغة كلب: أصده عنه إذا منعه، فوضع الصدود موضع الأصداد. والسيافى- بالفاء-: الرياح، لأنها تسفو التراب. وقيل: هي بالقاف جمع ساق أو ساقية، وهي فوق الجدول. والحوايم: الجمال العطاش، لأنها تحوم حول الماء جمع حائم، ويطلق على طير إذا اشتد عطشه حام حول الماء، فإذا ناله سقط ريشه فيغرق فيه. وجمعه حوايم أيضا. ويجوز أن يراد هنا، أو الجبال لأنها لارتفاعها تشرف من بعد كأنها حائمة، أو لأن الطير يحوم فوقها فنسبة الفعل إليها مجاز لأنها محله، يقول: قوم منعوا الناس عن أنفسهم بالسيف لمنع الرياح وضربها في أنوف. الجمال، أو في أعالى الجبال، أو كمنع السقاة إبل غيرهم عن إبلهم في السقي، أو كمنع الأنهار لبعد مائها الإبل العطاش أو الطيور العطاش عن الشرب، لأن الطيور تخاف الغرق فيه. ويروى: عن أنوف الحوايم. وفيه تشبيه الأعداء بالعطاش وأصحاب السيوف، أو السيوف بالرياح ضمنا.
2. . قال محمود: «أى ليفقهوا عنه ما يدعوهم إليه فلا يكون لهم حجة
…. الخ» قال أحمد: جميع الفصل مرضى، لكن في هذه الخاتمة نظر، لأن فيها إشعاراً بأن إعجاز القرآن من حيث اللغة العربية خاصة يتقاصر عن إعجازه، لو قدر منزلا بكل لسان، حتى إنه لو ينزل بجميع اللغات لبلغ من الوضوح إلى حد يكاد أن يكون إلجاء إلى الايمان به، وهذا فيه نظر، والقول به غير متعين، لأن المعجز يفيد العلم بصدق من ظهر على يده، ومتى حصل العلم لم يكن بين علم وعلم تفاوت ولا ترجيح، فلو نزل القرآن بجميع اللغات، لكان العلم الحاصل منه وقد نزل بلغة واحدة، هو العلم الحاصل منه ولو نزل بالجميع، لا تفاوت ولا ترجيح بين العلمين، هذا هو التحقيق، والله أعلم. والزمخشري يبنى في كثير من كلامه على أن العلوم تتفاوت وتنقسم إلى جلى وأجلى، وهو من الحق بمعزل، وإنما ظن ذلك طائفة ظاهرية، والله الموفق.
03
Q 14:4 · Vol. 2, pp. 538–540

Verse 4

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them. Then God sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." (4)
وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلاَّ بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (4)
Vol. 2, p. 538
"Except in the language of his people, to state clearly for them": that is, so that they understand from him what he calls them to, so that they have no argument against God (2)
إِلَّا بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ أى ليفقهوا عنه ما يدعوهم إليه، فلا يكون لهم حجة على الله «2»
Vol. 2, p. 539
and they not say: "We did not understand what we were addressed with," as He said, "And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qurʾān, they would have said: 'Why are its verses not made clear?'"
ولا يقولوا: لم نفهم ما خوطبنا به، كما قال وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآناً أَعْجَمِيًّا لَقالُوا لَوْلا فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ.
Question
If you ask: the Messenger of God ﷺ was not sent to the Arabs alone; he was sent to all people: "Say, 'O people, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all,'" indeed to the two weighty creatures [humans and jinn], and they are of differing tongues; so if the Arabs have no argument [because it is in Arabic], then others have an argument; and if others have no argument, then had it been sent down in a non-Arabic tongue, the Arabs also would have had no argument.
فإن قلت: لم يبعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى العرب وحدهم، وإنما بعث إلى الناس جميعاً قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعاً بل إلى الثقلين، وهم على ألسنة مختلفة، فإن لم تكن للعرب حجه فلغيرهم الحجة وإن لم تكن لغيرهم حجة فلو نزل بالعجمية، لم تكن للعرب حجة أيضاً.
Answer
I say: it cannot be other than that it be sent down in all tongues or in one of them; and there is no need for its being sent down in all tongues, because translation stands in for that and spares the lengthiness; so there remains that it be sent down in a single tongue, and the most fitting of tongues was the tongue of the people of the Messenger, because they are nearest to him; so when they understood from him and grasped it, and it was transmitted from them and spread, translators stood up to explain and convey it, as you see the situation and witness it from the deputizing of translators in every non-Arab nation; together with what there is in that of the agreement of the people of distant lands, remote regions (1), differing nations and unequal generations upon one Book, and their striving to learn its wording and learn its meanings, and what branches off from that of great benefits, and what multiplies, in the wearying of souls and the toil of minds in it, of acts of nearness and obedience leading to abundant reward; and because it is further from distortion and alteration, and safer from dispute and disagreement; and because, had it been sent down in the tongues of the two weighty creatures all together, despite their differing and multiplicity, and had it been independently possessed of the attribute of inimitability in each one of them, and had the Arab Messenger spoken to each nation in its own tongue as he spoke to his own community, of which he is, reciting it to them as an inimitable miracle, that would have been a matter close to compulsion. The meaning of "in the language of his people" is "in the language of his people." It has also been read bi-lisni qawmihi. Al-lisn and al-lisān are like al-rīsh and al-riyāsh, in the sense of language. It has also been read bi-lusuni qawmihi, with a ḍamma on the lām and the sīn with a ḍamma or a sukūn, which is the plural of lisān, like ʿimād, ʿumud and ʿumd in the lightened form. It is also said that the pronoun in "his people" refers to Muḥammad ﷺ and they report it from al-Ḍaḥḥāk; and that all the Books were sent down in Arabic, then each prophet delivered them in the language of his people; but this is not sound, because "to state clearly for them," the pronoun of "the people," refers to the Arabs, which leads to God having sent down the Torah from heaven in Arabic to make it clear to the Arabs, and this is a corrupt meaning. "Then God sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills" is like His saying "so among you is the disbeliever and among you is the believer," because God leads astray only him of whom He knows that he will not believe, and guides only him of whom He knows that he will believe. What is meant by leading astray is abandonment and the withholding of kindnesses (2), and by guidance, success and kindness, so that is a metonym for unbelief and belief. "And He is the Exalted in Might," so He is not overcome in His will; "the Wise," so He does not abandon any but those who deserve abandonment, and does not show kindness except to those who deserve kindness.
قلت: لا يخلو إمّا أن ينزل بجميع الألسنة أو بواحد منها، فلا حاجة إلى نزوله بجميع الألسنة، لأن الترجمة تنوب عن ذلك وتكفى التطويل، فبقى أن ينزل بلسان واحد، فكان أولى الألسنة لسان قوم الرسول، لأنهم أقرب إليه، فإذا فهموا عنه وتبينوه وتنوقل عنهم وانتشر. قامت التراجم ببيانه وتفهيمه، كما ترى الحال وتشاهدها من نيابة التراجم في كل أمّة من أمم العجم، مع ما في ذلك من اتفاق أهل البلاد المتباعدة، والأقطار المتنازحة، «1» والأمم المختلفة والأجيال المتفاوتة، على كتاب واحد، واجتهادهم في تعلم لفظه وتعلم معانيه، وما يتشعب من ذلك من جلائل الفوائد، وما يتكاثر في إتعاب النفوس وكدّ القرائح فيه، من القرب والطاعات المفضية إلى جزيل الثواب، ولأنه أبعد من التحريف والتبديل، وأسلم من التنازع والاختلاف، ولأنه لو نزل بألسنة الثقلين كلها- مع اختلافها وكثرتها، وكان مستقلا بصفة الإعجاز في كل واحد منها، وكلم الرسول العربىّ كل أمّة بلسانها كما كلم أمّته التي هو منها يتلوه عليهم معجزاً- لكان ذلك أمراً قريباً من الإلجاء. ومعنى بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ بلغة قومه. وقرئ: بلسن قومه. واللسن واللسان: كالريش والرياش، بمعنى اللغة. وقرئ: «بلسن قومه» بضم اللام والسين مضمومة أو ساكنة، وهو جمع لسان، كعماد وعمد وعمد على التخفيف. وقيل: الضمير في قومه لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ورووه عن الضحاك. وأن الكتب كلها نزلت بالعربية، ثم أدّاها كل نبىّ بلغة قومه، وليس بصحيح، لأنّ قوله لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ ضمير القوم وهم العرب، فيؤدّى إلى أن الله أنزل التوراة من السماء بالعربية ليبين للعرب، وهذا معنى فاسد فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ كقوله فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ لأنّ الله لا يضلّ إلا من يعلم أنه لن يؤمن. ولا يهدى إلا من يعلم أنه يؤمن. والمراد بالإضلال: التخلية ومنع الألطاف «2» ، وبالهداية: التوفيق واللطف، فكان ذلك كناية عن الكفر والإيمان وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ فلا يغلب على مشيئته الْحَكِيمُ فلا يخذل إلا أهل الخذلان، ولا يلطف إلا بأهل اللطف
Vol. 2, p. 540
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 538
1. (1). "People who turned people away from them with the sword / with the repelling of the sawāfī against the noses of the thirsty camels (ḥawāyim)." By Dhū al-Rumma; al-Farrāʾ recited it from him. One says ṣaddahu ʿan kadhā, and in the dialect of Kalb: aṣaddahu ʿanhu when he prevented him, so ṣudūd was put in the place of iṣdād. Al-sawāfī (with fāʾ) are the winds, because they scatter dust. It is also said that it is with qāf, the plural of sāq or sāqiya, which is a channel above the stream. Al-ḥawāyim are thirsty camels, because they circle (taḥūmu) around water; plural of ḥāʾim; it is also applied to a bird which, when its thirst is intense, circles around the water, and when it reaches it its feathers fall and it drowns in it; its plural too is ḥawāyim. It may also be meant here [the camels], or the mountains, because by their height they look out from afar as though circling, or because the birds circle above them, so the ascription of the act to them is figurative because they are its locus. He says: a people who kept people off from themselves with the sword, like the winds' prevention and their striking at the noses of the camels, or at the tops of the mountains; or like watering-men preventing the camels of others from [reaching] their own camels at the drinking; or like the rivers, by the distance of their water, preventing the thirsty camels or the thirsty birds from drinking, because the birds fear drowning in it. It is also related as "ʿan unūf al-ḥawāyim." In it is a comparison of the enemies to the thirsty, and of the swordsmen, or the swords, to the winds, by implication.
2. . Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "That is, so that they understand from him what he calls them to, so that they have no argument..." etc. Aḥmad said: The whole section is satisfactory, but in this ending there is a point for consideration, because it contains an intimation that the inimitability of the Qurʾān, in respect of the Arabic language in particular, falls short of its [full] inimitability, had it been supposed to be sent down in every tongue, such that if it had been sent down in all languages it would have reached such clarity that it would almost be compulsion to believe in it. This is open to question, and holding it is not necessary, because the miracle gives knowledge of the truthfulness of the one at whose hand it appears, and whenever knowledge has been attained, there is no disparity or preferability between one knowledge and another; so if the Qurʾān had been sent down in all languages, the knowledge arising from it, [compared with] its having been sent down in a single language, is [the same] knowledge; and were it sent down in all of them, there is no disparity or preferability between the two knowledges. This is the verification, and God knows best. Al-Zamakhsharī builds, in much of his discourse, on the view that knowledges differ and divide into the clear and the clearer, which is far from the truth, and only a faction of the Ẓāhirīs thought that. And God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . أناس أصدوا الناس بالسيف عنهم
…. صدود السواني في أنوف الحوايم لذي الرمة، أنشده عنه الفراء، يقال: صده عن كذا، ولغة كلب: أصده عنه إذا منعه، فوضع الصدود موضع الأصداد. والسيافى- بالفاء-: الرياح، لأنها تسفو التراب. وقيل: هي بالقاف جمع ساق أو ساقية، وهي فوق الجدول. والحوايم: الجمال العطاش، لأنها تحوم حول الماء جمع حائم، ويطلق على طير إذا اشتد عطشه حام حول الماء، فإذا ناله سقط ريشه فيغرق فيه. وجمعه حوايم أيضا. ويجوز أن يراد هنا، أو الجبال لأنها لارتفاعها تشرف من بعد كأنها حائمة، أو لأن الطير يحوم فوقها فنسبة الفعل إليها مجاز لأنها محله، يقول: قوم منعوا الناس عن أنفسهم بالسيف لمنع الرياح وضربها في أنوف. الجمال، أو في أعالى الجبال، أو كمنع السقاة إبل غيرهم عن إبلهم في السقي، أو كمنع الأنهار لبعد مائها الإبل العطاش أو الطيور العطاش عن الشرب، لأن الطيور تخاف الغرق فيه. ويروى: عن أنوف الحوايم. وفيه تشبيه الأعداء بالعطاش وأصحاب السيوف، أو السيوف بالرياح ضمنا.
2. . قال محمود: «أى ليفقهوا عنه ما يدعوهم إليه فلا يكون لهم حجة
…. الخ» قال أحمد: جميع الفصل مرضى، لكن في هذه الخاتمة نظر، لأن فيها إشعاراً بأن إعجاز القرآن من حيث اللغة العربية خاصة يتقاصر عن إعجازه، لو قدر منزلا بكل لسان، حتى إنه لو ينزل بجميع اللغات لبلغ من الوضوح إلى حد يكاد أن يكون إلجاء إلى الايمان به، وهذا فيه نظر، والقول به غير متعين، لأن المعجز يفيد العلم بصدق من ظهر على يده، ومتى حصل العلم لم يكن بين علم وعلم تفاوت ولا ترجيح، فلو نزل القرآن بجميع اللغات، لكان العلم الحاصل منه وقد نزل بلغة واحدة، هو العلم الحاصل منه ولو نزل بالجميع، لا تفاوت ولا ترجيح بين العلمين، هذا هو التحقيق، والله أعلم. والزمخشري يبنى في كثير من كلامه على أن العلوم تتفاوت وتنقسم إلى جلى وأجلى، وهو من الحق بمعزل، وإنما ظن ذلك طائفة ظاهرية، والله الموفق.
Vol. 2, p. 539
1. (1). His statement "wa-l-aqṭār al-mutanāziḥa": that is, extremely distant. Al-Ṣiḥāḥ gives this. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "what is meant by leading astray is abandonment and the withholding of kindnesses": this is according to the Muʿtazila. As for the Ahl al-Sunna, it is the creation of error in the heart, because God, according to the Muʿtazila, does not create evil, whereas according to the Ahl al-Sunna He creates it as He creates good. (ʿ)

04
Q 14:5 · Vol. 2, p. 540

Verse 5

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], 'Bring out your people from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of God.' Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful." (5)
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ (5)
Vol. 2, p. 540
"An akhrij" is in the sense of "that is: bring out," because the sending contains the sense of speaking, as though it were said: "We sent him and said to him: bring out." It is also possible that an is the particle that governs the subjunctive; it is proper to link it to an imperative verb, because the purpose is to connect it with what, together with it, comes to be interpreted as a verbal noun, and that is the verb, and the imperative and other forms are alike in being verbal. The proof that it may be the particle governing the subjunctive is their saying awʿaza ilayhi bi-an ifʿal, where they brought the preposition in upon it. So too the implied meaning is "bi-an akhrij qawmaka." "And remind them of the days of God": warn them of His battles that befell the nations before them: the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd. From this are the "days of the Arabs," for their wars and battles, like the Day of Dhū Qār, the Day of al-Fijār, the Day of Qaḍa and others, and this is the apparent sense. From Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with both: His blessings and His trials. So the destruction of generations is for "everyone patient and grateful," who is patient in God's trial and grateful for His blessings; so when he hears of the trial God sent down upon the nations, or the blessings He poured upon them, he is alerted to what is obligatory for him of patience and gratitude, and takes a lesson. It is also said that He meant every believer, because gratitude and patience are among their characteristics, as an alert to them.
أَنْ أَخْرِجْ بمعنى أى أخرج، لأنّ الإرسال فيه معنى القول، كأنه قيل: أرسلناه وقلنا له أخرج. ويجوز أن تكون أن الناصبة للفعل، وإنما صلح أن توصل بفعل الأمر، لأنّ الغرض وصلها بما تكون معه في تأويل المصدر وهو الفعل والأمر، وغيره سواء في الفعلية. والدليل على جواز أن تكون الناصبة للفعل: قولهم أو عز إليه بأن افعل، فأدخلوا عليها حرف الجر. وكذلك التقدير بأن أخرج قومك وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ وأنذرهم بوقائعه التي وقعت على الأمم قبلهم: قوم نوح وعاد وثمود. ومنه أيام العرب لحروبها وملاحمها، كيوم ذى قار، ويوم الفجار، ويوم قضة وغيرها، وهو الظاهر. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: نعماؤه وبلاؤه. فإهلاك القرون لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ يصبر على بلاء الله ويشكر نعماءه، فإذا سمع بما أنزل الله من البلاء على الأمم، أو أفاض عليهم من النعم، تنبه على ما يجب عليه من الصبر والشكر واعتبر. وقيل: أراد لكل مؤمن، لأنّ الشكر والصبر من سجاياهم، تنبيهاً عليهم.

05
Q 14:6 · Vol. 2, pp. 540–541

Verse 6

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And [recall] when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of God upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment and were slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.'" (6)
وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنْجاكُمْ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِساءَكُمْ وَفِي ذلِكُمْ بَلاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (6)
Vol. 2, p. 540
"When He saved you" is an adverbial for "favor" in the sense of bestowing favor, that is, His bestowing favor upon you at that time.
إِذْ أَنْجاكُمْ ظرف للنعمة بمعنى الإنعام، أى إنعامه عليكم ذلك الوقت.
Question
If you ask: is it permissible that it be governed by "upon you"?
فإن قلت: هل يجوز أن ينتصب بعليكم؟
Answer
I say: it cannot be other than that it is either a complement of "favor" in the sense of bestowing favor, or not a complement, if by "favor" you mean the gift; if it is a complement it does not govern it, and if it is not a complement, in the sense of "remember the favor of God settled upon you," it governs it, and the difference between the two ways becomes clear (1) in that when you say "the favor of God upon you," if you make it a complement it is not a complete utterance until you say "abundant" or the like; otherwise it is a complete utterance. It is also possible that "idh" is a substitute for "the favor of God," that is: remember the time of your being saved; and it is a substitution of inclusion.
قلت: لا يخلو من أن يكون صلة للنعمة بمعنى الإنعام، أو غير صلة إذا أردت بالنعمة العطية، فإذا كان صلة لم يعمل فيه، وإذا كان غير صلة بمعنى اذكروا نعمة الله مستقرّة عليكم عمل فيه، ويتبين «1» الفرق بين الوجهين أنك إذا قلت: نعمة الله عليكم، فإن جعلته صلة لم يكن كلاماً حتى تقول فائضة أو نحوها، وإلا كان كلاما. ويجوز أن يكون «إذ» بدلا من نعمة الله، أى: اذكروا وقت إنجائكم، وهو من بدل الاشتمال.
Question
If you ask: in Sūrat al-Baqara it is yudhabbiḥūna, in al-Aʿrāf yuqattilūna, and here wa-yudhabbiḥūna with the wāw, so what is the difference?
فإن قلت: في سورة البقرة يُذَبِّحُونَ وفي الأعراف يُقَتِّلُونَ وهاهنا وَيُذَبِّحُونَ مع الواو، فما الفرق؟
Answer
I say: the difference is that where the wāw was dropped, the slaughtering was made an explanation of the torment and a clarification of it, and where it was kept, the slaughtering was set apart because it was more complete in regard to
قلت: الفرق أنّ التذبيح حيث طرح الواو جعل تفسيراً للعذاب وبياناً له، وحيث أثبت جعل التذبيح لأنه أو في على
Vol. 2, p. 541
the kind of torment, and was added to it with an evident addition, as though it were another kind.
جنس العذاب، وزاد عليه زيادة ظاهرة كأنه جنس آخر.
Question
If you ask: how could what the people of Pharaoh did be a trial from their Lord?
فإن قلت: كيف كان فعل آل فرعون بلاء من ربهم؟
Answer
I say: His giving them power and respite until they did what they did was a trial from God. There is also another way, which is that "that" is a reference to the saving, which is a great trial, and trial (balāʾ) can be testing by blessing and by affliction together. God, Exalted is He, said: "And We test you with evil and with good as a trial," and Zuhayr said: "So He tried the two with the best of the trials by which He tries (1)."
قلت: تمكينهم وإمهالهم، حتى فعلوا ما فعلوا ابتلاء من الله. ووجه آخر وهو أن ذلك إشارة إلى الإنجاء وهو بلاء عظيم، والبلاء يكون ابتلاء بالنعمة والمحنة جميعا، قال تعالى وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وقال زهير: فَأَبْلَاهُمَا خَيرَ البَلَاءِ الذِى يَبْلُوا «1»

Vol. 2, p. 540

06
Q 14:7 · Vol. 2, p. 541

Verse 7

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will certainly increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'" (7)
وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ وَلَئِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذابِي لَشَدِيدٌ (7)
Vol. 2, p. 541
"And when your Lord proclaimed" is part of what Moses said to his people, and its accusative is by coordination with His saying "the favor of God upon you," as though it were said: "And when Moses said to his people: remember the favor of God upon you, and remember when your Lord proclaimed." The meaning of taʾadhdhana rabbukum is "your Lord gave notice" (adhina). A parallel of taʾadhdhana and adhina: tawaʿʿada and awʿada, tafaḍḍala and afḍala. In the form tafaʿʿala there must be an added meaning not in afʿala, as though it were said: "and when your Lord gave notice, a thorough notice, by which doubts are removed and uncertainties dispelled." The meaning is: "and when your Lord proclaimed, then said: 'If you are grateful'"; or taʾadhdhana was treated as "he said," because it is a kind of saying. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "wa-idh qāla rabbukum la-in shakartum," that is, if you are grateful, O Children of Israel, for what I have bestowed upon you of the blessing of rescue and other blessings, with pure faith and righteous deed, "I will surely increase you" blessing upon blessing, and I will double for you what I gave you; "but if you deny" and belittle (2) what I have favored you with, "indeed, My punishment is severe" for one who denies My blessing.
وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ من جملة ما قال مومى لقومه، وانتصابه للعطف على قوله نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ كأنه قيل: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم، واذكروا حين تأذن ربكم. ومعنى تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ: أذن ربكم. ونظير تأذن وأذن: توعد وأوعد، تفضل وأفضل. ولا بدّ في تفعل من زيادة معنى ليس في أفعل، كأنه قيل: وإذ أذن ربكم إيذانا بليغا تنتفى عنده الشكوك وتنزاح الشبه. والمعنى: وإذ تأذن ربكم فقال لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ أو أجرى تَأَذَّنَ مجرى، قال، لأنه ضرب من القول. وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: «وإذ قال ربكم لئن شكرتم» ، أى لئن شكرتم يا بنى إسرائيل ما خولتكم من نعمة الإنجاء وغيرها من النعم بالإيمان الخالص والعمل الصالح لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ نعمة إلى نعمة، ولأضاعفن لكم ما آتيتكم وَلَئِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ وغمطتم «2» ما أنعمت به عليكم إِنَّ عَذابِي لَشَدِيدٌ لمن كفر نعمتي.

07
Q 14:8 · Vol. 2, p. 541

Verse 8

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And Moses said, 'If you disbelieve, you and those on earth entirely, indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.'" (8)
وَقالَ مُوسى إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا أَنْتُمْ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ (8)
Vol. 2, p. 541
And Moses said: if you disbelieve, you, O Children of Israel, and all the people, you have only harmed yourselves and deprived them of the good which you cannot do without and of which you are in need; "God is Free of need" of your gratitude, "Praiseworthy," deserving of praise by the abundance of His favors and gifts, even if the praisers do not praise Him.
وَقالَ مُوسى إن كفرتم أنتم يا بنى إسرائيل والناس كلهم، فإنما ضررتم أنفسكم وحرمتموها الخير الذي لا بدّ لكم منه وأنتم إليه محاويج، اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عن شكركم حَمِيدٌ مستوجب للحمد بكثرة أنعمه وأياديه، وإن لم يحمده الحامدون.

08
Q 14:9 · Vol. 2, pp. 541–542

Verse 9

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"Has there not reached you the news of those before you, the people of Noah and ʿĀd and Thamūd, and those after them? None knows them but God. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they returned their hands to their mouths and said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt.'" (9)
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَؤُا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْواهِهِمْ وَقالُوا إِنَّا كَفَرْنا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّا لَفِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَنا إِلَيْهِ مُرِيبٍ (9)
Vol. 2, p. 542
"And those after them, none knows them but God": a sentence of subject and predicate, which occurs as a parenthesis; or "those after them" is coordinated to "the people of Noah," and "none knows them but God" is the parenthesis. The meaning is: they are so many that none knows their number but God. From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ: between ʿAdnān and Ismāʿīl there are thirty fathers who are unknown; and Ibn Masʿūd, when he recited this verse, used to say: "The genealogists have lied," meaning that they claim knowledge of lineages, while God has negated the knowledge of them from the servants. "But they returned their hands to their mouths": they bit them in rage and vexation at what the messengers brought (1), as in His saying "they bite at you the fingertips in rage"; or in laughter and mockery, like one overcome by laughter who puts his hand on his mouth; or they pointed with their hands to their tongues and to what these had uttered of their saying "we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent," that is, this is our answer to you, we have nothing else, to make them despair of [their] acceptance. Do you not see His saying "they returned their hands to their mouths and said: 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent'"? And this is a strong view. Or they placed them over their mouths, saying to the prophets: "Close your mouths and be silent." Or they put them back into the mouths of the prophets, signaling to them to be silent. Or they placed them upon their [own] mouths, silencing them and not letting them speak. It is also said: al-aydī is the plural of yad, which is the favor (niʿma), like al-ayādī, that is: they returned the favors of the prophets, which are the greatest of favors, of their exhortations and counsels and what was revealed to them of laws and signs, into their mouths, because when they denied them and did not accept them, it was as though they sent them back into their mouths and returned them to where they came from, by way of parable. "To that to which you invite us": of belief in God. It has been read tadʿūnā with assimilation of the nūn. "Disquieting" (murīb) means putting into doubt, or possessing doubt, from arābahu and arāba (2) the man, which is restlessness of the soul and not being at ease about the matter.
وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ جملة من مبتدإ وخبر، وقعت اعتراضا: أو عطف الذين من بعدهم على قوم نوح. ولا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ اعتراض. والمعنى: أنهم من الكثرة بحيث لا يعلم عددهم إلا الله. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: بين عدنان وإسماعيل ثلاثون أبا لا يعرفون، وكان ابن مسعود إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال: كذب النسابون، يعنى أنهم يدّعون علم الأنساب، وقد نفى الله علمها عن العباد فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْواهِهِمْ فعضوها غيظا وضجرا مما جاءت به الرسل «1» ، كقوله عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَنامِلَ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ أو ضحكا واستهزاء كمن غلبه الضحك فوضع يده على فيه. أو وأشاروا بأيديهم إلى ألسنتهم وما نطقت به من قولهم إِنَّا كَفَرْنا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ أى هذا جوابنا لكم ليس عندنا غيره، إقناطاً لهم من التصديق. ألا ترى إلى قوله فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْواهِهِمْ وَقالُوا إِنَّا كَفَرْنا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ وهذا قول قوى. أو وضعوها على أفواههم يقولون للأنبياء: أطبقوا أفواهكم واسكتوا. أو ردّوها في أفواه الأنبياء يشيرون لهم إلى السكوت. أو وضعوها على أفواههم يسكتونهم ولا يذرونهم يتكلمون. وقيل: الأيدى، جمع يد وهي النعمة بمعنى الأيادى، أى: ردوا نعم الأنبياء التي هي أجل النعم من مواعظهم ونصائحهم وما أوحى إليهم من الشرائع والآيات في أفواههم، لأنهم إذا كذبوها ولم يقبلوها، فكأنهم ردوها في أفواههم ورجعوها إلى حيث جاءت منه على طريق المثل مِمَّا تَدْعُونَنا إِلَيْهِ من الإيمان بالله. وقرئ: «تدعونا» ، بإدغام النون مُرِيبٍ موقع في الريبة أو ذى ريبة، من أرابه، وأراب «2» الرجل، وهي قلق النفس وأن لا تطمئن إلى الأمر.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 541
1. (1). The explanation of this poetic proof-text has preceded in this Part, page 208; consult it if you wish. End of the editor's note.
2. . His statement "wa-ghamaṭtum mā anʿamtu bihi ʿalaykum": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, ghamaṭa al-shayʾ means he became insolent toward it and despised it. (ʿ)
1. (1) . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بهذا الجزء صفحة 208 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
2. . قوله «وغمطتم ما أنعمت به عليكم» في الصحاح «غمط الشيء» بطره وحقره. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 542
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "Its meaning is: they bit them in rage and vexation at what the messengers brought..." etc. Aḥmad said: The strongest of these views is this one, which the author noted as distinguished by strength; and it is so because making the messengers despair of belief, in word and deed, by placing the hand in the mouth, is what suits their envy in unbelief. And the opening of the expression with the emphatic particle, and facing the messengers with pronouns of address, and repeating that, is exaggeration in emphasis; and the context is not suited to laughter, nor rage, nor silencing the messengers, as it is suited to making them despair of acceptance. Do you not see that when they replied to the messengers with speech and did not rebuke them for returning to disputation, this indicates that they had not silenced them at first, nor was that their aim? And God knows best.
2. . His statement "wa-arāba al-rajul": perhaps it should be "aw arāba." (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «معناه عضوها غيظا وضجرا مما جاءت به الرسل
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وأقوى هذه الوجوه هذا الوجه الذي نبه المصنف على اختصاصه بالقوة، وإنما كان كذلك لأن إقناطهم الرسل من الايمان قولا وفعلا بوضع اليد في الفم، هو المناسب لحسدهم في الكفر. وتصدير العبارة بالحرف المؤكد ومواجهة الرسل بضمائر الخطاب وإعادة ذلك مبالغة في التأكيد وليس السياق بمناسب الضحك ولا الغيظ ولا لتصميت الرسل كمناسبته لاقناطهم من القبول. ألا ترى أنهم لما أعادوا للرسل القول ولم ينكروا عليهم عودهم إلى المجادلة، دل على أنهم لم يسكتوهم أولا، ولا كان غرضهم ذلك، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «وأراب الرجل» لعله: أو أراب. (ع)
09
Q 14:10 · Vol. 2, pp. 542–544

Verse 10

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"Their messengers said, 'Can there be doubt about God, Creator of the heavens and earth? He invites you to forgive you of your sins and to defer you for a specified term.' They said, 'You are not but men like us who wish to avert us from what our fathers [used to] worship. So bring us a clear authority.'" (10)
قالَتْ رُسُلُهُمْ أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرَكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى قالُوا إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَصُدُّونا عَمَّا كانَ يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا فَأْتُونا بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ (10)
Vol. 2, p. 542
"Can there be doubt about God": the hamza of denial entered upon the adverbial, because the speech is not about the doubt itself but about the thing doubted, and that it does not admit doubt because of the clarity of the proofs and their witness to it. "He invites you to forgive you of your sins"
أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ أدخلت همزة الإنكار على الظرف، لأن الكلام ليس في الشك، إنما هو في المشكوك فيه، وأنه لا يحتمل الشك لظهور الأدلة وشهادتها عليه يَدْعُوكُمْ لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ
Vol. 2, p. 543
that is, He calls you to faith in order to forgive you, or He calls you for the sake of forgiveness, as in "I called him that he might help me" and "I called him that he might eat with me." [The poet] said: "I called Miswar for what befell me, and he answered, answered, the two hands of Miswar (1)."
أى يدعوكم إلى الإيمان ليغفر لكم أو يدعوكم لأجل المغفرة كقوله: دعوته لينصرنى، ودعوته ليأكل معى، وقال: دَعَوْتُ لِمَا نَابَنِى مِسْوَرا … فَلَبَّى فَلَبَّى يَدَىْ مِسْوَرِ «1»
Question
If you ask: what is the meaning of the partitive "min" in "of your sins"?
فإن قلت: ما معنى التبعيض في قوله: من ذنوبكم؟
Answer
I say: I know it to have come thus only in the address to unbelievers, as in His saying "and fear Him and obey me; He will forgive you of your sins," "O our people, respond to the Caller of God and believe in him; He will forgive you of your sins"; and He said in the address to believers: "Shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?" until He said "He will forgive you your sins," and others that inductive survey will make known to you; and that was to differentiate between the two addresses, and so that the two groups not be made equal in the promise. It is also said: what is meant is that He forgives them what is between them and God, unlike what is between them and the servants of wrongs and the like. "And to defer you for a specified term": until a time God has named and made clear its extent, He will bring you to it if you believe, and otherwise He will hasten you to destruction before that time. "You are not but men like us": there is no superiority between us and you, and no superiority for you over us, so why are you singled out for prophethood (2) rather than us? And had God sent messengers to humankind He would have made them of a kind better than they, namely the angels (3). "A clear authority": a clear proof; though their messengers had come to them with clear proofs and arguments, by "a clear authority" they meant only a sign that they had proposed out of obstinacy and contentiousness.
قلت: ما علمته جاء هكذا إلا في خطاب الكافرين، كقوله وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ، يا قَوْمَنا أَجِيبُوا داعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وقال في خطاب المؤمنين: هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ إلى أن قال يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وغير ذلك مما يقفك عليه الاستقراء، وكان ذلك للتفرقة بين الخطابين، ولئلا يسوى بين الفريقين في الميعاد. وقيل: أريد أنه يغفر لهم ما بينهم وبين الله، بخلاف ما بينهم وبين العباد من المظالم ونحوها وَيُؤَخِّرَكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى إلى وقت قد سماه الله وبين مقداره، يبلغكموه إن آمنتم، وإلا عاجلكم بالهلاك قبل ذلك الوقت إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ما أنتم إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا لا فضل بيننا وبينكم، ولا فضل لكم علينا، فلم تخصون بالنبوّة «2» دوننا، ولو أرسل الله إلى البشر رسلا لجعلهم من جنس أفضل منهم وهم الملائكة «3» بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ بحجة بينة، وقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات والحجج، وإنما أرادوا بالسلطان المبين آية قد اقترحوها تعنتاً ولجاجا.
Vol. 2, p. 544
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 542
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "Its meaning is: they bit them in rage and vexation at what the messengers brought..." etc. Aḥmad said: The strongest of these views is this one, which the author noted as distinguished by strength; and it is so because making the messengers despair of belief, in word and deed, by placing the hand in the mouth, is what suits their envy in unbelief. And the opening of the expression with the emphatic particle, and facing the messengers with pronouns of address, and repeating that, is exaggeration in emphasis; and the context is not suited to laughter, nor rage, nor silencing the messengers, as it is suited to making them despair of acceptance. Do you not see that when they replied to the messengers with speech and did not rebuke them for returning to disputation, this indicates that they had not silenced them at first, nor was that their aim? And God knows best.
2. . His statement "wa-arāba al-rajul": perhaps it should be "aw arāba." (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «معناه عضوها غيظا وضجرا مما جاءت به الرسل
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وأقوى هذه الوجوه هذا الوجه الذي نبه المصنف على اختصاصه بالقوة، وإنما كان كذلك لأن إقناطهم الرسل من الايمان قولا وفعلا بوضع اليد في الفم، هو المناسب لحسدهم في الكفر. وتصدير العبارة بالحرف المؤكد ومواجهة الرسل بضمائر الخطاب وإعادة ذلك مبالغة في التأكيد وليس السياق بمناسب الضحك ولا الغيظ ولا لتصميت الرسل كمناسبته لاقناطهم من القبول. ألا ترى أنهم لما أعادوا للرسل القول ولم ينكروا عليهم عودهم إلى المجادلة، دل على أنهم لم يسكتوهم أولا، ولا كان غرضهم ذلك، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «وأراب الرجل» لعله: أو أراب. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 543
1. (1). By a Bedouin of Banū Asad. Labbā means "he answered"; Ibn Ḥabīb wrote it with an alif though it is yāʾ-final, to distinguish it from the dual that follows it. Labbay is among the nouns that are bound to annexation to a pronoun, and its annexation to a noun is anomalous, as here; it is from labba bi-l-makān, labban, "he stayed in it," and what is meant is the constancy of his answering, answer upon answer, not just two. It is accusative as a verbal noun by an omitted verb; this is the school of Sībawayh. Yūnus claimed that it is a singular, an alif-final noun whose alif, with the pronoun, turns into yāʾ like ladā and ʿalā; Sībawayh answered him that if it were so, its alif would not turn to yāʾ with a noun, as with ladā and ʿalā; but when they annexed it to a noun they turned it into yāʾ, as in the verse. He says: I called Miswar for what befell me, and he answered me, labbā yadayhi, that is, God answered his prayer, answer after answer, and "the two hands" is inserted because they are raised at the supplication, so it is as though they were the ones answered; or because his help came about through them, so it contains an indication that he rescued him. It is also said that he called him to pay the blood-money on his behalf, and he answered him, mentioning his two hands because he gave with them. It is said: that was the custom of the Arabs, and it was forbidden. It is reported from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: "When one of you calls his brother and he says 'labbayka,' let him not say 'labbā yadayka,' but let him say: 'May God answer you with what you love.'"
2. . His discourse returns. He said: "And their saying 'you are not but men like us': its meaning is: why are you singled out for prophethood rather than us? And had God sent messengers to humankind He would have made them of a kind better than they, namely the angels." Aḥmad said: In his eagerness to win support for his belief in the superiority of angels over the messengers from humankind, he seeks help until he loads the unbelievers with the claim that they believed as the Qadariyya believe in the superiority of the angel over the messenger, because he claims that this is a matter implanted in natures and known by necessity. And God is the Granter of success. [.....]
3. . His statement "He would have made them of a kind better than they, namely the angels": this is according to the school of the Muʿtazila; as for the Ahl al-Sunna, some of humankind are better. (ʿ)
1. (1) . لأعرابى من بنى أسد. ولبى: بمعنى أجاب، ورسمه ابن حبيب بالألف وإن كان يائيا للفرق بينه وبين المثنى بعده. ولبى من الأسماء اللازمة للاضافة إلى الضمير، وشذ إضافته للظاهر كما هنا، من لب بالمكان لبا أقام به والمراد ملازمة إجابته إجابة بعد إجابة لا اثنين فقط، وهو منصوب على المصدرية بفعل محذوف. هذا مذهب سيبويه. وزعم يونس أنه مفرد مقصور، قلبت ألفه مع الضمير ياء كلدى وعلى، فرد عليه سيبويه بأنه لو كان كذلك لم تنقلب ألفه مع الظاهر ياء كلدى وعلى، لكنهم لما أضافوه للظاهر قلبوها ياء كما في البيت. يقول: دعوت مسورا لما أصابنى، فأجابنى فلبى يديه، أى أجاب الله دعاءه بعد إجابة، وأقحم اليدين لأنهما يرفعان عند الدعاء، فكأنهما المجابتان، أو لأن نصره حصل بهما، ففيه إشارة إلى أنه أنقذه. وقيل: إنه دعاه ليغرم عنه الدية، فأجابه، فذكر يديه لأنه بذل بهما. قيل: وكانت عادة العرب ذلك فنهى عنه. وروى عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وآله وسلم أنه قال. إذا دعا أحدكم أخاه فقال: لبيك، فلا يقولن لبى يديك، وليقل أجابك الله بما تحب.
2. . عاد كلامه. قال: «وقولهم إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا: معناه فلم تخصون بالنبوة دوننا؟ ولو أرسل الله إلى البشر رسلا لجعلهم من جنس أفضل منهم وهم الملائكة» ؟ قال أحمد: ومن تهالكه على الانتصار لاعتقاده تفضيل الملائكة على الرسل من البشر، يستعين حتى يحمل الكفار على أنهم كانوا يعتقدون كمعتقد القدرية في تفضيل الملك على الرسول، لأنه يدعى ذلك أمراً مركوزاً في الطباع معلوما ضرورة، والله الموفق. [.....]
3. . قوله «لجعلهم من جنس أفضل منهم وهم الملائكة» هذا على مذهب المعتزلة، أما عند أهل السنة فبعض البشر أفضل. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 544
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "If you ask: how was that repeated after His saying 'and upon God let the believers rely'?..." etc. Aḥmad said: By this he escapes from the territory of "whoever kills a slain man shall have his spoils." And God knows best.
2. . His word "ḥālifīn": a circumstantial qualifier of the subject of "said." The wording of al-Nasafī is "and they swore." (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت كيف كرر ذلك بعد قوله وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وبهذا يخرج عن وادى «من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه» والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «حالفين» حال من فاعل قال. وعبارة النسفي «وحلفوا» . (ع)
10
Q 14:11–12 · Vol. 2, p. 544

Verses 11 to 12

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Their messengers said to them, 'We are only men like you, but God confers favor upon whom He wills of His servants. And it was not for us to bring you an authority except by permission of God. And upon God let the believers rely.'" (11) "And why should we not rely upon God while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient against whatever harm you cause us. And upon God let those who would rely [indeed] rely." (12)
قالَتْ لَهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ وَما كانَ لَنا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (11) وَما لَنا أَلاَّ نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدانا سُبُلَنا وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلى ما آذَيْتُمُونا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ (12)
Vol. 2, p. 544
"We are only men like you" is a concession of their statement, that they are men like them, meaning that they are like them in humanity alone; but beyond that they were not like them, yet they did not mention their superiority, out of humility on their part, and confined themselves to their saying "but God confers favor upon whom He wills of His servants" with prophethood, because He knows that He singles them out for that honor only when they are fit to be singled out for it, because of characteristics in them by which they have preferred themselves over the people of their kind. "Except by permission of God": they meant that bringing the sign which you have proposed is not up to us nor within our power, and it is only a matter attached to God's will. "And upon God let the believers rely" is a command from them to all the believers to rely, and they intended by it themselves first and foremost and commanded themselves with it, as though they said: "And it is our duty to rely on God in patience with your obstinacy and enmity, and what comes upon us from you." Do you not see His saying "and why should we not rely upon God"? Its meaning is: what excuse do we have for not relying upon Him, "while He has guided us," and has done for us what makes it necessary for us to rely upon Him, namely success in guiding each one of us to the way that he must follow in religion?
إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ تسليم لقولهم، وأنهم بشر مثلهم، يعنون أنهم مثلهم في البشرية وحدها، فأما ما وراء ذلك فما كانوا مثلهم، ولكنهم لم يذكروا فضلهم تواضعاً منهم، واقتصروا على قولهم وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ بالنبوّة، لأنه قد علم أنه لا يختصهم بتلك الكرامة إلا وهم أهل لاختصاصهم بها، لخصائص فيهم قد استأثروا بها على أبناء جنسهم إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ أرادوا أن الإتيان بالآية التي اقترحتموها ليس إلينا ولا في استطاعتنا، وما هو إلا أمر يتعلق بمشيئة الله وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ أمر منهم للمؤمنين كافة بالتوكل، وقصدوا به أنفسهم قصدا أوليا وأمروها به، كأنهم قالوا: ومن حقنا أن نتوكل على الله في الصبر على معاندتكم ومعاداتكم وما يجرى علينا منكم. ألا ترى إلى قوله وَما لَنا أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ ومعناه: وأىّ عذر لنا في أن لا نتوكل عليه وَقَدْ هَدانا وقد فعل بنا ما يوجب توكلنا عليه، وهو التوفيق لهداية كل واحد منا سبيله الذي يجب عليه سلوكه في الدين،
Question
If you ask: how was the command to rely repeated (1)?
فإن قلت: كيف كرّر الأمر بالتوكل «1» ؟
Answer
I say: the first is for initiating reliance, and His saying "let those who would rely indeed rely" means: let those who rely persevere in the reliance they have initiated, and their aiming at themselves as has preceded.
قلت: الأول لاستحداث التوكل، وقوله فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ معناه فليثبت المتوكلون على ما استحدثوا من توكلهم وقصدهم إلى أنفسهم على ما تقدّم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 544
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "If you ask: how was that repeated after His saying 'and upon God let the believers rely'?..." etc. Aḥmad said: By this he escapes from the territory of "whoever kills a slain man shall have his spoils." And God knows best.
2. . His word "ḥālifīn": a circumstantial qualifier of the subject of "said." The wording of al-Nasafī is "and they swore." (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت كيف كرر ذلك بعد قوله وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وبهذا يخرج عن وادى «من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه» والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «حالفين» حال من فاعل قال. وعبارة النسفي «وحلفوا» . (ع)
11
Q 14:12–14 · Vol. 2, pp. 544–545

Verses 12 to 14

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And why should we not rely upon God while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient against whatever harm you cause us. And upon God let those who would rely [indeed] rely." (12) "And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, 'We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion.' So their Lord inspired to them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers,'" (13) "'and We will surely cause you to dwell in the land after them. That is for he who fears My position and fears My threat.'" (14)
وَما لَنا أَلاَّ نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدانا سُبُلَنا وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلى ما آذَيْتُمُونا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ (12) وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِرُسُلِهِمْ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِنا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنا فَأَوْحى إِلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ لَنُهْلِكَنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ (13) وَلَنُسْكِنَنَّكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ خافَ مَقامِي وَخافَ وَعِيدِ (14)
Vol. 2, p. 544
"We will surely drive you out, or you must return": one of the two matters will surely occur, either your being driven out or your return, they swearing (2) to that.
لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُمْ، أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ ليكونن أحد الأمرين لا محالة، إما إخراجكم وإما عودكم حالفين «2» على ذلك.
Question
If you ask: it is as though they were [first] upon their religion that they should [now] return to it?
فإن قلت: كأنهم كانوا على ملتهم حتى يعودوا فيها.
Answer
I say: God forbid; but "return" (ʿawd) is in the sense of becoming, and this is very frequent in the speech of the Arabs, a widespread frequency, so that you hardly hear them using
قلت: معاذ الله، ولكن العود بمعنى الصيرورة، وهو كثير في كلام العرب كثرة فاشية لا تكاد تسمعهم يستعملون
Vol. 2, p. 545
ṣāra, but rather ʿāda: "I do not see him any longer speaking to me" (mā ʿudtu arāhu ʿāda lā yukallimunī), "So-and-so no longer has any wealth" (mā ʿāda li-fulān māl). Or they addressed it to every messenger and those who believed in him, and so gave priority to the plural over the singular in the address. "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers" is a quotation that requires an implied "saying," or the treating of inspiration as a kind of saying, because it is a species of it. Abū Ḥaywa read "la-yuhlikanna" and "la-yuskinannakum" with yāʾ, taking account of "He inspired," whose wording is third-person; similar is your saying "Zayd swore that he would go out" (la-yakhrujanna) and "that I would go out" (la-akhrujanna). What is meant by "the land" is the land of the wrongdoers and their homes, like "and We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts of it," and "and He caused you to inherit their land and their homes." From the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever harms his neighbor, God makes him inherit his house" (1). And I witnessed this a short time ago: I had a maternal uncle whom the great man of the village I come from used to wrong, and he also harmed me through him; that great man died and God gave me ownership of his estate, and one day I looked at the sons of my uncle going back and forth in it, entering its houses and leaving, commanding and forbidding, and I remembered the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ and told them of it, and we prostrated in thanks to God. "That" is a reference to what God decreed of the destruction of the wrongdoers and the settling of the believers in their homes, that is: that matter is true "for he who fears My position," My standing, and it is the standing of reckoning, because it is God's standing in which His servants stand (2) on the Day of Resurrection; or on the view that "maqām" is an insertion. It is also said: he who fears My standing over him and My preserving of his deeds. The meaning is that that is true for the God-fearing, as in His saying "and the [best] outcome is for the God-fearing."
صار، ولكن عاد، ما عدت أراه عاد لا يكلمني، ما عاد لفلان مال. أو خاطبوا به كل رسول ومن آمن به، فغلبوا في الخطاب الجماعة على الواحد لَنُهْلِكَنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ حكاية تقتضي إضمار القول، أو إجراء الإيحاء مجرى القول، لأنه ضرب منه. وقرأ أبو حيوة: «ليهلكنّ» ، و «ليسكننكم» بالياء اعتباراً لأوحى، وأن لفظه لفظ الغيبة، ونحوه قولك: أقسم زيد ليخرجن ولأخرجن. والمراد بالأرض. أرض الظالمين وديارهم، ونحوه وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغارِبَهَا، وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيارَهُمْ. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «من آذى جاره ورثه الله داره «1» » ولقد عاينت هذا في مدة قريبة: كان لي خال يظلمه عظيم القرية التي أنا منها ويؤذيني فيه، فمات ذلك العظيم وملكني الله ضيعته، فنظرت يوما إلى أبناء خالي يتردّدون فيها ويدخلون في دورها ويخرجون ويأمرون وينهون فذكرت قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وحدّثتهم به، وسجدنا شكراً لله ذلِكَ إشارة إلى ما قضى به الله من إهلاك الظالمين إسكان المؤمنين ديارهم، أى ذلك الأمر حق لِمَنْ خافَ مَقامِي موقفي وهو موقف الحساب، لأنه موقف الله الذي يقف «2» فيه عباده يوم القيامة، أو على إقحام المقام. وقيل: خاف قيامي عليه وحفظي لأعماله. والمعنى أنّ ذلك حق للمتقين، كقوله وَالْعاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 544
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "If you ask: how was that repeated after His saying 'and upon God let the believers rely'?..." etc. Aḥmad said: By this he escapes from the territory of "whoever kills a slain man shall have his spoils." And God knows best.
2. . His word "ḥālifīn": a circumstantial qualifier of the subject of "said." The wording of al-Nasafī is "and they swore." (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت كيف كرر ذلك بعد قوله وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وبهذا يخرج عن وادى «من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه» والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «حالفين» حال من فاعل قال. وعبارة النسفي «وحلفوا» . (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 545
1. (1). I did not find it.
2. . His statement "yaqifu fīhi ʿibāduhu": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: it is both transitive and intransitive. (ʿ)
1. (1) . لم أجده.
2. . قوله «يقف فيه عباده» في الصحاح: يتعدى ولا يتعدى. (ع)
12
Q 14:15–17 · Vol. 2, pp. 545–547

Verses 15 to 17

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And they sought victory [or judgment], and disappointed to loss was every obstinate tyrant." (15) "Behind him is Hell, and he will be given to drink of purulent water." (16) "He will gulp it, but he will hardly be able to swallow it, and death will come to him from every place, yet he is not to die; and before him is a massive punishment." (17)
وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ (15) مِنْ وَرائِهِ جَهَنَّمُ وَيُسْقى مِنْ ماءٍ صَدِيدٍ (16) يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ وَما هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ وَمِنْ وَرائِهِ عَذابٌ غَلِيظٌ (17)
Vol. 2, p. 545
"And they sought victory": they asked God for help against their enemies, as in "If you seek victory, then the victory has come to you"; or they sought God's judgment and asked Him to decide between them, from al-fatāḥa, which is judgment, as in His saying, Exalted is He, "Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth." It is coordinated with "so He inspired to them." It has also been read "wa-stafṭiḥū" in the imperative form, coordinated with "We will surely destroy," that is: their Lord inspired to them and said to them "We will surely destroy," and said to them "seek victory." "And disappointed to loss was every obstinate tyrant": its meaning is: so they were given victory and prevailed and succeeded, "and disappointed to loss was every obstinate tyrant," and they were their people. It is also said: the unbelievers sought victory against the messengers, thinking that they were upon the truth and the messengers upon falsehood, "and disappointed to loss was every obstinate tyrant" among them, and he did not succeed by his seeking victory. "Behind him" means before him. [The poet] said:
وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا واستنصروا الله على أعدائهم إِنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ أو استحكموا الله وسألوه القضاء بينهم من الفتاحة وهي الحكومة، كقوله تعالى رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالْحَقِّ وهو معطوف على فَأَوْحى إِلَيْهِمْ وقرئ: «واستفتحوا» ، بلفظ الأمر. وعطفه على لَنُهْلِكَنَّ أى: أوحى إليهم ربهم وقال لهم لنهلكنّ وقال لهم استفتحوا وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ معناه فنصروا وظفروا وأفلحوا، وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ، وهم قومهم. وقيل: واستفتح الكفار على الرسل، ظنا منهم بأنهم على الحق والرسل على الباطل، وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ منهم ولم يفلح باستفتاحه مِنْ وَرائِهِ من بين يديه. قال:
Vol. 2, p. 546
"Perhaps the distress in which you have spent the evening will have behind it a near relief (1)." This is a description of his state while he is in this world, because he is set aside for Hell, so it is as though it were before him and he were at its brink; or a description of his state in the Hereafter when he is raised and made to stand. If you ask: to what is "and he will be given to drink" coordinated? I say: to an omitted element, whose implied form is: "behind him is Hell: he will be cast into it and will be cast; and he will be given to drink of purulent water," as though it were the severest of its punishment and so singled out for mention, together with His saying "and death will come to him from every place, yet he is not to die." If you ask: what is the point of His saying "of purulent water"? I say: "purulent" (ṣadīd) is an explanatory apposition to "water"; He said "he will be given to drink of water," leaving it indeterminate, then specified it by His saying "purulent," which is what flows from the skins of the people of the Fire. "He will gulp it" means he will take pains to swallow it; "but will hardly be able to swallow it": kāda entered for emphasis. He means: he will not come close to swallowing it, so how could swallowing take place? as in "he can hardly see it," that is, he does not come near to seeing it, so how could he see it? "And death will come to him from every place": as though the causes of death and all its kinds had massed against him (2) and surrounded him from every direction, to make terrible what befalls him of pains. It is also said: "from every place" of his body, even from the big toe of his foot. It is also said: from the root of every hair. "And behind him," and before him, "is a massive punishment," that is: at every time that he faces, he meets a punishment more severe than the one before it and more massive. From al-Fuḍayl: it is the cutting of breaths and their being held in the bodies. It is also possible that the people of Mecca sought rain ("seeking victory," istiftāḥ, meaning seeking rain, al-fatḥ being rain) in the years of drought that were sent upon them through the prayer of the Messenger of God ﷺ and were not given rain; so the Glorified mentioned that, and that He disappointed the hope of every obstinate tyrant, and that he will be given to drink in Hell, in place of his drinking [rain], another water, namely the pus of the people of the Fire. And "they sought victory," according to this interpretation:
عَسَى الْكَرْبُ الَّذِى أَمْسَيْتَ فِيهِ … يَكُونُ وَرَاءَهُ فَرَجٌ قَرِيبُ «1» وهذا وصف حاله وهو في الدنيا، لأنه مرصد لجهنم، فكأنها بين يديه وهو على شفيرها أو وصف حاله في الآخرة حين يبعث ويوقف. فان قلت: علام عطف وَيُسْقى؟ قلت: على محذوف تقديره: من ورائه جهنم يلقى فيها ما يلقى ويسقى من ماء صديد، كأنه أشد عذابها فخصص بالذكر مع قوله وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ وَما هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ. فإن قلت: ما وجه قوله تعالى مِنْ ماءٍ صَدِيدٍ؟ قلت: صديد عطف بيان لماء، قال وَيُسْقى مِنْ ماءٍ فأبهمه إبهاما ثم بينه بقوله صَدِيدٍ وهو ما يسيل من جلود أهل النار يَتَجَرَّعُهُ يتكلف جرعه وَلا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ دخل كاد للمبالغة. يعنى: ولا يقارب أن يسيغه، فكيف تكون الإساغة، كقوله لَمْ يَكَدْ يَراها أى لم يقرب من رؤيتها فكيف يراها وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ كأنّ أسباب الموت وأصنافه كلها قد تألبت عليه «2» وأحاطت به من جميع الجهات، تفظيعا لما يصيبه من الآلام. وقيل مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ من جسده حتى من إبهام رجله. وقيل: من أصل كل شعرة وَمِنْ وَرائِهِ ومن بين يديه عَذابٌ غَلِيظٌ أى في كل وقت يستقبله يتلقى عذابا أشدّ مما قبله وأغلظ. وعن الفضيل: هو قطع الأنفاس وحبسها في الأجساد. ويحتمل أن يكون أهل مكة قد استفتحوا أى استمطروا- والفتح المطر- في سنى القحط التي أرسالات عليهم بدعوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يسقوا، فذكر سبحانه ذلك، وأنه خيب رجاء كل جبار عنيد وأنه يسقى في جهنم بدل سقياه ماء آخر، وهو صديد أهل النار. وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا- على هذا التفسير-:
Vol. 2, p. 547
is a new statement, cut off from the account of the messengers and their communities.
كلام مستأنف منقطع عن حديث الرسل وأممهم.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 545
1. (1). I did not find it.
2. . His statement "yaqifu fīhi ʿibāduhu": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: it is both transitive and intransitive. (ʿ)
1. (1) . لم أجده.
2. . قوله «يقف فيه عباده» في الصحاح: يتعدى ولا يتعدى. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 546
1. (1). "Sleeplessness afflicts me, the gloom of Abū Numayr, so my heart, from his gloom, is gloomy. / So I said to him, 'May God guide you, take it easy, and the best speech is that of the possessor of intellect who hits the mark. / Perhaps the distress in which you have spent the evening will have behind it a near relief.'" By Hudba b. Khashram al-ʿUdhrī; it is also related "Kharsham." He was imprisoned awaiting execution. Al-taʾrīq is making sleepless; al-iktiʾāb is dejection and change of color from grief, and al-kaʾāba likewise. Abū Numayr was a friend of his, who visited him in the prison and grieved for him. Mahlan is a verbal noun standing in place of the wording of its verb. "And the best speech..." is a parenthetical sentence in the midst of what was said. Al-lubb is the intellect. "Perhaps the distress..." completes what was said. It is related as "amsayta" with ḍamma and with fatḥa. Al-Jawharī said: "warāʾ" comes in the sense of "behind," and it sometimes comes in the sense of "in front of," so it is one of the words with opposite senses, since what is "behind" (warāʾ) a person is what his body conceals from himself or from others, and concealing from oneself is possible only in the back, so it is frequent there; or it is the place of concealment absolutely, and it is more often in the back. The subject of "yakūnu" is a pronoun referring to the distress, and "warāʾahu" is connected to an omitted element that is the predicate of "yakūnu," and "faraj" is the subject of the adverbial; it is also possible that "faraj" is a subject and "warāʾahu," connected to an omitted element, is its predicate, the sentence being the predicate of "yakūnu," and the omitted element must be a complete "being," not an incomplete one, so as not to need yet another omitted element, which would produce a regress of supposition; and "faraj" is not made nominative by "yakūnu," because the predicate of verbs of proximity does not raise a noun foreign to their subjects. The sentence of "yakūnu" is the predicate of "ʿasā," and stripping its predicate of "an" is rare; that is: perhaps relief will come after distress.
2. . His statement "qad taʾallabat ʿalayhi": that is, gathered together. Al-Ṣiḥāḥ gives this. (ʿ)
1. (1) . يؤرقنى اكتئاب أبى نمير
…. فقلبي من كآبته كئيب فقلت له هداك الله مهلا
…. وخير القول ذو اللب المصيب عسى الكرب الذي أمسيت فيه
…. يكون وراءه فرج قريب لهدبة بن خشرم العذرى. ويروى: خرشم. وكان مسجونا للقتل. والتأريق: التسهير، والاكتئاب: الانكسار وتغير اللون من الحزن، والكآبة كذلك. وأبو نمير كان صديقا له، فزاره لك السجن وحزن عليه. ومهلا: مصدر بدل من اللفظ بفعله. وخبر القول: جملة اعتراضية في أثناء مقول القول. واللب: العقل. وعسى الكرب: تتمة مقول القول. ويروى: أمسيت، بالضم والفتح. وقال الجوهري «وراء» يأتى بمعنى خلف، وقد يأتى بمعنى قدام، فهو من الأضداد اه، لأنه ما وراء الشخص بجرمه عن نفسه أو عن غيره، ومواراته عن نفسه لا يمكن إلا في الخلف، فكثر فيه. أو هو مكان المواراة مطلقا، وهو في الخلف أكثر. واسم «يكون» ضمير الكرب، ووراءه متعلق بمحذوف خبر ليكون، و «فرج» فاعل بالظرف. ويجوز أن «فرج» مبتدأ و «وراءه» متعلق بمحذوف خبر له، والجملة خبر ليكون، ويجب كون المحذوف كونا تاما لا ناقصا، لئلا يحتاج إلى تقدير محذوف أيضا، فيتسلسل التقدير، ولم يجعل «فرج» مرفوع بيكون، لأن خبر أفعال المقاربة لا يرفع الأجنبى عن أسمائها. وجملة «يكون» خبر ليس «وتجريد خبرها من «أن» قليل أى عسى أن يحصل الفرج بعد الكرب.
2. . قوله «قد تألبت عليه» أى تجمعت. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 547

Q 14:18 · Vol. 2, p. 547

Verse 18

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is [that] their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they are unable [to keep] anything of what they earned. That is the extreme error." (18)
مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمالُهُمْ كَرَمادٍ اشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي يَوْمٍ عاصِفٍ لا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا عَلى شَيْءٍ ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ (18)
Vol. 2, p. 547
It is a subject whose predicate is omitted, according to Sībawayh; its implied form is: "and among what is recounted to you is the example of those who disbelieve in their Lord." "Example" is borrowed for a description that has something strange in it. And His saying "their deeds are like ashes" is a new sentence on the assumption of a questioner asking, "What is their example?" and it was said: "their deeds are like ashes." It is also possible that the meaning is: "the example of the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord"; or that this sentence is a predicate for the subject, that is: "the description of those who disbelieve: their deeds are like ashes," as you say "the description of Zayd: his honor is protected and his wealth is spent freely"; or "their deeds" is a substitute for "the example of those who disbelieve," on the assumption "the example of their deeds," with "like ashes" as the predicate. It has been read al-riyāḥ. "On a stormy day": storminess was made [an attribute] of the day, though it belongs to what is in it, namely the wind or winds, as you say "a rainy day" and "a drunken night"; the "drunkenness" (sukūr) is only of its wind (1). It has also been read "fī yawmi ʿāṣifin," by annexation. The deeds of the unbelievers are the noble acts they had, of maintaining kinship ties, freeing slaves, ransoming captives, slaughtering camels for guests, helping the distressed, granting protection, and other such works of theirs; He likened them, in their being nullified and going as scattered dust, because they were built on no foundation of knowledge of God and belief in Him and of their being for His sake, to ashes carried off by a violent wind. "They are unable," on the Day of Resurrection, "of what they earned" of their deeds, "[to keep] anything," that is, they see no trace of reward for it, just as nothing can be held of ashes carried off in the wind. "That is the extreme error" is a reference to the remoteness of their error from the path of truth or from reward. "In truth" means with wisdom and a sound purpose (2) and a great matter; and He did not create them in vain nor out of desire.
هو مبتدأ محذوف الخبر عند سيبويه، تقديره: وفيما يقص عليك مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ والمثل مستعار للصفة التي فيها غرابة وقوله أَعْمالُهُمْ كَرَمادٍ جملة مستأنفة على تقدير سؤال سائل يقول: كيف مثلهم؟ فقيل: أعمالهم كرماد. ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: مثل أعمال الذين كفروا بربهم. أو هذه الجملة خبرا للمبتدإ، أى صفة الذين كفروا أعمالهم كرماد، كقولك صفة زيد عرضه مصون وماله مبذول، أو يكون أعمالهم بدلا من مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا على تقدير: مثل أعمالهم، وكرماد: الخبر. وقرئ: الرياح فِي يَوْمٍ عاصِفٍ جعل العصف لليوم، وهو لما فيه، وهو الريح أو الرياح، كقولك: يوم ماطر وليلة ساكرة. وإنما السكور لريحها «1» وقرئ: في يوم عاصف، بالإضافة. وأعمال الكفرة المكارم التي كانت لهم، من صلة الأرحام وعتق الرقاب، وفداء الأسارى، وعقر الإبل للأضياف، وإغاثة الملهوفين، والإجازة، وغير ذلك من صنائعهم، شبهها في حبوطها وذهابها هباء منثورا لبنائها على غير أساس من معرفة الله والإيمان به، وكونها لوجهه: برماد طيرته الريح العاصف لا يَقْدِرُونَ يوم القيامة مِمَّا كَسَبُوا من أعمالهم عَلى شَيْءٍ أى لا يرون له أثرا من ثواب، كما لا يقدر من الرماد المطير في الريح على شيء ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ إشارة إلى بعد ضلالهم عن طريق الحق أو عن الثواب بِالْحَقِّ بالحكمة والغرض الصحيح «2» والأمر العظيم، ولم يخلقها عبثا ولا شهوة

Q 14:19–20 · Vol. 2, pp. 547–548

Verses 19 to 20

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Do you not see that God created the heavens and earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation." (19) "And that is not difficult for God." (20)
أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ (19) وَما ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ بِعَزِيزٍ (20)
Vol. 2, p. 547
It has also been read khāliqu al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi. "If He wills, He can do away with you": that is, He is able to annihilate people and create in their place another creation, of their shape or contrary to their shape, as an announcement from Him of His power to annihilate the existent and bring into existence the non-existent; He is able to do a thing and its contrary kind. "And that is not difficult for God," not hard,
وقرئ: خالق السموات والأرض إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ أى هو قادر على أن يعدم الناس ويخلق مكانهم خلقا آخر على شكلهم أو على خلاف شكلهم، إعلاما منه باقتداره على إعدام الموجود وإيجاد المعدوم، يقدر على الشيء وجنس ضده وَما ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ بِعَزِيزٍ بمتعذر،
Vol. 2, p. 548
rather it is light and easy for Him (1), because He is powerful in His essence, with no specificity for one object of power over another; so when the motive for something becomes pure for Him and the deterrent is absent, it comes to be without delay, like the moving of your finger when something calls you to it and no deterrent intervenes. These verses are an explanation of how far they went in error and the greatness of their mistake in disbelieving in God, given the clarity of His signs that bear witness to Him and indicate His dazzling power and perfect wisdom, and that He is the one worthy of being worshipped, whose punishment is to be feared and whose reward is to be hoped for in the abode of recompense.
بل هو هين عليه يسير «1» ، لأنه قادر الذات لا اختصاص له بمقدور دون مقدور، فإذا خلص له الداعي إلى شيء وانتفى الصارف، تكوّن من غير توقف: كتحريك أصبعك إذا دعاك إليه داع ولم يعترض دونه صارف. وهذه الآيات بيان لإبعادهم في الضلال وعظيم خطئهم في الكفر بالله، لوضوح آياته الشاهدة له الدالة على قدرته الباهرة وحكمته البالغة وأنه هو الحقيق بأن يعبد، ويخاف عقابه ويرجى ثوابه في دار الجزاء.
