1. (1). His discourse returns. He said: "Its meaning is: 'and that is not difficult for God,' that is, easy for Him, because He is powerful by His essence," etc. Aḥmad said: This is out-and-out Muʿtazilism of theirs, which he cloaks in presenting. How hideous is his saying about God, majestic is His majesty, "the motive became pure for Him and the deterrent passed," and how far it is from the hearing of the verifiers who know the proper conduct toward God, Exalted is He, and what is obligatory in regard to His majesty; and what is sufficient on it has already preceded.
2. . His statement "khādim and khadam, ghāʾib and ghayab": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: the yāʾ was retained in it with vowelization only because it was likened to ṣayd, though it is a plural; and ṣayd is a verbal noun from the expression "baʿīr aṣyad," because it is permissible to intend a verbal noun by it. (ʿ)
1. (1) . عاد كلامه. قال: معناه وما ذلك على الله بعزيز، أى: هين عليه، لأنه قادر بالذات الخ
…. قال أحمد: وهذا اعتزال صراح لهم يتقنع في إبرازه، وما أبشع قوله عن الله جل جلاله، خلص له الداعي وأمضى الصارف، وما أنباه عن سمع المحققين العارفين بآداب الله تعالى وبما يجب في حق جلاله، وقد تقدم ما فيه كفاية.
2. . قوله «خادم وخدم وغائب وغيب» في الصحاح: وإنما ثبتت فيه الياء في التحريك، لأنه شبه بصيد وإن كان جمعا، وصيد مصدر قولك «بعير أصيد» لأنه يجوز أن ينوى به المصدر. (ع)
15
Q 14:21 · Vol. 2, pp. 548–550

Verse 21

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And they will all come out before God, and the weak will say to those who had been arrogant, 'Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of God?' They will say, 'If God had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show intolerance or are patient: there is for us no place of escape.'" (21)
وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً فَقالَ الضُّعَفاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعاً فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا مِنْ عَذابِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قالُوا لَوْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ لَهَدَيْناكُمْ سَواءٌ عَلَيْنا أَجَزِعْنا أَمْ صَبَرْنا ما لَنا مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (21)
Vol. 2, p. 548
"And they will come out before God": they will come out on the Day of Resurrection. It was put in the past form only because what He, Mighty and Exalted, reports, by its truthfulness, is as though it had already occurred and come to exist, like "and the companions of Paradise called out" and "and the companions of the Fire called out" and their like. The meaning of their "coming out before God" (and God, Exalted is He, is such that nothing is hidden from Him, so that anything should come out to Him) is that they used to conceal themselves from eyes when committing indecencies and thought that that was hidden from God; so when it is the Day of Resurrection they will be uncovered before God in their own selves, and will know that nothing is hidden from God. Or they came out of their graves and so came out to God's reckoning and judgment. If you ask: why was "al-ḍuʿafāʾ" written with a wāw before the hamza? I say: it was written according to the pronunciation of one who gives the alif before the hamza a heavy articulation and inclines it toward the wāw. Its parallel is "ʿulamāʾu banī Isrāʾīl." Al-ḍuʿafāʾ are the followers and the common people. "Those who had been arrogant" are their chiefs and elders, who had made them followers and led them astray and turned them aside from listening to the prophets and their followers. "Followers" (tabaʿan) means those who follow: plural of tābiʿ on the pattern tabaʿ, as in "khādim and khadam," "ghāʾib and ghayab" (2); or possessors of following; and al-tabaʿ means the followers; one says tabiʿahu tabaʿan. If you ask: what is the difference between "min" in "min ʿadhābi Allāh" and "min" in "min shayʾin"? I say: the first is explanatory, and the second partitive, as though it were said: "Are you able to avail us some of the thing which is the punishment of God?" It is also possible that both are partitive, in the sense: "Are you able to avail us some thing that is some of the punishment of God," that is, some of some of the punishment of God
وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ ويبرزون يوم القيامة. وإنما جيء به بلفظ الماضي، لأنّ ما أخبر به عزّ وعلا لصدقه كأنه قد كان ووجد، ونحوه وَنادى أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ، وَنادى أَصْحابُ النَّارِ ونظائر له. ومعنى بروزهم لله- والله تعالى لا يتوارى عنه شيء حتى يبرز له- أنهم كانوا يستترون من العيون عند ارتكاب الفواحش، ويظنون أن ذلك خاف على الله، فإذا كان يوم القيامة انكشفوا لله عند أنفسهم وعلموا أنّ الله لا يخفى عليه خافية. أو خرجوا من قبورهم فبرزوا لحساب الله وحكمه. فإن قلت: لم كتب «الضعفؤا» بواو قبل الهمزة؟ قلت: كتب على لفظ من يفخم الألف قبل الهمزة فيميلها إلى الواو. ونظيره «علمؤا بنى إسرائيل» والضعفاء: الأتباع والعوام. والذين استكبروا: ساداتهم وكبراؤهم، الذين استتبعوهم واستغووهم وصدورهم عن الاستماع إلى الأنبياء وأتباعهم تَبَعاً تابعين: جمع تابع على تبع، كقولهم: خادم وخدم وغائب وغيب «2» أو ذوى تبع. والتبع: الأتباع، يقال: تبعه تبعا. فان قلت: أى فرق بين من في مِنْ عَذابِ اللَّهِ وبينه في مِنْ شَيْءٍ؟ قلت: الأولى للتبيين، والثانية للتبعيض، كأنه قيل: هل أنتم مغنون عنا بعض الشيء الذي هو عذاب الله. ويجوز أن تكونا للتبعيض معا، بمعنى: هل أنتم مغنون عنا بعض شيء هو بعض عذاب الله، أى: بعض بعض عذاب الله
Vol. 2, p. 549
If you ask: what then is the meaning of His saying "If God had guided us, we would have guided you"? I say: what the weak said to them was a rebuke of them (1) and a reproach for their making them followers and leading them astray. And their saying "so can you avail us anything" is by way of silencing, because they knew that they were unable to avail them anything; so they answered them, excusing what had come from them toward them: that had God guided them to faith they would have guided them and not led them astray, either imputing the guilt (2) for their error and their leading astray to God, as God relates of them, "And they said: 'If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers'," "'If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything other than Him'"; they say that in the Hereafter just as they used to say it in the world. The proof of it is His saying, reporting of the hypocrites, "On the Day when God will resurrect them all, they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they will think that they are upon something." Or the meaning may be: had we been of the people of kindness, and our Lord shown us kindness and we been guided, we would have guided you to faith. It is also said: its meaning is: had God guided us to the path of salvation from the punishment, we would have guided you, that is, we would have availed you and led you along the path of salvation as we led you along the path of destruction. "It is all the same for us whether we show intolerance or are patient": impatience and patience are equal for us. The hamza and "am" are for equalization. Similar is: "So be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you." It is reported that they will say: "Come, let us be impatient," so they will be impatient for five hundred years without benefit; then they will say: "Come, let us be patient," and will be patient likewise; then they will say: "It is all the same for us." If you ask: how is His saying "it is all the same for us" connected with what precedes? I say: its connection is that their reproach of them was an impatience at what they were in, so they said: "It is all the same for us whether we are impatient or patient," meaning themselves and the others, because of their being together in the punishment of the error in which they had been together; they say: "What is this impatience and rebuke? There is no benefit in impatience just as there is no benefit in patience, and the matter is graver than that." Or when they said, "had God guided us to the path of salvation we would have availed you and saved you," they followed it with despair of salvation, saying "there is for us no place of escape," that is, no refuge or place to flee, whether we are impatient or patient. It is also possible that it is the speech of the weak and the arrogant together, as though it were said: "They all said: it is all the same for us," as in "That is so that he [Joseph] may know that I did not betray him..."
فإن قلت: فما معنى قوله لَوْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ لَهَدَيْناكُمْ؟ قلت الذي قال لهم الضعفاء كان توبيخا لهم «1» وعتابا على استتباعهم واستغوائهم. وقولهم فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا من باب التبكيت، لأنهم قد علموا أنهم لا يقدرون على الإغناء عنهم، فأجابوهم معتذرين عما كان منهم إليهم: بأن الله لو هداهم إلى الإيمان لهدوهم ولم يضلوهم، إما موركين الذنب «2» في ضلالهم وإضلالهم على الله، كما حكى الله عنهم وقالوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أَشْرَكْنا وَلا آباؤُنا، لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما عَبَدْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يقولون ذلك في الآخرة كما كانوا يقولونه في الدنيا. ويدل عليه قوله حكاية عن المنافقين يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ. وإما أن يكون المعنى: لو كنا من أهل اللطف فلطف بنا ربنا واهتدينا لهديناكم إلى الإيمان. وقيل: معناه لو هدانا الله طريق النجاة من العذاب لهديناكم، أى: لأغنينا عنكم وسلكنا بكم طريق النجاة كما سلكنا بكم طريق الهلكة سَواءٌ عَلَيْنا أَجَزِعْنا أَمْ صَبَرْنا مستويان علينا الجزع والصبر. والهمزة وأم للتسوية. ونحوه: فَاصْبِرُوا أَوْ لا تَصْبِرُوا سَواءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وروى أنهم يقولون: تعالوا نجزع، فيجزعون خمسمائة عام فلا ينفعهم، فيقولون: تعالوا نصبر، فيصبرون كذلك ثم يقولون: سواء علينا. فإن قلت: كيف اتصل قوله سواء علينا بما قبله؟ قلت: اتصاله به من حيث أنّ عتابهم لهم كان جزعا مما هم فيه، فقالوا: سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا، يريدون أنفسهم وإياهم، لاجتماعهم في عقاب الضلالة التي كانوا مجتمعين فيها، يقولون: ما هذا الجزع والتوبيخ، ولا فائدة في الجزع كما لا فائدة في الصبر والأمر من ذلك أطمّ. أو لما قالوا لو هدانا الله طريق النجاة لأغنينا عنكم وأنجيناكم، أتبعوه الإقناط من النجاة فقالوا ما لَنا مِنْ مَحِيصٍ أى منجى ومهرب، جزعنا أم صبرنا. ويجوز أن يكون من كلام الضعفاء والمستكبرين جميعاً، كأنه قيل: قالوا جميعا سواء علينا، كقوله ذلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ
Vol. 2, p. 550
and "al-maḥīṣ" may be a verbal noun, like al-maghīb and al-mashīb, and a place, like al-mabīt and al-maṣīf. One says ḥāṣa ʿanhu and jāḍa, in one meaning.
والمحيص يكون مصدراً، كالمغيب والمشيب. ومكانا، كالمبيت والمصيف. ويقال: حاص عنه وجاض، بمعنى واحد.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 548
1. (1). His discourse returns. He said: "Its meaning is: 'and that is not difficult for God,' that is, easy for Him, because He is powerful by His essence," etc. Aḥmad said: This is out-and-out Muʿtazilism of theirs, which he cloaks in presenting. How hideous is his saying about God, majestic is His majesty, "the motive became pure for Him and the deterrent passed," and how far it is from the hearing of the verifiers who know the proper conduct toward God, Exalted is He, and what is obligatory in regard to His majesty; and what is sufficient on it has already preceded.
2. . His statement "khādim and khadam, ghāʾib and ghayab": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: the yāʾ was retained in it with vowelization only because it was likened to ṣayd, though it is a plural; and ṣayd is a verbal noun from the expression "baʿīr aṣyad," because it is permissible to intend a verbal noun by it. (ʿ)
1. (1) . عاد كلامه. قال: معناه وما ذلك على الله بعزيز، أى: هين عليه، لأنه قادر بالذات الخ
…. قال أحمد: وهذا اعتزال صراح لهم يتقنع في إبرازه، وما أبشع قوله عن الله جل جلاله، خلص له الداعي وأمضى الصارف، وما أنباه عن سمع المحققين العارفين بآداب الله تعالى وبما يجب في حق جلاله، وقد تقدم ما فيه كفاية.
2. . قوله «خادم وخدم وغائب وغيب» في الصحاح: وإنما ثبتت فيه الياء في التحريك، لأنه شبه بصيد وإن كان جمعا، وصيد مصدر قولك «بعير أصيد» لأنه يجوز أن ينوى به المصدر. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 549
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "What the weak said to them was a rebuke of them..." etc. Aḥmad said: When he sensed the verse's indication of the creed of the Sunna, which comprises that whatever God, Exalted is He, wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be, and that the guidance of the polytheists is among what He did not will, for had He willed it they would have been guided: this indication arises only from the citation of this speech of the unbelievers in the Abode of Truth, when the realities have become manifest to them and the covering has been removed; and the purpose of recounting it is to warn their like in this world, and to caution them against the regret and remorse in the Hereafter when the punishment becomes due upon them and they acknowledge the truth and say the speech mentioned; and this guides to its being a speech sound in meaning. So when al-Zamakhsharī perceived that, he set about establishing the error of their saying this in the Hereafter, as he had declared them mistaken in the world, so that his belief might be complete, that God wills what does not come to be and what He does not will comes to be; and from that is the guidance of the unbelievers, for God, Exalted is He, wills it in this world, yet it did not come to be. And how could he [be right in] that, when the context of the verse approves the speech mentioned and warns the heedless of it in this world and cautions them against plunging into what leads to this remorse where it does not avail, and draws to this regret since it does not benefit, just as the speech of Satan was cited right after that, when he acknowledges the truth in the Abode of Truth, where his faith does not benefit him, and he says: "Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, then failed you" etc.; it was cited only as a warning and admonition, by coincidence. And God is the Granter of success.
2. . His word "mūrikīn al-dhanb": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: warraka fulān dhanbahu ʿalā ghayrihi, that is, laid it upon him; that is, accused him of it. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «الذي قال لهم الضعفاء كان توبيخا لهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: لما استشعر دلالة الآية لعقيدة السنة المشتملة على أن الله تعالى مهما شاء كان، وما لم يشأ لم يكن، وأن هد آية المشركين مما لم يشأه، ولو شاءها لاهتدوا. وإنما تنشأ هذه الدلالة من إيراد هذا الكلام عن الكفار في دار الحق حين حقت لهم الحقائق وانكشف الغطاء. والمقصود من اقتصاصه: إنذار أمثالهم في الدنيا، وتحذيرهم من الحسرة والندم في الآخرة إذا حق عليهم العذاب واعترفوا بالحق وقالوا القول المذكور، وهذا يرشد إلى أنه كلام صحيح المعنى، فلما فطن الزمخشري لذلك شرع في تقرير تخطئتهم في هذا القول في الآخرة كما خطأهم في الدنيا، ليتم له اعتقاد أن الله يشاء ما لا يكون ويكون ما لا يشاء، ومن ذلك هد آية الكفار فان الله تعالى يشاؤها في الدنيا، لكنها لم تكن. وأنى له ذلك، وسياق الآية يصوب الكلام المذكور وينذر الغافلين عنه في الدنيا، ويحذرهم من التورط فيما يؤدى إلى هذا الندم، حيث لا ينفع ويجر إلى هذه الحسرة، إذ لا ينجع، كما أورد كلام الشيطان عقيب ذلك حين يعترف بالحق في دار الحق، وحيث لا ينفعه إيمانه، فيقول: إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم
…. الخ. وإنما سيق تحذيراً وإنذارا اتفاقا، والله الموفق.
2. . قوله «موركين الذنب» في الصحاح: ورك فلان ذنبه على غيره، أى: قرفه به اه، أى: اتهمه به. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 550
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "It is reported that Satan will stand at that time as a preacher..." etc. Aḥmad said: He interpreted the saying of the unbelievers in the first verse as annulment of ascription [of blame to God], because it does not suit his belief, and cited as proof that lying then is not impossible or unattainable God's saying "so they will swear to Him as they swear to you." Then, when he thought that this saying of Satan suits his belief, he strove to prove it right and sound, even though its speaker is Satan; all of that is from him a following of whim wherever it turns and whichever way it goes. And we, the Ahl al-Sunna, whom he nicknames the Mujbira, say: God, Exalted is He, cited this speech not rejecting it, nor declaring Satan mistaken in it, just as He recounted the speech of the unbelievers in the first verse. And we believe that blame is directed only to the one charged with duties, while God, Exalted is He, is far above it, and His is the conclusive argument and the true decree. That is because we acknowledge what God, Exalted is He, created for the servant of the choice which he finds in himself, by necessity, in the pull of the two sides of voluntary acts, and by that the argument stands for Him against His creation, even though we deprive created power of effect in the act; so there is no contradiction between the creed of the Sunna and directing blame to the one charged with duties. And God is the Granter of success. [.....]
2. . His statement "chooses wretchedness or happiness and brings it about for himself": this is the school of the Muʿtazila; and his word "al-mujbira" means the Ahl al-Sunna, whose school is that God is the Creator of the causes of happiness and the causes of wretchedness, but the servant has acquisition (kasb) in them, and from this blame is directed at him, contrary to the Muʿtazila in their saying that the servant is the creator of them and is the one who brings it about for himself. Its verification is in the science of tawḥīd. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «روى أن الشيطان يقوم عند ذلك خطيبا
…. الخ» قال أحمد: قد حمل قول الكفار في الآية الأولى على إبطال الانتحال، لأنه لا يلائم معتقده، واستشهد على أن الكذب حينئذ غير ممتنع ولا متعذر بقول تعالى فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ ثم لما ظن أن قول الشيطان هذا يلائم معتقده، اجتهد في الاستدلال على تصويبه وتصحيحه وإن كان قائله الشيطان، كل ذلك منه اتباع للهوى حيثما توجه وأية سلك. ونحن معاشر أهل السنة الملقبين عنده بالمجبرة نقول: إن الله تعالى إنما أورد هذا الكلام غير راد له، ولا مخطئ فيه الشيطان، كما اقتص كلام الكفار في الآية الأولى كذلك. ونحن نعتقد أن الملامة إنما تتوجه على المكلف وأما الله تعالى فمقدس عن ذلك. وحجته البالغة، وقضاؤه الحق. وذلك أنا نعترف بما خلقه الله تعالى للعبد من الاختيار الذي يجده من نفسه عند تجاذب طرفى الأفعال الارادية ضرورة، وبذلك قامت الحجة له على خلقه، وإن سلبنا عن قدرة الخلق تأثيرها في الفعل، فلا تناقض إذاً بين عقيدة السنة وبين صرف الملامة إلى المكلف، والله الموفق. [.....]
2. . قوله «يختار الشقاوة أو السعادة ويحصلها لنفسه» هذا مذهب المعتزلة، وقوله «المجبرة» يعنى أهل السنة، ومذهبهم أن الله هو الخالق لأسباب السعادة وأسباب الشقاوة، لكن العبد له فيها الكسب. ومن هذا يتوجه عليه اللوم، خلافا للمعتزلة في قولهم: إن العبد هو الخالق لها، وهو الذي يحصل لنفسه. وتحقيقه في علم التوحيد. (ع)
16
Q 14:22 · Vol. 2, pp. 550–552

Verse 22

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, 'Indeed, God had promised you the promise of truth; and I promised you, but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; rather, blame yourselves. I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with God] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.'" (22)
وَقالَ الشَّيْطانُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ وَوَعَدْتُكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ وَما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي فَلا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ ما أَنَا بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرْتُ بِما أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ (22)
Vol. 2, p. 550
"When the matter has been concluded": when the matter was cut off and finished, namely the reckoning, the issuing forth of the two groups, one of them entering Paradise and the other entering the Fire. It is reported that Satan will stand at that time as a preacher (1) among the wretched of jinn and humankind and say that. "Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth," which is the Resurrection and the recompense for deeds, and He fulfilled for you what He promised you; "and I promised you" the opposite of that, "but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you," no domination or compulsion by which to force you into unbelief and disobedience and drive you to them, "except that I invited you," except my inviting you to error by my whispering and adornment; and invitation is not of the kind of authority, but it is like your saying "Their greeting is only a beating." "So do not blame me; rather, blame yourselves," since you were deceived by me and obeyed me when I invited you, and did not obey your Lord when He invited you. This is proof that the human being is the one who chooses wretchedness or happiness and brings it about for himself (2), and from God there is only the enabling, and from Satan only the adorning. Had it been as the Mujbira claim, he would have said: "Do not blame me nor yourselves, for God decreed unbelief upon you and compelled you to it." If you ask:
لَمَّا قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ لما قطع الأمر وفرغ منه، وهو الحساب، وتصادر الفريقين ودخول أحدهما الجنة ودخول الآخر النار. وروى أنّ الشيطان يقوم عند ذلك خطيباً «1» في الأشقياء من الجنّ والإنس فيقول ذلك إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ وهو البعث والجزاء على الأعمال فوفى لكم بما وعدكم وَوَعَدْتُكُمْ خلاف ذلك فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ وَما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ من تسلط وقهر فأقسركم على الكفر والمعاصي وألجئكم إليها إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ إلا دعائي إياكم إلى الضلالة بوسوستي وتزييني، وليس الدعاء من جنس السلطان، ولكنه كقولك: ما تحيتهم إلا الضرب. فَلا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ حيث اغتررتم بى وأطعتمونى إذ دعوتكم، ولم تطيعوا ربكم إذ دعاكم. وهذا دليل على أنّ الإنسان هو الذي يختار الشقاوة أو السعادة ويحصلها لنفسه، «2» وليس من الله إلا التمكين، ولا من الشيطان إلا التزيين. ولو كان الأمر كما تزعم المجبرة لقال: فلا تلوموني ولا أنفسكم، فإنّ الله قضى عليكم الكفر وأجبركم عليه. فإن قلت:
Vol. 2, p. 551
Satan's speech is false and it is not sound to rely upon it. I say: had this speech from him been false, God would have made clear its falsity and shown His denial of it, besides which there is no benefit to him in uttering falsehood in that place: do you not see His saying "Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, then I betrayed you," how he came in it with truth and honesty, and in His saying "and I had no authority over you," which is like the saying of God, Exalted is He: "Indeed, My servants, there is for you no authority over them, except those who follow you of the deviators"? "I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper": none of us saves another from the punishment of God, nor helps him. Al-iṣrākh is helping. It has also been read bi-muṣrikhiyi, with a kasra on the yāʾ, which is weak, and they cited for it a verse of unknown authorship: "He said to her: 'Do you have [any desire], O woman?' She said to him: 'You are not the approved one' (1)." It is as though he supposed the yāʾ of annexation to be silent with a silent yāʾ before it, so he vowelized it with a kasra, on the basis of the original rule for the meeting of two silent letters; but this is not sound, because the yāʾ of annexation is only vowelized with a fatḥa, where an alif precedes it, as in ʿaṣāya; so what of it when a yāʾ precedes it?
قول الشيطان باطل لا يصح التعلق به. قلت: لو كان هذا القول منه باطلا لبين الله بطلانه وأظهر إنكاره، على أنه لا طائل له في النطق بالباطل في ذلك المقام: ألا ترى إلى قوله إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ وَوَعَدْتُكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ كيف أتى فيه بالحق والصدق، وفي قوله وَما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ وهو مثل قول الله تعالى: إِنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْغاوِينَ، ما أَنَا بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ لا ينجى بعضنا بعضا من عذاب الله ولا يغيثه. والإصراخ: الإغاثة. وقرئ: بمصرخي، بكسر الياء وهي ضعيفة، واستشهدوا لها ببيت مجهول: قَالَ لَهَا هَلْ لَكِ يَا تَافِىِّ … قَالَتْ لَهُ مَا أنْتَ بِالمَرْضِى «1» وكأنه قدّر ياء الإضافة ساكنة وقبلها ياء ساكنة، فحرّكها بالكسر لما عليه أصل التقاء الساكنين، ولكنه غير صحيح، لأنَّ ياء الإضافة لا تكون إلا مفتوحة، حيث قبلها ألف في نحو عصاي، فما بالها وقبلها ياء؟
Question
If you ask: the first yāʾ was treated as a sound letter because of the assimilation, so it is as though it were a yāʾ falling silent after a silent sound letter, and so was vowelized with a kasra by the original rule.
فإن قلت: جرت الياء الأولى مجرى الحرف الصحيح لأجل الإدغام، فكأنها ياء وقعت ساكنة بعد حرف صحيح ساكن، فحرّكت بالكسر على الأصل.
Answer
I say: this is a fine analogy, but the widespread usage, which is in the position of a mass-transmitted report, makes analogies diminish before it. "Mā" in "bi-mā ashraktumūni" is a source-particle, and "from before" is connected to "ashraktumūni," meaning: "I disbelieve today in your associating me [with God] before this day," that is, in the world, as in His saying, Exalted is He, "and on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association"; and the meaning of his disbelief in their associating him is his disavowal of it and denouncing it, as in His saying, Exalted is He, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship besides God; we have denied you." It is also said that "from before" is connected to "I disbelieved," and "mā" is a relative, that is: I disbelieved before, when I refused to prostrate to Adam, in the One whom you made me a partner of, and He is God, Mighty and Majestic; you say "I made Zayd a partner," and when you make it transitive by the hamza you say "ashrakanīhi fulān," that is, made me a partner to him. Like this "mā" is the "mā" in their saying: "Glory be to the One who subjected these to us" (subḥāna mā sakhkharakunna lanā). The meaning of their associating Satan with God is their obedience
قلت: هذا قياس حسن، ولكن الاستعمال المستفيض الذي هو بمنزلة الخبر المتواتر تتضاءل إليه القياسات. «ما» في بِما أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ مصدرية، ومِنْ قَبْلُ متعلقة بأشركتمونى، يعنى: كفرت اليوم بإشراككم إياى من قبل هذا اليوم، أى في الدنيا، كقوله تعالى وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِكُمْ ومعنى كفره بإشراكهم إياه: تبرؤه منه واستنكاره له، كقوله تعالى إِنَّا بُرَآؤُا مِنْكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَفَرْنا بِكُمْ وقيل: مِنْ قَبْلُ يتعلق بكفرت. وما موصولة، أى: كفرت من قبل حين أبيت السجود لآدم بالذي أَشركتمونيه وهو الله عز وجل، تقول: شركت زيداً، فإذا نقلت بالهمزة قلت: أَشركنيه فلان، أى: جعلني له شريكا. ونحو «ما» هذه «ما» في قولهم: سبحان ما سخركنّ لنا. ومعنى إشراكهم الشيطان بالله: طاعتهم
Vol. 2, p. 552
of him in what he used to adorn for them of worshipping idols and other things, and this is the end of Iblīs's speech. And His saying "Indeed, for the wrongdoers..." is the speech of God, Mighty and Majestic. It is also possible that it is part of the speech of Iblīs, and that God, Mighty and Exalted, related only what he will say at that time, so that it may be a kindness to the hearers in looking to their final outcome and preparing for what they must inevitably reach, and that they picture in themselves that standing in which Satan says what he says, so that they fear and do what will free them from it and save them. It has also been read fa-lā yalūmūnī with yāʾ, by way of a shift of person, as in His saying, Exalted is He, "until when you are in the ships and they run with them."
له فيما كان يزينه لهم من عبادة الأوثان وغيرها، وهذا آخر قوله إبليس. وقوله إِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ قول الله عز وجل. ويحتمل أن يكون من جملة قول إبليس، وإنما حكى الله عزّ وعلا ما سيقوله في ذلك الوقت، ليكون لطفا للسامعين في النظر لعاقبتهم والاستعداد لما لا بدّ لهم من الوصول إليه، وأن يتصوّروا في أنفسهم ذلك المقام الذي يقول الشيطان فيه ما يقول، فيخافوا ويعملوا ما يخلصهم منه وينجيهم. وقرئ: فلا يلومونى، بالياء على طريقة الالتفات، كقوله تعالى حَتَّى إِذا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 550
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "It is reported that Satan will stand at that time as a preacher..." etc. Aḥmad said: He interpreted the saying of the unbelievers in the first verse as annulment of ascription [of blame to God], because it does not suit his belief, and cited as proof that lying then is not impossible or unattainable God's saying "so they will swear to Him as they swear to you." Then, when he thought that this saying of Satan suits his belief, he strove to prove it right and sound, even though its speaker is Satan; all of that is from him a following of whim wherever it turns and whichever way it goes. And we, the Ahl al-Sunna, whom he nicknames the Mujbira, say: God, Exalted is He, cited this speech not rejecting it, nor declaring Satan mistaken in it, just as He recounted the speech of the unbelievers in the first verse. And we believe that blame is directed only to the one charged with duties, while God, Exalted is He, is far above it, and His is the conclusive argument and the true decree. That is because we acknowledge what God, Exalted is He, created for the servant of the choice which he finds in himself, by necessity, in the pull of the two sides of voluntary acts, and by that the argument stands for Him against His creation, even though we deprive created power of effect in the act; so there is no contradiction between the creed of the Sunna and directing blame to the one charged with duties. And God is the Granter of success. [.....]
2. . His statement "chooses wretchedness or happiness and brings it about for himself": this is the school of the Muʿtazila; and his word "al-mujbira" means the Ahl al-Sunna, whose school is that God is the Creator of the causes of happiness and the causes of wretchedness, but the servant has acquisition (kasb) in them, and from this blame is directed at him, contrary to the Muʿtazila in their saying that the servant is the creator of them and is the one who brings it about for himself. Its verification is in the science of tawḥīd. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «روى أن الشيطان يقوم عند ذلك خطيبا
…. الخ» قال أحمد: قد حمل قول الكفار في الآية الأولى على إبطال الانتحال، لأنه لا يلائم معتقده، واستشهد على أن الكذب حينئذ غير ممتنع ولا متعذر بقول تعالى فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ ثم لما ظن أن قول الشيطان هذا يلائم معتقده، اجتهد في الاستدلال على تصويبه وتصحيحه وإن كان قائله الشيطان، كل ذلك منه اتباع للهوى حيثما توجه وأية سلك. ونحن معاشر أهل السنة الملقبين عنده بالمجبرة نقول: إن الله تعالى إنما أورد هذا الكلام غير راد له، ولا مخطئ فيه الشيطان، كما اقتص كلام الكفار في الآية الأولى كذلك. ونحن نعتقد أن الملامة إنما تتوجه على المكلف وأما الله تعالى فمقدس عن ذلك. وحجته البالغة، وقضاؤه الحق. وذلك أنا نعترف بما خلقه الله تعالى للعبد من الاختيار الذي يجده من نفسه عند تجاذب طرفى الأفعال الارادية ضرورة، وبذلك قامت الحجة له على خلقه، وإن سلبنا عن قدرة الخلق تأثيرها في الفعل، فلا تناقض إذاً بين عقيدة السنة وبين صرف الملامة إلى المكلف، والله الموفق. [.....]
2. . قوله «يختار الشقاوة أو السعادة ويحصلها لنفسه» هذا مذهب المعتزلة، وقوله «المجبرة» يعنى أهل السنة، ومذهبهم أن الله هو الخالق لأسباب السعادة وأسباب الشقاوة، لكن العبد له فيها الكسب. ومن هذا يتوجه عليه اللوم، خلافا للمعتزلة في قولهم: إن العبد هو الخالق لها، وهو الذي يحصل لنفسه. وتحقيقه في علم التوحيد. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 551
1. (1). "He said to her: 'Do you have [any desire], O woman? / She said to him: You are not the approved one, / One who goes ahead whenever he sets out to go ahead.'" Its speaker is unknown. Tā is a demonstrative, that is, "O this woman, do you have a desire for...?" The original of the yāʾ of the first person is silence, and if vowelized it is with fatḥa, but since here it met, silent, the yāʾ before it, vowelizing it with kasra was allowed, on the original rule in escaping from the meeting of two silent letters. "She said" is a new sentence, as though he was asked: "And what did she say?" and he said: "She said to him: you are not approved, for you are a man who goes ahead in every matter he is bent upon." So "going ahead" (māḍin) is the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is a new answer to the question about the reason for non-approval. And he expressed with the third-person pronoun in his saying "hum" as parallels for the good. It is also possible to supply the subject as the word "huwa," in which case it would be a shift from address to third person, indicating turning away from him and mentioning the reason to someone else.
1. (1) . قال لها هل لك يا تافىّ
…. قالت له ما أنت بالمرضى ماض إذا ما هم بالمضي قائله مجهول. وتا: اسم إشارة، أى: هل لك يا هذه المرأة رغبة في. وأصل ياء المتكلم السكون، فان حركت فبالفتح، لكن لما التقت هنا ساكنة مع الياء قبلها ساغ كسرها، على الأصل في التخلص من التقاء الساكنين. وقالت: استئناف، كأنه قيل له: فماذا قالت؟ فقال: قالت له لست مرضيا، فإنك رجل ماض في كل أمرتهمّ فيه، فماض: خبر لمبتدإ محذوف. والجملة: استئناف جواب للسؤال عن علة عدم الرضا. وعبر بضمير الغيبة في قوله: هم نظراء للخير. ويجوز تقدير المبتدأ لفظ «هو» فيكون التفاتا من الخطاب إلى الغيبة، دلالة على الاعراض عنه، وذكر السبب لغيره.
Vol. 2, p. 552
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "And al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd read: wa-udkhilu alladhīna āmanū in the first-person verb..." etc. Aḥmad said: If you ask: what turned al-Zamakhsharī away from taking it as a shift of person from first to third, and forced him to connect it with what follows, when he had latitude in that, and the shift of person in this manner is frequent and widespread? Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He, "Ṭā Hā. We did not send down to you the Qurʾān that you be distressed," then He said "a revelation from the One who created the earth," and did not say "a revelation from Us." I say: it was for some reason that he turned the speech away from this way, namely that the apparent sense of "udkhila" in the first-person form intimates that their admission to Paradise was not through an intermediary but from God, Exalted is He, directly, whereas the apparent sense of "permission" intimates ascribing the entering to an intermediary, so there is a clash between them; but in my view it is good that it be connected with "abiding," and abiding is other than entering, so there is no clash. And God knows best.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد: وأدخل الذين آمنوا على فعل المتكلم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فان قلت: ما الذي صرف الزمخشري عن حمله على الالتفات من التكلم إلى الغيبة، وألجأه إلى تعليقه بما بعده، وقد كانت له في ذلك مندوحة، والالتفات على هذا الوجه كثير مستفيض. ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى طه ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى ثم قال تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ ولم يقل تنزيلا منا. قلت: لأمر ما صرف الكلام عن هذا الوجه، وهو أن ظاهر أُدْخِلَ بلفظ المتكلم، يشعر بأن إدخالهم الجنة لم يكن بواسطة، بل من الله تعالى مباشرة، وظاهر الاذن يشعر باضافة الدخول إلى الواسطة، فبينهما تنافر، ولكن يحسن عندي أن يعلق بخالدين، والخلود غير الدخول، فلا تنافر، والله أعلم.
17
Q 14:23 · Vol. 2, p. 552

Verse 23

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein by permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be 'Peace.'" (23)
وَأُدْخِلَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ تَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ (23)
Vol. 2, p. 552
Al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd read: wa-udkhilu alladhīna āmanū (1), in the first-person verb, in the sense of "and I will admit"; and this is proof that it is from the speech of God, not from the speech of Iblīs. "By permission of their Lord" is connected with "admitted," that is: the angels admitted them to Paradise by God's permission and command.
وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد: وأدخل الذين آمنوا، «1» على فعل المتكلم، بمعنى: وأدخل أنا وهذا دليل على أنه من قول الله، لا من قوله إبليس بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ متعلق بأدخل، أى: أدخلتهم الملائكة الجنة بإذن الله وأمره.
Question
If you ask: in the other reading what does it connect with, since your saying "and I will admit them, by permission of their Lord" is an ill-fitting utterance?
فإن قلت: فبهم يتعلق في القراءة الأخرى، وقولك: وأدخلهم أنا بإذن ربهم، كلام غير ملتئم؟
Answer
I say: the way in this reading is that His saying "by permission of their Lord" be connected with what follows it, that is, "their greeting therein will be 'Peace,' by permission of their Lord," meaning that the angels greet them by permission of their Lord.
قلت: الوجه في هذه القراءة أن يتعلق قوله: بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ بما بعده، أى تَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ بإذن ربهم، يعنى: أن الملائكة يحيونهم بإذن ربهم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 552
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "And al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd read: wa-udkhilu alladhīna āmanū in the first-person verb..." etc. Aḥmad said: If you ask: what turned al-Zamakhsharī away from taking it as a shift of person from first to third, and forced him to connect it with what follows, when he had latitude in that, and the shift of person in this manner is frequent and widespread? Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He, "Ṭā Hā. We did not send down to you the Qurʾān that you be distressed," then He said "a revelation from the One who created the earth," and did not say "a revelation from Us." I say: it was for some reason that he turned the speech away from this way, namely that the apparent sense of "udkhila" in the first-person form intimates that their admission to Paradise was not through an intermediary but from God, Exalted is He, directly, whereas the apparent sense of "permission" intimates ascribing the entering to an intermediary, so there is a clash between them; but in my view it is good that it be connected with "abiding," and abiding is other than entering, so there is no clash. And God knows best.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد: وأدخل الذين آمنوا على فعل المتكلم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فان قلت: ما الذي صرف الزمخشري عن حمله على الالتفات من التكلم إلى الغيبة، وألجأه إلى تعليقه بما بعده، وقد كانت له في ذلك مندوحة، والالتفات على هذا الوجه كثير مستفيض. ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى طه ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى ثم قال تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ ولم يقل تنزيلا منا. قلت: لأمر ما صرف الكلام عن هذا الوجه، وهو أن ظاهر أُدْخِلَ بلفظ المتكلم، يشعر بأن إدخالهم الجنة لم يكن بواسطة، بل من الله تعالى مباشرة، وظاهر الاذن يشعر باضافة الدخول إلى الواسطة، فبينهما تنافر، ولكن يحسن عندي أن يعلق بخالدين، والخلود غير الدخول، فلا تنافر، والله أعلم.
18
Q 14:24–25 · Vol. 2, pp. 552–553

Verses 24 to 25

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Have you not considered how God presents an example: a good word, like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches [high] in the sky? (24) It produces its fruit all the time, by permission of its Lord. And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded." (25)
أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلاً كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُها ثابِتٌ وَفَرْعُها فِي السَّماءِ (24) تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّها وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ (25)
Vol. 2, p. 552
"Have you not seen" has been read with a sukūn on the rā', as "whoever fears [God]" was read, and there is weakness in it. "God presents an example": He relied on an example and set it down. And "a good word" is in the accusative by an implied verb, that is: "He made a good word like a good tree," and it is
قرئ أَلَمْ تَرَ ساكنة الراء، كما قرئ: من يتق، وفيه ضعف ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا اعتمد مثلا ووضعه. وكَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً نصب بمضمر، أى: جعل كلمة طيبة كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وهو
Vol. 2, p. 553
an explanation of His saying "God presents an example," as you say: "The emir honored Zayd: he clothed him with a robe and mounted him on a horse." It is also possible that "an example" and "a good word" are both accusative by "presents," that is: "He presented a good word as an example," in the sense of making it an example; then He said "like a good tree," as a predicate of an omitted subject, in the sense of "it is like a good tree," "whose root is firmly fixed," meaning in the earth, striking its roots in it, "and its branch" and its uppermost part and its head "in the sky." It is also possible that He means "and its branches," by being satisfied with the wording of the genus. Anas b. Mālik read: ka-shajaratin ṭayyibatin thābitin aṣluhā.
تفسير لقوله ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا كقولك: شرّف الأمير زيداً: كساه حلة، وحمله على فرس. ويجوز أن ينتصب مَثَلًا وكَلِمَةً بضرب، أى: ضرب كلمة طيبة مثلا، بمعنى: جعلها مثلا ثم قال كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ على أنها خبر مبتدأ محذوف، بمعنى هي كشجرة طيبة أَصْلُها ثابِتٌ يعنى في الأرض ضارب بعروقه فيها وَفَرْعُها وأعلاها ورأسها فِي السَّماءِ ويجوز أن يريد: وفروعها، على الاكتفاء بلفظ الجنس. وقرأ أنس بن مالك: كشجرة طيبة ثابت أصلها
Question
If you ask: what is the difference between the two readings?
فإن قلت: أىّ فرق بين القراءتين؟
Answer
I say: the reading of the community is stronger in meaning, because in the reading of Anas the description was made to run upon the tree; and when you say "I passed by a man whose father is standing" (abūhu qāʾim), it is stronger in meaning than your saying "I passed by a man standing is his father" (qāʾimin abūhu), because the one reported about is the father and not the man. The good word is the word of tawḥīd. It is also said: every good word, like glorification, praise, seeking forgiveness, repentance and invitation. From Ibn ʿAbbās: the testimony that there is no god but God. As for the tree, it is every fruit-bearing tree with good fruits, like the date palm, the fig tree, the grapevine, the pomegranate and others. From Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of God ﷺ said one day: "God has presented the example of the believer as a tree; so tell me what it is" (1). The people fell to thinking of desert trees, and I was a boy, and it occurred to my heart that it was the date palm, but I was awed to say it, being the youngest of the people. It is also related: "The presence of ʿUmar [my father] stopped me; I was shy." ʿUmar said to me: "My son, had you said it, it would have been dearer to me than red camels." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "It is the date palm." From Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with both: a tree in Paradise. His saying "in the sky" means in the direction of height and ascent, and does not mean the canopy [of heaven], as you say of a mountain "tall into the sky," meaning its height and loftiness. "It produces its fruit all the time": it gives its fruit at every time God has appointed for its fruiting, "by permission of its Lord," by the facilitation of its Creator and His bringing it into being. "That perhaps they will be reminded," because in presenting examples there is increased understanding and reminding and depicting of meanings.
قلت: قراءة الجماعة أقوى معنى، لأنّ في قراءة أنس أجريت الصفة على الشجرة، وإذا قلت: مررت برجل أبوه قائم، فهو أقوى معنى من قولك: مررت برجل قائم أبوه، لأنّ المخبر عنه إنما هو الأب لا رجل. والكلمة الطيبة: كلمة التوحيد. وقيل: كل كلمة حسنة كالتسبيحة والتحميدة والاستغفار والتوبة والدعوة. وعن ابن عباس: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله. وأما الشجرة فكل شجرة مثمرة طيبة النمار، كالنخلة وشجرة التين والعنب والرمّان وغير ذلك. وعن ابن عمر أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ذات يوم: «إن الله ضرب مثل المؤمن شجرة فأخبرونى ما هي» «1» فوقع الناس في شجر البوادي، وكنت صبيا، فوقع في قلبي أنها النخلة، فهبت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أقولها وأنا أصغر القوم. وروى: فمنعني مكان عمرو استحييت، فقال لي عمر: يا بنىّ لو كنت قلتها لكانت أحبّ إلىّ من حمر النعم، ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «ألا إنها النخلة» وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: شجرة في الجنة وقوله فِي السَّماءِ معناه في جهة العلوّ والصعود، ولم يرد المظلة، كقولك في الجبل: طويل في السماء تريد ارتفاعه وشموخه تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ تعطى ثمرها كل وقت وقته الله لإثمارها بِإِذْنِ رَبِّها بتيسير خالقها وتكوينه لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ لأن في ضرب الأمثال زيادة إفهام وتذكير وتصوير للمعاني.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 552
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "And al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd read: wa-udkhilu alladhīna āmanū in the first-person verb..." etc. Aḥmad said: If you ask: what turned al-Zamakhsharī away from taking it as a shift of person from first to third, and forced him to connect it with what follows, when he had latitude in that, and the shift of person in this manner is frequent and widespread? 1. (1) . قال محمود: «وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد: وأدخل الذين آمنوا على فعل المتكلم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فان قلت: ما الذي صرف الزمخشري عن حمله على الالتفات من التكلم إلى الغيبة، وألجأه إلى تعليقه بما بعده، وقد كانت له في ذلك مندوحة، والالتفات على هذا الوجه كثير مستفيض. ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى طه ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى ثم قال تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ ولم يقل تنزيلا منا. قلت: لأمر ما صرف الكلام عن هذا الوجه، وهو أن ظاهر أُدْخِلَ بلفظ المتكلم، يشعر بأن إدخالهم الجنة لم يكن بواسطة، بل من الله تعالى مباشرة، وظاهر الاذن يشعر باضافة الدخول إلى الواسطة، فبينهما تنافر، ولكن يحسن عندي أن يعلق بخالدين، والخلود غير الدخول، فلا تنافر، والله أعلم.

1. (1). Agreed upon, with several wordings.
2. . His word "al-kushūth": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-kushūth is a plant that clings to the branches of trees without striking a root in the earth. The poet said: "It is the dodder: it has no root nor leaf, nor breeze, nor shade, nor fruit." (ʿ)
1. (1) . متفق عليه وله ألفاظ.
2. . قوله «والكشوث» في الصحاح الكشوث نبت يتعلق بأغصان الشجر من غير أن يضرب بعرق في الأرض. قال الشاعر: هو الكشوث فلا أصل ولا ورق
…. ولا نسيم ولا ظل ولا ثمر (ع)
19
Q 14:26 · Vol. 2, pp. 553–554

Verse 26

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And the example of a evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, not having any stability." (26)
وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ اجْتُثَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْأَرْضِ ما لَها مِنْ قَرارٍ (26)
Vol. 2, p. 553
"Like an evil tree" means "like the example of an evil tree," that is: its description is like its description. It has also been read wa-mathala kalimatin in the accusative, coordinated to "a good word." The evil word is the word of associating partners [with God]. It is also said: every ugly word. As for the evil tree, it is every tree whose fruit is not good, like the colocynth tree and the dodder (2) and the like. His saying "uprooted from the surface of the earth" is in contrast to His saying "its root is firmly fixed," and the meaning of "uprooted" is torn out by the roots. The truth of ijtithāth
كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كمثل شجرة خبيثة، أى: صفتها كصفتها. وقرئ: ومثل كلمة بالنصب، عطفا على كلمة طيبة. والكلمة الخبيثة: كلمة الشرك. وقيل: كل كلمة قبيحة. وأمّا الشجرة الخبيثة فكل شجرة لا يطيب ثمرها كشجرة الحنظل والكشوث «2» ونحو ذلك. وقوله اجْتُثَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْأَرْضِ في مقابلة قوله أَصْلُها ثابِتٌ ومعنى اجْتُثَّتْ استؤصلت. وحقيقة الاجتثاث
Vol. 2, p. 554
is taking the whole body (juththa). "Not having any stability" (qarār), that is, settling. One says qarra al-shayʾ qarāran, like "he was firm, thabāt"; He likened to it speech that is not supported by proof, which is refuted and not firm; and what does not remain either fades soon because of its falsity, from their saying "falsehood is jumbled (lajlaj)" (1). From Qatāda: one of the scholars was asked: "What do you say about an evil word?" He said: "I know for it no settling place in the earth, nor any ascent in the sky, except that it clings to the neck of its speaker until he arrives with it at the Resurrection."
أخذ الجثة كلها ما لَها مِنْ قَرارٍ أى استقرار. يقال: قرّ الشيء قراراً، كقولك: ثبت ثباتا، شبه بها القول الذي لم يعضد بحجة، فهو داحض غير ثابت والذي لا يبقى إما يضمحل عن قريب لبطلانه، من قولهم: الباطل لجلج «1» . وعن قتادة أنه قيل لبعض العلماء: ما تقول في كلمة خبيثة؟ فقال: ما أعلم لها في الأرض مستقراً، ولا في السماء مصعداً، إلا أن تلزم عنق صاحبها حتى يوافى بها القيامة.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 553
1. (1). Agreed upon, with several wordings.
2. . His word "al-kushūth": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-kushūth is a plant that clings to the branches of trees without striking a root in the earth. The poet said: "It is the dodder: it has no root nor leaf, nor breeze, nor shade, nor fruit." (ʿ)
1. (1) . متفق عليه وله ألفاظ.
2. . قوله «والكشوث» في الصحاح الكشوث نبت يتعلق بأغصان الشجر من غير أن يضرب بعرق في الأرض. قال الشاعر: هو الكشوث فلا أصل ولا ورق
…. ولا نسيم ولا ظل ولا ثمر (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 554
1. (1). His statement "from their saying: al-bāṭil lajlaj": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "the truth is clear (ablaj), and falsehood is jumbled (lajlaj)," that is, it is bandied back and forth without getting through. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "the firm word, which became firm through proof": since the good word was interpreted as the word of tawḥīd and the evil one as the word of associating partners, the fitting interpretation of the firm word is the saying "There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God," and the leading astray of the wrongdoers is leaving them upon the word of associating partners: "Indeed, associating [others] with God is great injustice." As for holding to proof and imitating shaykhs, it is far from the context. And in it is a rebuttal of the Ahl al-Sunna, who are content with imitation in the realization of faith. (ʿ)
3. . This is a part of a long ḥadīth of his, transmitted by Abū Dāwūd, Abū ʿAwāna, al-Ḥākim, Aḥmad, Ibn Rāhawayh, Ibn Abī Shayba and Abū Yaʿlā from the transmission of Saʿd b. ʿUbayda; in al-Bukhārī, raised [to the Prophet], regarding His saying "God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word": he said: it was revealed regarding the punishment of the grave. It is said to him: "Who is your Lord and who is your prophet?" and he says: "My Lord is God and my prophet is Muḥammad ﷺ." That is His saying, Exalted is He, "God keeps firm those who believe..." the verse.
1. (1) . قوله «من قولهم الباطل لجلج» في الصحاح: الحق أبلج، والباطل لجلج، أى: يردد من غير أن ينفذ. (ع)
2. . قوله «القول الثابت الذي ثبت بالحجة» لما فسرت الكلمة الطيبة بكلمة التوحيد والخبيثة بكلمة الشرك، فالمتجه تفسير القول الثابت بقول «لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله» وإضلال الظالمين بابقائهم على كلمة الشرك، إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ وأما التمسك بالحجة وتقليد الشيوخ فبعيد عن السياق. وفيه رد على أهل السنة المكتفين بالتقليد في تحقق الايمان. (ع)
3. . هذا طرف من حديث له طويل أخرجه أبو داود وأبو عوانة والحاكم وأحمد وابن راهويه وابن أبى شيبة وأبو يعلى من رواية سعد بن عبيدة عند البخاري مرفوعا في قوله يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ قال: نزلت في عذاب القبر. يقال له: من ربك ومن نبيك؟ فيقول: ربى الله. ونبى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. وذلك قوله تعالى يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا
…. الآية.
20
Q 14:27 · Vol. 2, pp. 554–555

Verse 27

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"God keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And God sends astray the wrongdoers. And God does what He wills." (27)
يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ (27)
Vol. 2, p. 554
"With the firm word" is that which has become firm in the heart of its owner through proof (2) and demonstration, and has settled in it, so he believes it and his soul is at ease with it. Their being kept firm by it in this world: that when they are tried in their religion they do not slip, as those whom the People of the Trench tried stood firm, and those who were sawed with saws and whose flesh was combed with iron combs, and as Jirjīs and Shamsūn and others stood firm. And their being kept firm in the Hereafter: that when they are asked, at the standing of the witnesses, about their belief and their religion, they will not falter nor be dumbfounded, and the terrors of the Gathering will not confound them. It is also said that its meaning is firmness at the questioning in the grave. From al-Barāʾ b. ʿĀzib ؓ that the Messenger of God ﷺ mentioned the taking of the believer's soul and said: "Then his soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and sit him up in his grave and say to him: 'Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muḥammad.' Then a caller calls from heaven: 'My servant has spoken truly.' That is His saying: 'God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word'" (3). "And God sends astray the wrongdoers," who did not hold to any proof in their religion, but confined themselves to imitating their elders and shaykhs, as the polytheists imitated their fathers and said "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion"; and their being led astray in this world is that they do not stand firm in the places of trial and their feet slip at the very first thing, and in the Hereafter they are more astray and more abased. "And God does what He wills," that is, what wisdom requires, because God's will follows
بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ الذي ثبت بالحجة «2» والبرهان في قلب صاحبه وتمكن فيه، فاعتقده واطمأنت إليه نفسه. وتثبيتهم به في الدنيا: أنهم إذا فتنوا في دينهم لم يزلوا، كما ثبت الذين فتنهم أصحاب الأخدود، والذين نشروا بالمناشير ومشطت لحومهم بأمشاط الحديد، وكما ثبت جرجيس وشمسون وغيرهما. وتثبيتهم في الآخرة. أنهم إذا سئلوا عند تواقف الأشهاد عن معتقدهم ودينهم، لم يتلعثموا ولم يبهتوا، ولم تحيرهم أهوال الحشر. وقيل معناه الثبات عند سؤال القبر. وعن البراء ابن عازب رضى الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر قبض روح المؤمن فقال «ثم يعاد روحه في جسده فيأتيه ملكان فيجلسانه في قبره ويقولان له: من ربك؟ وما دينك؟ ومن نبيك؟ فيقول: ربى الله، ودينى الإسلام، ونبيي محمد، فينادى مناد من السماء أن صدق عبدى فذلك قوله: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت» «3» وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ الذين لم يتمسكوا بحجة في دينهم، وإنما اقتصروا على تقليد كبارهم وشيوخهم، كما قلد المشركون آباءهم فقالوا إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وإضلالهم في الدنيا أنهم لا يثبتون في مواقف الفتن وتزل أقدامهم أوّل شيء، وهم في الآخرة أضل وأذل وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ أى ما توجبه الحكمة، لأن مشيئة الله تابعة
Vol. 2, p. 555
wisdom: of keeping the believers firm and supporting them, protecting them in their steadfastness and resolve, and of leading the wrongdoers astray and abandoning them, and leaving them to their own affair at their slips.
للحكمة، من تثبيت المؤمنين وتأييدهم، وعصمتهم عند ثباتهم وعزمهم، ومن إضلال الظالمين وخذلانهم، والتخلية بينهم وبين شأنهم عند زللهم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 554
1. (1). His statement "from their saying: al-bāṭil lajlaj": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "the truth is clear (ablaj), and falsehood is jumbled (lajlaj)," that is, it is bandied back and forth without getting through. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "the firm word, which became firm through proof": since the good word was interpreted as the word of tawḥīd and the evil one as the word of associating partners, the fitting interpretation of the firm word is the saying "There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God," and the leading astray of the wrongdoers is leaving them upon the word of associating partners: "Indeed, associating [others] with God is great injustice." As for holding to proof and imitating shaykhs, it is far from the context. And in it is a rebuttal of the Ahl al-Sunna, who are content with imitation in the realization of faith. (ʿ)
3. . This is a part of a long ḥadīth of his, transmitted by Abū Dāwūd, Abū ʿAwāna, al-Ḥākim, Aḥmad, Ibn Rāhawayh, Ibn Abī Shayba and Abū Yaʿlā from the transmission of Saʿd b. ʿUbayda; in al-Bukhārī, raised [to the Prophet], regarding His saying "God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word": he said: it was revealed regarding the punishment of the grave. It is said to him: "Who is your Lord and who is your prophet?" and he says: "My Lord is God and my prophet is Muḥammad ﷺ." That is His saying, Exalted is He, "God keeps firm those who believe..." the verse.
1. (1) . قوله «من قولهم الباطل لجلج» في الصحاح: الحق أبلج، والباطل لجلج، أى: يردد من غير أن ينفذ. (ع)
2. . قوله «القول الثابت الذي ثبت بالحجة» لما فسرت الكلمة الطيبة بكلمة التوحيد والخبيثة بكلمة الشرك، فالمتجه تفسير القول الثابت بقول «لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله» وإضلال الظالمين بابقائهم على كلمة الشرك، إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ وأما التمسك بالحجة وتقليد الشيوخ فبعيد عن السياق. وفيه رد على أهل السنة المكتفين بالتقليد في تحقق الايمان. (ع)
3. . هذا طرف من حديث له طويل أخرجه أبو داود وأبو عوانة والحاكم وأحمد وابن راهويه وابن أبى شيبة وأبو يعلى من رواية سعد بن عبيدة عند البخاري مرفوعا في قوله يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ قال: نزلت في عذاب القبر. يقال له: من ربك ومن نبيك؟ فيقول: ربى الله. ونبى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. وذلك قوله تعالى يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا
…. الآية.
21
Q 14:28–30 · Vol. 2, p. 555

Verses 28 to 30

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin," (28) "Hell, which they will enter? And wretched is the settlement." (29) "And they set up rivals to God to mislead [people] from His way. Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire.'" (30)
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ كُفْراً وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ دارَ الْبَوارِ (28) جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَها وَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ (29) وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْداداً لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ قُلْ تَمَتَّعُوا فَإِنَّ مَصِيرَكُمْ إِلَى النَّارِ (30)
Vol. 2, p. 555
"They exchanged the favor of God for disbelief," that is, the gratitude for God's favor, [exchanged] for disbelief, because they put disbelief in the place of the gratitude for it that was obligatory upon them, so it is as though they changed gratitude into disbelief and exchanged it. Similar is "and you make your provision that you deny," that is, the gratitude for your provision, in that you put denial in its place. And there is another way: that they exchanged the very favor for disbelief, in that when they disbelieved in it they were stripped of it, so they were left stripped of the favor, described with disbelief, with disbelief accruing to them in place of the favor. They are the people of Mecca: God settled them in His sanctuary, made them the keepers of His House, and honored them with Muḥammad ﷺ but they disbelieved in God's favor instead of the great gratitude that was incumbent on them. Or God afflicted them with favor, in ease and abundance, through their accustomedness to the two journeys, but they disbelieved in His favor, so He struck them with drought for seven years, so disbelief accrued to them in place of the favor; so too when they were captured and killed on the day of Badr, the favor had gone from them and disbelief remained a collar upon their necks. From ʿUmar ؓ: they are the two most wicked [clans] of Quraysh: Banū al-Mughīra and Banū Umayya; as for Banū al-Mughīra, you were spared [dealing with] them on the day of Badr; as for Banū Umayya, they were given enjoyment for a while. It is also said: they are the Arabs who became Christian: Jabala b. al-Ayham and his companions. "And settled their people," of those who followed them in disbelief, "in the home of ruin," the home of destruction. And "Hell" is coordinated to "the home of ruin" as an explanatory apposition. "To mislead" has been read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and with a ḍamma.
بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ أى شكر نعمة الله كُفْراً لأن شكرها الذي وجب عليهم وضعوا مكانه كفراً، فكأنهم غيروا الشكر إلى الكفر وبدلوه تبديلا، ونحوه وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ أى شكر رزقكم حيث وضعتم التكذيب موضعه. ووجه آخر: وهو أنهم بدلوا نفس النعمة كفراً على أنهم لما كفروها سلبوها فبقوا مسلوبي النعمة موصوفين بالكفر، حاصلا لهم الكفر بدل النعمة. وهم أهل مكة: أسكنهم الله حرمه، وجعلهم قوّام بيته، وأكرمهم بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فكفروا نعمة الله بدل ما لزمهم من الشكر العظيم. أو أصابهم الله بالنعمة في الرخاء والسعة لإيلافهم الرحلتين، فكفروا نعمته، فضربهم بالقحط سبع سنين، فحصل لهم الكفر بدل النعمة، كذلك حين أسروا وقتلوا يوم بدر وقد ذهبت عنهم النعمة وبقي الكفر طوقا في أعناقهم. وعن عمر رضى الله عنه: هم الأفجران من قريش: بنو المغيرة وبنو أمية، فأما بنو المغيرة فكفيتموهم يوم بدر. وأما بنو أمية فمتعوا حتى حين. وقيل: هم متنصرة العرب: جبلة بن الأيهم وأصحابه وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ ممن تابعهم على الكفر دارَ الْبَوارِ دار الهلاك. وعطف جَهَنَّمَ على دار البوار عطف بيان. قرئ لِيُضِلُّوا بفتح الياء وضمها.
Question
If you ask: error and leading astray were not their aim in taking up rivals, so what is the meaning of the lām?
فإن قلت: الضلال والإضلال لم يكن غرضهم في اتخاذ الأنداد، فما معنى اللام؟
Answer
I say: since error and leading astray were the result of taking up rivals, as the honoring was, in your saying "I came to you that you might honor me," the result of the coming, the lām entered it even though it was not an aim, by way of likening and approximation. "Enjoy yourselves" is an announcement that, because of their immersion in enjoying the present, and that they know nothing else and want nothing else, they are commanded to it; a commander who is obeyed has commanded them, whom they cannot disobey, and they have no command of their own besides it, and that is the command of desire. The meaning is: "If you continue upon what you are of complying with the command of desire, then indeed your destination is the Fire." It is also possible that abandonment and being left alone is meant; similar is "Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed you are of the companions of the Fire.'"
قلت: لما كان الضلال والإضلال نتيجة اتخاذ الأنداد، كما كان الإكرام في قولك: جئتك لتكرمنى، نتيجة المجيء، دخلته اللام وإن لم يكن غرضا، على طريق التشبيه والتقريب تَمَتَّعُوا إيذان بأنهم لانغماسهم في التمتع بالحاضر، وأنهم لا يعرفون غيره ولا يريدونه، مأمورون به، قد أمرهم آمر مطاع لا يسعهم أن يخالفوه ولا يملكون لأنفسهم أمراً دونه، وهو أمر الشهوة. والمعنى: إن دمتم على ما أنتم عليه من الامتثال لأمر الشهوة فَإِنَّ مَصِيرَكُمْ إِلَى النَّارِ ويجوز أن يراد الخذلان والتخلية ونحوه قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ.
22
Q 14:31 · Vol. 2, pp. 555–556

Verse 31

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"Tell My servants who have believed to establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, before there comes a Day in which there is no exchange and no friendship." (31)
قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَيُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خِلالٌ (31)
Vol. 2, p. 556
What is to be said is omitted (1), because the answer to "say" indicates it, and its implied form is: "Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer and spend." "Let them establish prayer and spend": they allowed that "yuqīmū" and "yunfiqū" are in the sense of "let them establish" and "let them spend," and that this is the thing said; they said: it is permissible to omit the lām only because the imperative "say" is a substitute for it, and had it been said as an opening "yuqīmū al-ṣalāta wa-yunfiqū," omitting the lām, it would not be allowed.
المقول محذوف، «1» لأن جواب قُلْ يدل عليه، وتقديره قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أقيموا الصلاة وأنفقوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَيُنْفِقُوا وجوزوا أن يكون يقيموا وينفقوا، بمعنى: ليقيموا ولينفقوا، ويكون هذا هو المقول، قالوا: وإنما جاز حذف اللام، لأنّ الأمر الذي هو قُلْ عوض منه، ولو قيل: يقيموا الصلاة وينفقوا ابتداء بحذف اللام، لم يجز.
Question
If you ask: what is the grammatical case of "secretly and publicly"?
فإن قلت: علام انتصب سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً؟
Answer
I say: accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, that is: possessing secrecy and publicness, in the sense of "keeping secret and making public"; or as an adverbial, that is, at times of secrecy and publicness; or as a verbal noun, that is: spending of secrecy and spending of publicness. The meaning: concealing the voluntary of charitable gifts and making public the obligatory. Al-khilāl is friendship (mukhālla).
قلت: على الحال، أى: ذوى سرّ وعلانية، بمعنى: مسرين ومعلنين. أو على الظرف، أى وقتى سر وعلانية، أو على المصدر، أى: إنفاق سر وإنفاق علانية، المعنى: إخفاء المتطوع به من الصدقات والإعلان بالواجب: والخلال: المخالة.
Question
If you ask: how does the command to spend fit with the description of the Day as "no exchange in it and no friendship" (2)?
فإن قلت: كيف طابق الأمر بالإنفاق وصف اليوم بأنه لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خِلالٌ؟ «2»
Answer
I say: because people bring out their wealth in contracts of exchange, giving something in order to take its like, and in acts of generosity and gift-giving to friends so as to draw on [in return] the like of their gifts or better. But spending purely for the face of God, as in His saying "and not for anyone with him is there any favor to be repaid, but only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High," is done only by sincere believers; so they are urged to it, in order to take its replacement on a Day in which there is no exchange and no friendship, that is: no benefit in it from trading nor from friendship, nor from what they spend their wealth upon of exchanges and acts of generosity, and one benefits in it only from spending for the face of God. It has also been read lā bayʿun fīhi wa-lā khilālun with the nominative.
قلت: من قبل أنّ الناس يخرجون أَموالهم في عقود المعاوضات، فيعطون بدلا ليأخذوا مثله، وفي المكارمات ومهاداة الأصدقاء ليستجروا بهداياهم أَمثالها أو خيراً منها. وأمّا الإنفاق لوجه الله خالصا كقوله وَما لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزى إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلى فلا يفعله إلا المؤمنون الخلص، فبعثوا عليه ليأخذوا بدله في يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلال، أى: لا انتفاع فيه بمبايعة ولا بمخالة، ولا بما ينفقون به أَموالهم من المعاوضات والمكارمات، وإنما ينتفع فيه بالإنفاق لوجه الله. وقرئ: لا بيع فيه ولا خلال، بالرفع.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 556
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "What is to be said is omitted..." etc. Aḥmad said: There is something to consider in this grammatical analysis, because the answer would then be a report from God, Exalted is He, that if He says this to them they will comply with its requirement, so they will establish prayer and spend; but it has been said to them and many of them did not comply, and God's report is too exalted to be contradicted. This point is what moved many of the grammarians to turn away from this grammatical analysis, which occurs to one at first glance in what is mentioned; but it can be made sound by taking the general as the majority and not as total inclusion, and it is strengthened by two fine points. One of them: this construction occurs only for one described with true faith, whose faith is lauded in the command, like this verse and like His saying "And tell My servants to say that which is best," "Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts," and "And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze." The second: its repeated coming for those described as servants of God, honored by their annexation to the name of God; and they have said that the word "servants" does not occur in the Noble Book except as praise of the believers, particularly when the annexation of honor to Him, Exalted is He, is added to it. The upshot is that the one commanded in these verses is one who is on the verge of compliance and in the zone of hastening to obedience, so the report regarding their like is true and honest, either as total inclusion if that is meant, or as the majority. And God knows best.
2. . His statement "bi-annahu lā bayʿa fīhi wa-lā khilāl": this reading is with building on the fatḥa. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «المقول محذوف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وفي هذا الاعراب نظر، لأن الجواب حينئذ يكون خبراً من الله تعالى، بأنه إن قال لهم هذا القول امتثلوا مقتضاه فأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا، لكنهم قد قيل لهم فلم يمتثل كثير منهم، وخبر الله تعالى يجل عن الخلف، وهذه النكتة هي الباعثة لكثير من المعربين على العدول عن هذا الوجه من الاعراب من تبادره فيما ذكر بادى الرأى، ويمكن تصحيحه بحمل العام على الغالب لا على الاستغراق، ويقوى بوجهين لطيفين، أحدهما: أن هذا النظم لم يرد إلا لموصوف بالايمان الحق المنوه بإيمانه عند الأمر، كهذه الآية وكقوله وَقُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ، قُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ، وَقُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِناتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصارِهِنَّ الثاني: تكرر مجيئه للموصوفين بأنهم عباد الله المشرفون باضافتهم إلى اسم الله، وقد قالوا إن لفظ العباد لم يرد في الكتاب العزيز إلا مدحة للمؤمنين، وخصوصاً إذا انضاف إليه تعالى إضافة التشريف، فالحاصل من ذلك أن المأمور في هذه الآي من هو بصدد الامتثال وفي حيز المسارعة للطاعة، فالخبر في أمثالهم حق وصدق، إما على العموم إن أريد، أو على الغالب، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «بأنه لا بيع فيه ولا خلال» هذه القراءة بالبناء على الفتح. (ع)

Q 14:32–33 · Vol. 2, pp. 556–557

Verses 32 to 33

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"God is the one who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you; and He subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command; and He subjected for you the rivers." (32) "And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, continuous [in orbit]; and He subjected for you the night and the day." (33)
اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ رِزْقاً لَكُمْ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْفُلْكَ لِتَجْرِيَ فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْهارَ (32) وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ دائِبَيْنِ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ (33)
Vol. 2, p. 557

Vol. 2, p. 556
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "What is to be said is omitted..." etc. Aḥmad said: There is something to consider in this grammatical analysis, because the answer would then be a report from God, Exalted is He, that if He says this to them they will comply with its requirement, so they will establish prayer and spend; but it has been said to them and many of them did not comply, and God's report is too exalted to be contradicted. This point is what moved many of the grammarians to turn away from this grammatical analysis, which occurs to one at first glance in what is mentioned; but it can be made sound by taking the general as the majority and not as total inclusion, and it is strengthened by two fine points. One of them: this construction occurs only for one described with true faith, whose faith is lauded in the command, like this verse and like His saying "And tell My servants to say that which is best," "Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts," and "And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze." The second: its repeated coming for those described as servants of God, honored by their annexation to the name of God; and they have said that the word "servants" does not occur in the Noble Book except as praise of the believers, particularly when the annexation of honor to Him, Exalted is He, is added to it. The upshot is that the one commanded in these verses is one who is on the verge of compliance and in the zone of hastening to obedience, so the report regarding their like is true and honest, either as total inclusion if that is meant, or as the majority. And God knows best.
2. . His statement "bi-annahu lā bayʿa fīhi wa-lā khilāl": this reading is with building on the fatḥa. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «المقول محذوف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وفي هذا الاعراب نظر، لأن الجواب حينئذ يكون خبراً من الله تعالى، بأنه إن قال لهم هذا القول امتثلوا مقتضاه فأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا، لكنهم قد قيل لهم فلم يمتثل كثير منهم، وخبر الله تعالى يجل عن الخلف، وهذه النكتة هي الباعثة لكثير من المعربين على العدول عن هذا الوجه من الاعراب من تبادره فيما ذكر بادى الرأى، ويمكن تصحيحه بحمل العام على الغالب لا على الاستغراق، ويقوى بوجهين لطيفين، أحدهما: أن هذا النظم لم يرد إلا لموصوف بالايمان الحق المنوه بإيمانه عند الأمر، كهذه الآية وكقوله وَقُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ، قُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ، وَقُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِناتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصارِهِنَّ الثاني: تكرر مجيئه للموصوفين بأنهم عباد الله المشرفون باضافتهم إلى اسم الله، وقد قالوا إن لفظ العباد لم يرد في الكتاب العزيز إلا مدحة للمؤمنين، وخصوصاً إذا انضاف إليه تعالى إضافة التشريف، فالحاصل من ذلك أن المأمور في هذه الآي من هو بصدد الامتثال وفي حيز المسارعة للطاعة، فالخبر في أمثالهم حق وصدق، إما على العموم إن أريد، أو على الغالب، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «بأنه لا بيع فيه ولا خلال» هذه القراءة بالبناء على الفتح. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 557

Q 14:32–34 · Vol. 2, p. 557

Verses 32 to 34

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"God is the one who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you; and He subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command; and He subjected for you the rivers." (32) "And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, continuous [in orbit]; and He subjected for you the night and the day." (33) "And He gave you from all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful." (34)
اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ رِزْقاً لَكُمْ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْفُلْكَ لِتَجْرِيَ فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْهارَ (32) وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ دائِبَيْنِ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ (33) وَآتاكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ ما سَأَلْتُمُوهُ وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ لا تُحْصُوها إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَظَلُومٌ كَفَّارٌ (34)
Vol. 2, p. 557
"God" is a subject, and "the one who created" its predicate; and "of the fruits" is an explanation of "provision," that is: He brought forth thereby a provision which is fruits. It is also possible that "of the fruits" is the object of "brought forth," and "provision" a circumstantial qualifier of the object, or an accusative as a verbal noun of "brought forth," because it is in the sense of "provided." "By His command" means by His saying "Be." "Continuous" (dāʾibayn) means they labor on in their course and their giving light and their driving back the darknesses, and their setting right what they set right of the earth and the bodies and the plants. "And He subjected for you the night and the day": they succeed one another for your livelihood and your rest (1). "And He gave you from all that you asked of Him": "min" is partitive, that is, He gave you some of all that you asked of Him, looking to your interests. It has also been read min kullin with tanwīn, and "mā sa'altumūhu" is a negation whose position is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, that is: He gave you of all that without your asking for it; and it is also possible that "mā" is a relative, so: "He gave you of all that what you needed and without which your conditions and livelihoods would not be set right, so it is as though you asked Him for it or demanded it by the tongue of your state." "You could not enumerate them": you could not enclose them or have the ability to count them and reach their end; this if they wished to count them in summary; as for the detail, none is able to do it or knows it but God. "Most unjust": he wrongs the favor by neglecting gratitude for it; "ungrateful," extremely ungrateful for it. It is also said: "unjust" in hardship, he complains and is impatient; "ungrateful" in favor, he hoards and withholds. "Mankind" is for the genus, so the report of injustice and ingratitude covers whoever they are found in.
اللَّهُ مبتدأ، والَّذِي خَلَقَ خبره، ومِنَ الثَّمَراتِ بيان للرزق، أى: أخرج به رزقا هو ثمرات. ويجوز أن يكون مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ مفعول أخرج، ورِزْقاً حالا من المفعول، أَو نصباً على المصدر من أخرج، لأنه في معنى رزق بِأَمْرِهِ بقوله كن دائِبَيْنِ يدأبان في سيرهما وإنارتهما ودرئهما الظلمات، وإصلاحهما ما يصلحان من الأرض والأبدان والنبات وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ يتعاقبان خلفة لمعاشكم وسباتكم «1» وَآتاكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ ما سَأَلْتُمُوهُ من للتبعيض، أى آتاكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه، نظراً في مصالحكم. وقرئ من كلّ بالتنوين، وما سألتموه نفى ومحله النصب على الحال أى: آتاكم من جميع ذلك غير سائليه، ويجوز أن تكون ما موصولة، على: وآتاكم من كل ذلك ما احتجتم إليه ولم تصلح أَحوالكم ومعايشكم إلا به، فكأنكم سألتموه أو طلبتموه بلسان الحال لا تُحْصُوها لا تحصروها ولا تطيقوا عدها وبلوغ آخرها، هذا إذا أَرادوا أَن يعدوها على الإجمال. وأمّا التفصيل فلا يقدر عليه ولا يعلمه إلا الله لَظَلُومٌ يظلم النعمة بإغفال شكرها كَفَّارٌ شديد الكفران لها. وقيل ظلوم في الشدّة يشكو ويجزع، كفار في النعمة يجمع ويمنع. والإنسان للجنس، فيتناول الإخبار بالظلم والكفران من يوجدان منه.
