Q 14:35–36 · Vol. 2, pp. 557–558

Verses 35 to 36

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.'" (35) "'My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people. So whoever follows me, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful.'" (36)
وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِناً وَاجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ الْأَصْنامَ (35) رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ فَمَنْ تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي وَمَنْ عَصانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (36)
Vol. 2, p. 557
"This city" means the Sacred City, God increased it in security and sufficed it against every aggressor and wrongdoer; He answered in it the supplication of His intimate friend Abraham ﷺ. "Secure" means possessing security.
هَذَا الْبَلَدَ يعنى البلد الحرام، زاده الله أَمناً، وكفاه كل باغ وظالم، أَجاب فيه دعوة خليله إبراهيم عليه السلام آمِناً ذا أمن.
Question
If you ask: what is the difference between His saying "make this a secure city" (ijʿal hādhā baladan āminan) and His saying "make this city secure" (ijʿal hādhā al-balada āminan)?
فإن قلت: أَى فرق بين قوله اجْعَلْ هذا بَلَداً آمِناً وبين قوله اجْعَلْ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِناً؟
Answer
I say: in the first he asked that He make it among the number of the cities whose people are secure and have no fear; in the second, that He bring it out of a state of fear in which it was to its opposite of security, as though he said: "It is a place of fear, so make it secure." "And keep me away": it has also been read wa-ajnibnī; in it there are three dialects: janabahu al-sharr, jannabahu and ajnabahu; the people of the Ḥijāz say jannabanī sharrahu with doubling, and the people of Najd
قلت: قد سأل في الأوّل أَن يجعله من جملة البلاد التي يأمن أهلها ولا يخافون، وفي الثاني أن يخرجه من صفة كان عليها من الخوف إلى ضدها من الأمن، كأنه قال: هو بلد مخوف، فاجعله آمناً وَاجْنُبْنِي وقرئ: وأجنبنى، وفيه ثلاث لغات: جنبه الشر، وجنبه، وأجنبه، فأهل الحجاز يقولون: جنبني شره بالتشديد، وأهل نجد
Vol. 2, p. 558
say jannabanī and ajnabanī. The meaning: keep us firm and make us persist in avoiding their worship. "And my sons": he meant his sons of his loins. Ibn ʿUyayna was asked: "How did the Arabs worship idols?" He said: "None of the descendants of Ismāʿīl worshipped an idol," and argued by His saying "and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols"; they were only stone pillars for each people; they said: "The House is a stone, so wherever we set up a stone it is in the position of the House," so they used to circle around that stone and call it the "dawwār"; so it was recommended that it be said "he performed ṭawāf around the House," and not said "he circled (dāra) around the House." "Indeed, they have led astray many among the people," so I seek refuge in You from Your not protecting me (1) and my sons from that; and they were made "misleaders" only because people went astray because of them, so it is as though they led them astray, as you say "the world tempted them and deceived them," that is, they were tempted by it and deceived because of it. "So whoever follows me," in my religion and was upright, a Muslim like me, "he is of me," that is, he is part of me, because of his great specialness to me and association with me; likewise "Whoever cheats us is not of us" (2), that is, he is not part of the believers, in the sense that cheating is not of their acts and attributes. "And whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful": You forgive him what has passed from him of his disobeying me if it occurs to him [to repent] and he renews obedience to me. It is also said: its meaning is "whoever disobeys me in what is less than associating partners [with God]."
جنبني وأجنبنى، والمعنى: ثبتنا وأدمنا على اجتناب عبادتها وَبَنِيَّ أراد بنيه من صلبه. وسئل ابن عيينة: كيف عبدت العرب الأصنام؟ فقال: ما عبد أحد من ولد إسماعيل صنما، واحتج بقوله وَاجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ الْأَصْنامَ إنما كانت أنصاب حجارة لكل قوم، قالوا: البيت حجر، فحيثما نصبنا حجراً فهو بمنزلة البيت، فكانوا يدورون بذلك الحجر ويسمونه الدوار، فاستحب أن يقال: طاف بالبيت، ولا يقال: دار بالبيت إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ فأعوذ بك أن تعصمني «1» وبنىّ من ذلك، وإنما جعلن مضلات، لأنّ الناس ضلوا بسببهنّ، فكأنهنّ أضللنهم، كما تقول: فتنتهم الدنيا وغرّتهم، أى افتتنوا بها واغتروا بسببها فَمَنْ تَبِعَنِي على ملتي وكان حنيفا مسلما مثلي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي أى هو بعضى لفرط اختصاصه بى وملابسته لي، وكذلك قوله «من غشنا فليس منا» «2» أى ليس بعض المؤمنين، على أنّ الغش ليس من أفعالهم وأوصافهم وَمَنْ عَصانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ تغفر له ما سلف منه من عصياني إذا بدا له فيه واستحدث الطاعة لي. وقيل: معناه ومن عصاني فيما دون الشرك.

1. (1) . قوله «فأعوذ بك أن تعصمني» لعله أن لا تعصمني. (ع)
2. . أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبى هريرة وابن حبان من حديث ابن مسعود وإسحاق والبزار من حديث ابن عمر. والبخاري في التاريخ. والطبراني في الأوسط من حديث البراء. والبزار من حديث عائشة. وابن أبى شيبة من حديث أبى الحمراء. والحاكم من رواية عمير بن سعيد النخعي وابن أبى شيبة من رواية جميع بن عمير عن خالد بن برزة والطبراني من حديث أبى موسى والبيهقي في الشعب من طريق حسين بن عبد الله بن ضمرة عن أبيه عن جده عن على بن أبى طالب رضى الله عنه، كذلك أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب، وأخرجه الطبراني من هذا الوجه. فلم يذكر عليا. وأخرجه أبو نعيم عن أنس وعن إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن عبد الله بن أبى ربيعة عن جده به.

Q 14:37 · Vol. 2, pp. 558–560

Verse 37

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that perhaps they will be grateful." (37)
رَبَّنا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ الْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنا لِيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ (37)
Vol. 2, p. 558
"Some of my descendants": some of my children, and they are Ismāʿīl and whoever was born from him. "In a valley": it is the valley of Mecca; "uncultivated": there is nothing in it of crops at all, as in His saying "an Arabic Qurʾān without any crookedness," meaning that no crookedness is found in it, there is in it only straightness and nothing else. It was called "the sacred House" (al-bayt al-muḥarram) because God forbade molesting it or taking it lightly, and made what is around it sacred because of its position; or because it has always been inviolable and mighty, feared by every tyrant, like a forbidden thing that is due to be avoided; or because it is respected, of great sanctity, not lawful to violate; or because it was made forbidden to the Flood, that is, protected from it, as it was called "ancient" (ʿatīq) because it was freed from it and the Flood did not seize it. "That they may establish prayer": the lām is connected to "I settled," that is: I did not settle them in this valley, empty and barren of every convenience and means of livelihood, except that they may establish
مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بعض أولادى وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه بِوادٍ هو وادى مكة غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ لا يكون فيه شيء من زرع قط، كقوله قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ بمعنى لا يوجد فيه اعوجاج، ما فيه إلا الاستقامة لا غير. وقيل للبيت المحرم، لأنّ الله حرم التعرض له والتهاون به، وجعل ما حوله حرما لمكانه، أو لأنه لم يزل ممنعا عزيزا يهابه كل جبار، كالشىء المحرم الذي حقه أن يجتنب، أو لأنه محترم عظيم الحرمة لا يحل انتهاكه، أو لأنه حرّم على الطوفان أى منع منه، كما سمى عتيقا لأنه أعتق منه فلم يستول عليه لِيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ اللام متعلقة بأسكنت، أى: ما أسكنتهم هذا الوادي الخلاء البلقع من كل مرتفق ومرتزق، إلا ليقيموا
Vol. 2, p. 559
prayer near Your sacred House, and make it flourish with Your remembrance and worship and with what Your mosques and places of worship are made to flourish with, seeking blessing from the place You have honored above other places, seeking felicity in Your noble neighborhood, drawing near to You by devotion at Your House and circumambulating it and bowing and prostrating around it, calling down the mercy with which You have favored the inhabitants of Your sanctuary. "Hearts among the people": hearts from among the hearts of the people, and "min" is partitive; and the proof of it is what is reported from Mujāhid: "Had he said 'the hearts of the people,' Persia and Byzantium would have crowded you upon it." It is also said: had he not said "min," they would have crowded upon it, even Byzantines, Turks and Indians. It is also possible that "min" is for the starting point, as you say "the heart is ill, from me," meaning "my heart," so it is as though it were said "the hearts of people"; the annexed-to was made indefinite in this illustration only for the indefiniteness of "hearts," because in the verse it is indefinite so as to cover some of the hearts. It has also been read āfidatan, on the pattern of ʿāqidatan. There are two ways [of explaining] it: one is that it is from inversion, as you say ādur for adʾur; the second is that it is an active participle from afadat al-riḥla, when it was hastened, that is: a group or groups traveling to them and hastening toward them. It has also been read afidatan, with two ways [of explanation]: that the hamza be dropped for lightening, though the way is to lighten it by pronouncing it between [hamza and its vowel letter]; and that it be from afida. "Incline toward them" means hasten to them and fly toward them in longing and yearning, from [the poet's] saying: "he swoops down upon its mountain passes like the swoop of the falcon (1)." It has also been read tuhwā ilayhim, in the passive voice, from hawā ilayhi and ahwāhu another; and tahwā ilayhim, from hawiya, yahwā when he loves, containing the sense of "yearn," so it was made transitive as that is. "And provide for them from the fruits," despite their dwelling in a valley
الصلاة عند بيتك المحرم، ويعمروه بذكرك وعبادتك وما تعمر به مساجدك ومتعبداتك، متبركين بالبقعة التي شرفتها على البقاع، مستسعدين بجوارك الكريم، متقربين إليك بالعكوف عند بيتك، والطواف به، والركوع والسجود حوله، مستنزلين الرحمة التي آثرت بها سكان حرمك أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ أفئدة من أفئدة الناس، ومن للتبعيض، ويدل عليه ما روى عن مجاهد: لو قال أَفئدة الناس لزحمتكم عليه فارس والروم، وقيل: لو لم يقل مِنْ لازدحموا عليه حتى الروم والترك والهند. ويجوز أن يكون مِنْ للابتداء، كقولك: القلب منى سقيم، تريد قلبي، فكأنه قيل: أفئدة ناس، وإنما نكرت المضاف إليه في هذا التمثيل لتنكير أفئدة، لأنها في الآية نكرة ليتناول بعض الأفئدة. وقرى: آفدة، بوزن عاقدة. وفيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون من القلب كقولك: آدر، في أدؤر. والثاني: أن يكون اسم فاعلة من أفدت الرحلة إذا عجلت، أى، جماعة أو جماعات يرتحلون إليهم ويعجلون نحوهم. وقرئ: أفدة، وفيه وجهان: أن تطرح الهمزة للتخفيف، وإن كان الوجه أن تخفف بإخراجها بين بين. وأن يكون من أفد تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ تسرع إليهم وتطير نحوهم شوقا ونزاعا من قوله: يَهْوِى مَخَارِمَهَا هُوِىَّ الأَجْدَلِ «1» وقرئ: تهوى إليهم، على البناء للمفعول، من هوى إليه وأهواه غيره. وتهوى إليهم، من هوى يهوى إذا أحب، ضمن معنى تنزع فعدّى تعديته وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ مع سكناهم
Vol. 2, p. 560
a valley in which there is nothing of them, by having them brought to them from [other] lands: "that perhaps they will be grateful": grateful for the favor of being provided kinds of fruits present in a desolate valley (1) in which there is neither herb nor tree nor water. No wonder that God, Mighty and Majestic, answered his supplication and made it a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of all things are brought as provision from Him; then He preferred it, in the existence of the kinds of fruits in it, over every fertile region and over the most fertile of lands and the richest in fruits; and in whichever land of the East and West you will see the wonder that God shows you in an uncultivated valley, namely the gathering of the early fruits and the fruits (2) of different seasons, of spring, summer and autumn, in a single day, and that is not astonishing among His signs. May God grant us enjoyment through dwelling in His sanctuary, give us success in thanking His favors, and perpetuate for us the honor of coming under the supplication of Abraham ﷺ and provide us a portion of the soundness of that sound heart.
واديا ما فيه شيء منها، بأن تجلب إليهم من البلاد لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ النعمة في أن يرزقوا أنواع الثمرات حاضرة في واد يباب ليس فيه نجم «1» ولا شجر ولا ماء لا جرم أن الله عز وجل أجاب دعوته فجعله حرما آمنا تجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنه، ثم فضله في وجود أصناف الثمار فيه على كل ريف وعلى أخصب البلاد وأكثرها ثمارا، وفي أى بلد من بلاد الشرق والغرب ترى الأعجوبة التي يريكها الله بواد غير ذى زرع، وهي اجتماع البواكير والفواكه «2» المختلفة الأزمان من الربيعية والصيفية والخريفية في يوم واحد، وليس ذلك من آياته بعجيب، متعنا الله بسكنى حرمه، ووفقنا لشكر نعمه، وأدام لنا التشرف بالدخول تحت دعوة إبراهيم عليه السلام، ورزقنا طرفا من سلامة ذلك القلب السليم.

Transmitted by Muslim from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra, and Ibn Ḥibbān from the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, and Isḥāq and al-Bazzār from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar; and al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh; and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the ḥadīth of al-Barāʾ; and al-Bazzār from the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾisha; and Ibn Abī Shayba from the ḥadīth of Abū al-Ḥamrāʾ; and al-Ḥākim from the transmission of ʿUmayr b. Abī Ṭālib ؓ; al-Bayhaqī transmitted it thus in al-Shuʿab, and al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it by this route without mentioning ʿAlī. And Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it from Anas and from Ismāʿīl b. 1. (1) . قوله «فأعوذ بك أن تعصمني» لعله أن لا تعصمني. (ع)
2. . أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبى هريرة وابن حبان من حديث ابن مسعود وإسحاق والبزار من حديث ابن عمر. والبخاري في التاريخ. والطبراني في الأوسط من حديث البراء. والبزار من حديث عائشة. وابن أبى شيبة من حديث أبى الحمراء. والحاكم من رواية عمير بن سعيد النخعي وابن أبى شيبة من رواية جميع بن عمير عن خالد بن برزة والطبراني من حديث أبى موسى والبيهقي في الشعب من طريق حسين بن عبد الله بن ضمرة عن أبيه عن جده عن على بن أبى طالب رضى الله عنه، كذلك أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب، وأخرجه الطبراني من هذا الوجه. فلم يذكر عليا. وأخرجه أبو نعيم عن أنس وعن إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن عبد الله بن أبى ربيعة عن جده به.
Vol. 2, p. 559
1. (1). "When the pebble is cast at him, you see him leaping at its fall, the leap of the Akhyal [bird]. / And when he starts up from sleep, you see him rising as the ankle bone rises, not feeble. / And when you hurl him into the wide ways, you see him swooping down its passes like the swoop of the falcon. / And when you look at the lines of his face, they gleam like the lightning of the overhanging cloud, wet." By Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī, describing Taʾabbaṭa Sharran as vigilant and brave. He says: when you cast a pebble at him, testing him to see whether he is asleep or awake, "yanzū," that is, he leaps quickly; "ṭumūr al-Akhyal," that is, the leaping of the Akhyal, that is, he rises as it rises; it is a bird that the Arabs take as an ill omen, and its origin is from takhayyul, and it is said from khuyalāʾ. "Rataba rutūban": he stood upright, he rose in rising; that is: I saw him rise from the ground like the rising of the ankle bone. Al-zamil, al-zimāl and al-zamīl (with doubled mīm in them) is the weak one wrapped in his garments. Then he said: and when you cast him into the sides of wide places, you see him swooping down on its passes, that is, he hurries in following its narrow paths, like the swoop of the ajdal, which is the falcon, that is, like its speed in flying. It is also related "al-jandal," which is the stone. Al-asirra are the lines of the forehead, plural of sirār. Al-ʿāriḍ is the cloud overhanging the horizon. Al-mutahallil is the gleaming, or the high one that will rain. It is reported from ʿĀʾisha ؓ that she said: "I was sitting spinning near the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was mending his sandal, and his forehead dripped sweat, which generated a light in my eye; so I began to look at him, and he said: 'What are you looking at?' and I told him that, and said: 'By God, if the Hudhalī saw you, he would know that you are more deserving of his verse.' He said: 'And what did he say?' I said: 'And when you look at the lines of his face...' the verse. So he put down what was in his hand and stood, and kissed what is between my eyes and said: 'May God reward you well; I was not as pleased as I am by your words.'" [.....]
1. (1) . فإذا نبذت له الحصاة رأيته
…. ينزو لوقعتها طمور الأخبل وإذا يهب من المنام رأيته
…. كرتوب كعب الساق ليس بزمل وإذا رميت به الفجاج رأيته
…. يهوى مخارمها هوى الأجدل وإذا نظرت إلى أسرة وجهه
…. برقت كبرق العارض المتبلل لأبى كبير الهذلي، يصف تأبط شراً بالتيقظ والشجاعة، يقول: إذا رميت له الحصاة مجرباً له هل هو نائم أو صاح، ينزو: أى يثب بسرعة، طمور الأخيل: أى وثوب الأخيل، أى ينهض كنهوضه: وهو طير تتشاءم منه العرب، وأصله من التخيل، وقيل من الخيلاء. ورتب رتوباً: انتصب انتصاباً وارتفع ارتفاعاً، أى: رأيته يرتفع عن الأرض كارتفاع كعب الساق. والزمل والزمال والزميل- بتشديد الميم فيها-: هو الضعيف الملتف بثيابه، ثم قال: وإذا قذفته في نواحي الأمكنة المتسعة، رأيته يهوى مخارمها، أى: يسرع في سلوك مسالكها الضيقة، كهوى الأجدل وهو الصقر، أى كاسراعه في الطيران. ويروى: الجندل وهو الحجر. والأسرة: خطوط الجبهة جمع سرار. والعارض: السحاب المعترض في الأفق. والمتهلل: اللامع، أو المرتفع الذي سيمطر. وروى عن عائشة رضى الله عنها أنها قالت: كنت قاعدة أغزل عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يخصف نعله، فنحضر جبينه عرفا، فتولد في عينى نوراً، فجعلت أنظر إليه فقال: ما تنظرين؟ فقلت له ذلك، وقلت: أما والله لو رآك الهذلي لعلم أنك أحق بشعره، فقال: وما قال: قلت: وإذا نظرت
…. البيت. فوضع ما في يده وقام فقبل ما بين عينى وقال: جزاك الله خيرا، ما سررت كسرورى بكلامك. [.....]

Q 14:38–39 · Vol. 2, pp. 560–561

Verses 38 to 39

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from God on the earth or in the heaven." (38) "Praise to God, who has granted me in old age Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication." (39)
رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ ما نُخْفِي وَما نُعْلِنُ وَما يَخْفى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ (38) الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى الْكِبَرِ إِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعاءِ (39)
Vol. 2, p. 560
The repeated call is a proof of humble entreaty and taking refuge in God, Exalted is He. "Indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare": You know the secret as You know the manifest, with a knowledge in which there is no disparity, because no unseen thing is veiled from You. The meaning is: You know better our conditions and what sets us right and what corrupts us, and You are more merciful to us and more sincere in counsel to us than we are to ourselves; so there is no need for supplication and asking; we supplicate You only to show servitude to You, humility before Your greatness, abasement before Your might, need of what is with You, eagerness to obtain Your gifts, and yearning for Your mercy, and as the servant fawns before his master, and desire to receive his kindness, even though the master is amply possessed of good dominion. It is related of one of them that he raised his need to a generous man and the success was slow in coming to him, so he wished to remind him and said: "One like you is not reminded out of regarding it as short, nor out of supposing heedlessness of the needs of the askers; but the one in need does not let his need leave him from speaking about it." It is also said: "what we conceal" of yearning because of the separation that occurred between us, "and what we declare" of weeping and supplication. It is also said: "what we conceal" of the dejection of separation, "and what we declare": he means what passed between him and Hājar when she said to him at the farewell: "To whom do you leave us?" He said: "To God I leave you." She said: "Did God command you this?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then we shall not fear; You left us to One who suffices." "And nothing is hidden from God" is from the speech of God, Mighty and Majestic, confirming Abraham ﷺ as in His saying "and thus they will do"; or from the speech of Abraham, meaning: nothing is hidden from God, who is the Knower of the unseen, in any place. "Min" is for total inclusion, as though it were said: "and nothing is hidden from Him"
النداء المكرر دليل التضرع واللجأ إلى الله تعالى إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ ما نُخْفِي وَما نُعْلِنُ تعلم السرَّ كما تعلم العلن علماً لا تفاوت فيه، لأنّ غيباً من الغيوب لا يحتجب عنك. والمعنى: أنك أعلم بأحوالنا وما يصلحنا وما يفسدنا منا، وأنت أرحم بنا وأنصح لنا منا بأنفسنا ولها، فلا حاجة إلى الدعاء والطلب، وإنما ندعوك إظهارا للعبودية لك، وتخشعا لعظمتك، وتذللا لعزتك، وافتقارا إلى ما عندك، واستعجالا لنيل أياديك، وولهاً إلى رحمتك، وكما يتملق العبد بين يدي سيده، ورغبة في إصابة معروفه، مع توفر السيد على حسن الملكة. وعن بعضهم: أنه رفع حاجته إلى كريم فأبطأ عليه النجح، فأراد أن يذكره فقال: مثلك لا يذكر استقصارا ولا توهما للغفلة عن حوائج السائلين، ولكن ذا الحاجة لا تدعه حاجته أن لا يتكلم فيها. وقيل: ما نخفى من الوجد لما وقع بيننا من الفرقة، وما نعلن من البكاء والدعاء. وقيل: ما نخفى من كآبة الافتراق، وما نعلن: يريد ما جرى بينه وبين هاجر حين قالت له عند الوداع: إلى من تكلنا؟ قال: إلى الله أكلكم. قالت: آلله أمرك بهذا؟ قال: نعم. قالت: إذن لا نخشى، تركتنا إلى كاف وَما يَخْفى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ من كلام الله عز وجل تصديقا لإبراهيم عليه السلام، كقوله وَكَذلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ أو من كلام إبراهيم، يعنى: وما يخفى على الله الذي هو عالم الغيب من شيء في كل مكان. «ومن» للاستغراق، كأنه قيل: وما يخفى عليه
Vol. 2, p. 561
anything. "ʿAlā" in His saying "in old age" means "with," as in the verse: "Indeed I, despite what you see of my old age, know from where the shoulder is eaten (1)." It stands in the position of a circumstantial clause, and its meaning is: He granted me [children] while I was old and in the state of old age. It is related that Ismāʿīl was born to him when he was ninety-nine years old and Isḥāq when he was one hundred and twelve; and it is also related that Ismāʿīl was born to him when he was sixty-four and Isḥāq when he was ninety. On the authority of Saʿīd b. Jubayr: no child was born to Abraham until after one hundred and seventeen years. He mentioned the state of old age only because the favor of granting a child is greater in it, since it is the state in which despair of begetting has set in, and attaining one's need on the heels of despair is among the greatest and sweetest of blessings in the soul of the one who attains it, and because begetting at that advanced age was a sign for Abraham. "Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication": he had supplicated his Lord and asked Him for a child, saying: "My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous," so he thanked God for the honor He showed him by answering him.
شيء ما. عَلَى في قوله عَلَى الْكِبَرِ بمعنى مع، كقوله: إنِّى عَلَى مَا تَرَيْنَ مِنْ كِبَرِى … أَعْلَمُ مِنْ حَيْثُ تُؤْكَلُ الْكَتِفُ «1» وهو في موضع الحال، معناه: وهب لي وأنا كبير وفي حال الكبر. روى أنّ إسماعيل ولد له وهو ابن تسع وتسعين سنة، وولد له إسحاق وهو ابن مائة وثنتى عشرة سنة، وقد روى أنه ولد له إسماعيل لأربع وستين. وإسحاق لتسعين. وعن سعيد بن جبير: لم يولد لإبراهيم إلا بعد مائة وسبع عشرة سنة، وإنما ذكر حال الكبر لأنّ المنة بهبة الولد فيها أعظم، من حيث أنها حال وقوع اليأس من الولادة. والظفر بالحاجة على عقب اليأس من أجلّ النعم وأحلاها في نفس الظافر، ولأنّ الولادة في تلك السنّ العالية كانت آية لإبراهيم إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعاءِ كان قد دعا ربه وسأله الولد، فقال: رب هب لي من الصالحين، فشكر لله ما أكرمه به من إجابته
Question
If you ask: God, Exalted is He, hears every supplication, whether He answers it or not.
فإن قلت: الله تعالى يسمع كل دعاء، أجابه أو لم يجبه.
Answer
I say: it comes from your saying "the king heard the speech of so-and-so," when he took it into account and accepted it; and from it comes "God hears whoever praises Him." And in the ḥadīth (2): "God has not listened to anything as He listens to a prophet who chants the Qurʾān (3)."
قلت: هو من قولك: سمع الملك كلام فلان إذا اعتد به وقبله. ومنه: سمع الله لمن حمده. وفي الحديث «2» «ما أذن الله لشيء كإذنه لنبي يتغنى بالقرآن «3» »
Question
If you ask: what is this annexation, the annexation of "al-samīʿ" to "al-duʿāʾ"?
فإن قلت: ما هذه الإضافة إضافة السميع إلى الدعاء؟
Answer
I say: it is the annexation of the attribute to its object, and its origin is "samīʿun al-duʿāʾ" [hearer of supplication]. Sībawayh mentioned faʿīl among the forms of intensification that govern like the verb, as in your saying: "this is a striker of Zayd (ḍarrūb Zaydan), and a striker of his brother (ḍarrāb akhāhu), and a slaughterer of his camels (minḥār ibilihi), and one wary of matters (ḥadhir umūran), and one merciful to his father (raḥīm abāhu)." It is also possible that it is an annexation of faʿīl to its agent, so that the supplication of God is made "hearing" by figurative attribution, and what is meant is God's hearing.
قلت: إضافة الصفة إلى مفعولها، وأصله لسميع الدعاء. وقد ذكر سيبويه فعيلا في جملة أبنية المبالغة العاملة عمل الفعل، كقولك: هذا ضروب زيداً، وضراب أخاه، ومنحار إبله، وحذر أموراً، ورحيم أباه ويجوز أن يكون من إضافة فعيل إلى فاعله، ويجعل دعاء الله سميعا على الإسناد المجازى. والمراد سماع الله.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 560
1. (1). His statement "fī wādin yabāb laysa fīhi najm": that is, ruined. Al-najm is a plant with no stalk, thus in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "wa-hiya ijtimāʿ al-bawākīr wa-l-fawākih": al-bākūra is the first of the fruit, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «في واد يباب ليس فيه نجم» أى خراب. والنجم: نبات لا ساق له، كذا في الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قوله «وهي اجتماع البواكير والفواكه» الباكورة: أول الفاكهة، كما في الصحاح. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 561
1. (1). "Tarayna": its origin is tarʾayīna, on the pattern of tafʿalīna; the fatḥa of the hamza was transferred to the rāʾ, then the hamza was dropped, and the first yāʾ was dropped after being changed to an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa. He says: I, together with what you see of my old age and decrepitude, which ordinarily brings senility, am knowledgeable about affairs and alert to them. He alluded to that by saying "I know from where the shoulder is eaten," that is: I know the answer to this question. It is also related as "min ḥaythu," so "min" is perhaps redundant. Some said: the shoulder is eaten from its lower part, and eating it from its upper part is difficult; it is a proverb applied to the experienced man who is shrewd about affairs.
2. . Agreed upon, from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra ؓ.
3. . His statement "ka-idhnihi li-nabiyyin yataghannā bi-l-Qurʾān": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "ka-idhnihi li-man yataghannā ..." etc. (ʿ)
1. (1) . ترين: أصله ترأيين كتفعلين، نقلت فتحة الهمزة إلى الراء، ثم حذفت وحذفت الياء الأولى بعد قلبها ألفا لتحركها وانفتاح ما قبلها. يقول. إنى مع ما تنظرينه من كبرى وهرمى الموجب للخرف عادة، عارف بالأمور متيقظ لها. وكنى عن ذلك بقوله: أعرف من أين تؤكل الكتف، أى: أعرف جواب هذا الاستفهام، ويروى: من حيث، فلعل من زائدة. قال بعضهم: تؤكل الكتف من أسفلها ويشق أكلها من أعلاها، وهو مثل يضرب للجرب المتفطن للأمور.
2. . متفق عليه من حديث أبى هريرة رضى الله عنه.
3. . قوله «كاذنه لنبي يتغنى بالقرآن» في الصحاح: كاذنه لمن يتغنى
…. الخ. (ع)

Q 14:40–41 · Vol. 2, pp. 561–562

Verses 40 to 41

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication." (40) "Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established." (41)
رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي رَبَّنا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعاءِ (40) رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسابُ (41)
Vol. 2, p. 561
"And from my descendants": and some of my descendants, a conjunction upon the accusative [pronoun] in "make me"; he said "some" only because he knew, through God's informing him, that there would be disbelievers among his descendants, and that is His saying "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers." "And accept my supplication": that is,
وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي وبعض ذرّيتى، عطفا على المنصوب في اجعلنى، وإنما بعض لأنه علم بإعلام الله أنه يكون في ذرّيته كفار، وذلك قوله لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ. وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعاءِ أى
Vol. 2, p. 562
my worship. "And I withdraw from you and from what you invoke besides God." In the reading of Ubayy: wa-li-abawayya. Saʿīd b. Jubayr read: wa-li-wālidī, in the singular, meaning his father. Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī ؓ both, read: wa-li-waladayya, meaning Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq. It has also been read: li-wuldī, with ḍamma on the wāw; al-wuld has the sense of al-walad, like al-ʿudm and al-ʿadam. It is also said that it is the plural of walad, like usd in asad. In some codices: wa-li-dhurriyyatī.
عبادتي وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَما تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ في قراءة أبىّ: ولأبوىّ. وقرأ سعيد بن جبير: ولوالدي، على الإفراد، يعنى أباه. وقرأ الحسن بن على رضى الله عنهما: ولولدىّ، يعنى إسماعيل وإسحاق. وقرئ: لولدي، بضم الواو. والولد بمعنى الولد، كالعدم والعدم. وقيل: جمع ولد، كأسد في أسد. وفي بعض المصاحف: ولذرّيتى.
Question
If you ask: how was it permissible for him to ask forgiveness for his parents when they were disbelievers?
فإن قلت: كيف جاز له أن يستغفر لأبويه وكانا كافرين؟
Answer
I say: it is among the things that reason permits (1), and the impermissibility of its permissibility cannot be known except through revelatory notification (tawqīf). It is also said that by "his parents" he meant Adam and Eve. It is also said that [he asked] on condition of Islam. His saying "except the saying of Abraham to his father, 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you'" rejects this, because if he had stipulated Islam, it would have been a valid asking of forgiveness about which there is nothing to say, so how could valid forgiveness-seeking be excepted from the whole of what is imitated in Abraham? "The Day the account is established": that is, becomes firm, and it is borrowed from the standing of one who stands over a man, and the proof for it is their saying: "the war stood on its leg." Similar is their saying: tarajjalat al-shams, when the sun rose and its light became firm, as though it stood on a foot. It is also possible that the standing of its people is attributed to the account by figurative attribution, or that it is like "and ask the town." On the authority of Mujāhid: God answered him in what he asked: no one of his descendants worshipped an idol after his supplication, and He made the land secure, provided its people with fruits, made him an imām, placed among his descendants those who establish prayer, showed him his rites, and turned to him in forgiveness. On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, that he said: al-Ṭāʾif was part of the land of Palestine; when Abraham said "Our Lord, I have settled..." the verse, God lifted it and put it where He put it, as provision for the Sanctuary.
قلت: هو من مجوّزات العقل «1» لا يعلم امتناع جوازه إلا بالتوقيف. وقيل: أراد بوالديه آدم وحواء. وقيل: بشرط الإسلام. ويأباه قوله إِلَّا قَوْلَ إِبْراهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ لأنه لو شرط الإسلام لكان استغفاراً صحيحا لا مقال فيه، فكيف يستثنى الاستغفار الصحيح من جملة ما يؤتسى فيه بإبراهيم يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسابُ أى يثبت، وهو مستعار من قيام القائم على الرجل، والدليل عليه قولهم: قامت الحرب على ساقها. ونحوه قولهم: ترجلت الشمس: إذا أشرقت وثبت ضوؤها، كأنها قامت على رجل. ويجوز أن يسند إلى الحساب قيام أهله إسناداً مجازيا، أو يكون مثل وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ وعن مجاهد: قد استجاب الله له فيما سأل، فلم يعبد أحد من ولده صنما بعد دعوته، وجعل البلد آمنا، ورزق أهله من الثمرات. وجعله إماما، وجعل في ذريته من يقيم الصلاة، وأراه مناسكه، وتاب عليه. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أنه قال: كانت الطائف من أرض فلسطين، فلما قال إبراهيم رَبَّنا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ الآية، رفعها الله فوضعها حيث وضعها رزقا للحرم.

Q 14:42–43 · Vol. 2, pp. 562–564

Verses 42 to 43

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]," (42) "hurrying, with heads raised, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts a void." (43)
وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غافِلاً عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ إِنَّما يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصارُ (42) مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُؤُسِهِمْ لا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَواءٌ (43)
Vol. 2, p. 562
Question
If you ask: God is exalted above forgetfulness and heedlessness, so how could the Messenger of God ﷺ who is the most knowing of people about Him, suppose Him heedless, so that it was said "And never think that God is unaware"?
فإن قلت: يتعالى الله عن السهو والغفلة، فكيف يحسبه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو أعلم الناس به غافلا حتى قيل وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غافِلًا؟
Answer
I say: if it is an address to the Messenger of God ﷺ there are two ways [of explaining] it. The first is confirmation of what he already held, namely that he does not suppose God heedless, like His saying "and never be of the polytheists" and "and do not invoke with God another god," just as it came in the command "O you who believe, believe in God and His Messenger." The second is that what is meant by the prohibition against supposing Him heedless is to give notice that He is aware of what the wrongdoers do, with nothing of it hidden from Him, and that He will punish them for the little and the much of it, by way of warning and threat, like His saying "and God is Knowing of what you do," meaning the warning. It is also possible that what is meant is: do not suppose Him to treat them with the treatment of
قلت: إن كان خطابا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ففيه وجهان. أحدهما التثبيت على ما كان عليه من أنه لا يحسب الله غافلا، كقوله وَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَلا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ، كما جاء في الأمر يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ والثاني: أنّ المراد بالنهى عن حسبانه غافلا، الإيذان بأنه عالم بما يفعل الظالمون، لا يخفى عليه منه شيء، وأنه معاقبهم على قليله وكثيره على سبيل الوعيد والتهديد كقوله: وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ يريد الوعيد. ويجوز أن يراد: ولا تحسبنه يعاملهم معاملة
Vol. 2, p. 563
the heedless one of what they do, but with the treatment of the watcher over them, who reckons even the speck on the date stone and the thin skin on it; and if it is an address to someone else, someone who might suppose Him heedless because of ignorance of His attributes, then there is no question in it. On the authority of Ibn ʿUyayna: it is consolation for the wronged and a threat to the wrongdoer; and it was said to him: who said this? He became angry and said: only someone who knew it said it. It has also been read yuʾakhkhiruhum, with nūn and with yāʾ. "Eyes will stare": that is, their eyes will not stay fixed in their places, because of the terror of what they see. "Hurrying" [muhṭiʿīn]: rushing toward the caller. It is also said: ihṭāʿ is that you turn your sight toward what is seen, keeping your gaze on it without blinking. "With heads raised" [muqniʿī ruʾūsihim]: raising them. "Their glance not returning to them": it does not come back to them that they blink with their eyes, that is: they do not blink, but their eyes are open and stretched wide without any movement of the eyelids; or: their sight does not return to them so that they might look at themselves. Al-hawāʾ: the void that no bodies occupy; it is used descriptively, so it is said "so-and-so's heart is hawāʾ" if he is cowardly, with no strength or boldness in his heart. It is also said of the fool: his heart is hawāʾ. Zuhayr said: "of the male ostriches, whose breast is void (1)," because the ostrich is a proverb for cowardice and foolishness. And Ḥassān said: "So you are hollow, craven, void (2)"
الغافل عما يعملون، ولكن معاملة الرقيب عليهم، المحاسب على النقير والقطمير، وإن كان خطابا لغيره ممن يجوز أن يحسبه غافلا، لجهله بصفاته، فلا سؤال فيه. وعن ابن عيينة: تسلية للمظلوم وتهديد للظالم، فقيل له. من قال هذا؟ فغضب وقال: إنما قاله من علمه. وقرئ: يؤخرهم، بالنون والياء تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصارُ أى أبصارهم لا تقرّ في أماكنها من هول ما ترى مُهْطِعِينَ مسرعين إلى الداعي. وقيل: الإهطاع أن تقبل ببصرك على المرئي تديم النظر إليه لا تطرف مُقْنِعِي رُؤُسِهِمْ رافعيها لا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ لا يرجع إليهم أن يطرفوا بعيونهم، أى: لا يطرفون، ولكن عيونهم مفتوحة ممدودة من غير تحريك للأجفان. أو لا يرجع إليهم نظرهم فينظروا إلى أنفسهم. الهواء: الخلاء الذي لم تشغله الأجرام، فوصف به فقيل: قلب فلان هواء إذا كان جبانا لا قوّة في قلبه ولا جرأة. ويقال للأحمق أيضا: قلبه هواء. قال زهير: مِنَ الظُّلْمَانِ جُؤْجُؤُهُ هَوَاءُ «1» لأنّ النعام مثل في الجبن والحمق. وقال حسان: فَأَنْتَ مُجَوَّفٌ نَخْبٌ هَوَاءُ «2»
Vol. 2, p. 564
On the authority of Ibn Jurayj: "and their hearts a void": empty of good, hollow of it. Abū ʿUbayda said: hollow, with no minds.
وعن ابن جريج أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَواءٌ صفر من الخير خاوية منه. وقال أبو عبيدة: جوف لا عقول لهم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 562
1. (1). His statement "it is among the things that reason permits": he means according to the school of the Muʿtazila, that reason may perceive a ruling without revelation, whereas the school of the Ahl al-Sunna holds that there is no ruling before revelation such that it could be perceived without it; so understand. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «هو من مجوزات العقل» يعنى على مذهب المعتزلة أن العقل قد يدرك الحكم بدون شرع، ومذهب أهل السنة أن لا حكم قبل الشرع حتى يدرك بدونه، فافهم. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 563
1. (1). "As though the saddle on her were upon a small-headed one, / of the male ostriches, whose breast is void, / knock-kneed, with ears cropped, for whom has ripened / in al-Sinn the tanūm and the āʾ." By Zuhayr b. Abī Sulmā, describing his she-camel. Al-ṣaʿl: the one whose head hair is bare, and the small-headed one. Al-ẓulmān: plural of ẓalīm, which is the young of the ostrich; al-juʾjuʾ: the chest. Al-hawāʾ: the empty, hollow one; he made its chest empty so that it would be quicker in going to its food. Al-aṣakk: the one whose knees knock together when he walks because of the length of his legs. Ṣalamahu: he cut it off; al-taṣlīm is intensive. It is said: ajnā al-thamar when the fruit ripened, and ajnat al-arḍ: its herbage and fertility became abundant. Al-sinn: the level place, and also the name of a specific place. Al-tanūm (on the pattern of tannūr): a tree whose husks split open to reveal a small grain which the people of the desert eat, its color predominantly black; it is said that it is the hemp tree. Al-āʾ: a genus of tree, the singular being āʾa; it is also said that it is the fruit of that tree, and the word is applied to a kind of sound. Al-tanūm is the subject of ajnā, that is, these two kinds became abundant for it in that place.
2. . "Hark, convey to Abū Sufyān from me: / you are hollow, craven, void; / that our swords have left ʿUbayd, / and ʿAbd al-Dār, with slave-girls as their masters. / You satirized Muḥammad, so I answered on his behalf, / and with God in that is the recompense. / Do you satirize him when you are no match for him? / Then the worse of you be ransom for the better of you! / Is he who satirizes the Messenger of God among you, / and he who praises him and supports him, the same? / For my father and his father and my honor / are a shield for the honor of Muḥammad against you." By Ḥassān, satirizing Abū Sufyān before his conversion to Islam. "Alā" is for alerting, and the one commanded to convey is not specified; one would have expected him to say "fa-innahu," that is, Abū Sufyān, but he addressed him with the censure because it is more enraging. It is also possible that the one commanded is Abū Sufyān, so that he is the vocative with the vocative particle omitted. Al-mujawwaf, al-nakhib and al-hawāʾ: empty of belly, or empty of heart of reason and courage. In place of this hemistich it is related: "mughalghalatan, for the concealment has gone." Al-mughalghala: the hot one, from al-ghulla (with ḍamma), which is intensity of thirst and heat; it is also said: the one transmitted from one place to another. Baraḥa (like samiʿa): it went and ceased; it is also said: it became manifest and clear, from barāḥ al-arḍ, which is the exposed part of it; so al-khafāʾ means concealment or secret. The attribution of leaving to the swords is a rational figure (majāz ʿaqlī), because they are the instrument of the act. ʿUbayd, in the diminutive, is a tribe, and likewise ʿAbd al-Dār; "sādatuhā" is the subject and "al-imāʾ" is its predicate, and the sentence is in the position of the second object of "taraktu," that is: they were made slaves who have no masters except women, and ʿAbd al-Dār was made likewise, meaning: we destroyed the men of those two [tribes], their noble leaders, so their nobles are the women and no one else; indeed it is possible that they are equal, the free women also, so that only the frail ones (al-raqāʾiq) remained. "Atahjūhu": a rebuking question, and the wāw after it is circumstantial (ḥāl), that is: that is not fitting. "Sharr" and "khayr" are of the type of the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), and they are distinguished by the dropping of their hamzas for lightness because of the frequency of their use, but what is intended by them here is the root of the attribute, not an excess in it; and "al-sharr" is Abū Sufyān, and the sentence is a supplication: he invoked against him that he be a ransom for the Messenger of God ﷺ and he presented it in a form of indeterminacy for the sake of fairness in speech, and therefore when those present heard it they said: this is half a verse that the Arabs have said, so hold to fairness. "Wa-a-man yahjū": a question of denial, that is, he who satirizes him among you and he who praises him and supports him among us are not equal. It is also possible that the hamza is for alerting or for the vocative, with the vocative omitted, that is: O people of Abū Sufyān, the one among you who satirizes the Messenger of God and the one who praises him and supports him are equal in the lack of any regard for them. It is also related as "fa-man," and a supplied estimation is necessary, that is: whoever satirizes him and forsakes him among you, so that forsaking corresponds to support as satire corresponds to praise. Then in this there is proof for the permissibility of omitting the relative pronoun (mawṣūl); the Kūfans and al-Akhfash permitted it, and Ibn Mālik followed them, on the condition that it be conjoined to another relative pronoun, as here. His saying "wa-wālidahu," that is, the father of my mother; it is also related as "wa-wālidatī." Al-wiqāʾ: that by which a harmful thing is guarded against, like the shield; [it is on the pattern of] al-ḥizām and al-ribāṭ, for the object of the action, so it is either in the sense of a passive participle or a noun of instrument; and I saw in the speech of al-Zamakhsharī what indicates that this pattern is called by the name of the passive participle. And in al-Hamʿ there is what indicates that it has come irregularly among the instrument patterns, like irāth for that by which fire is kindled, that is, set ablaze, and sirād for that with which one sews, that is, notches. When the Prophet ﷺ heard his saying "and with God in that is the recompense," he said: "May God reward you with Paradise, with goodness." And when he heard his saying "for my father," he said: "And may God protect you from the heat of the Fire, with goodness." The Prophet's approval ﷺ of requital by censure indicates permissibility.
1. (1) . كأن الرحل منها فوق صعل
…. من الظلمان جؤجؤه هواء أصك مصلم الأذنين أجنى
…. له بالسن تنوم وآء لزهير بن أبى سلمى يصف ناقته. والصعل: المنجرد شعر الرأس والصغير الرأس. والظلمان: جمع ظليم وهو ولد النعام، والجؤجؤ: الصدر. والهواء: الخالي الفارغ، وجعل صدره فارغا ليكون أسرع في السير إلى طعامه. والأصك: الذي تصطك ركبتاه عند المشي لطول رجليه. وصلمه: قطعه. والتصليم: مبالغة. ويقال: أجنى الثمر إذا أدرك، وأجنت الأرض: كثر كلؤها وخصيها. والسن، المكان المستوى واسم موضع بعينه. والتنوم- وزن تنور-: شجر تنفلق كمامه عن حب صغير تأكله أهل البادية، يغلب على لونه السواد. قيل: وهو شجر الشهدانج. والآء: جنس من الشجر واحده آءة. وقيل: ثمر ذلك الشجر يطلق على نوع من الصوت: والتنوم: فاعل أجنى، أى كثر له في ذلك المكان هذان النوعان.
2. . ألا أبلغ أبا سفيان عنى
…. فأنت مجوف نخب هواء بأن سيوفنا تركت عبيداً
…. وعبد الدار سادتها الإماء هجوت محمداً فأجبت عنه
…. وعند الله في ذاك الجزاء أتهجوه ولست له بكفء
…. فشركما لخيركما الفداء أمن يهجو رسول الله منكم
…. ويمدحه وينصره سواء فان أبى ووالده وعرضي
…. لعرض محمد منكم وقاء لحسان يهجو أبا سفيان قبل إسلامه. وألا التنبيه، والمأمور بالابلاغ غير معين، وكان الظن أن يقول: فانه، أى: أبا سفيان، لكن خاطبه بالذم لأنه أغيظ. ويجوز أن المأمور أبو سفيان، فهو منادى بحذف حرف النداء. والمجوف والنخب والهواء: خالي الجوف، أو فارغ القلب من العقل والشجاعة. وروى بدل هذا الشطر «مغلغلة فقد برح الخفاء» والمغلغلة: الحارة من الغلة بالضم، وهي شدة العطش والحرارة. وقيل. المنقولة من مكان لآخر، وبرح كسمع: ذهب وزال. وقيل: ظهر واتضح من براح الأرض وهو البارز منها، فالخفا بمعنى التستر أو السر. وإسناد الترك للسيوف مجاز عقلى، لأنها آلة للفعل. وعبيد بالتصغير قبيلة، وكذلك عبد الدار، وسادتها مبتدأ. والإماء خبره، والجملة في محل المفعول الثاني لتركت، أى صيرت عبيداً لا سادة لها إلا النساء، وصيرت عبد الدار كذلك، يعنى: أننا أفنينا رجالهما الرؤساء الأشراف، فأشرافهما النساء لا غير، بل يجوز أنهم سواء الحرائر أيضاً، فلم يبق إلا الرقائق. وأتهجوه: استفهام توبيخي، والواو بعده للحال، أى: لا ينبغي ذلك شر وخير، من قبيل أفعل التفضيل، واختصا بحذف همزتهما تخفيفاً لكثرة استعمالهما، لكن المراد بهما هنا أصل الوصف لا الزيادة فيه والشر أبو سفيان، والجملة دعائية، دعا عليه بأن يكون فداء الرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأبرزه في صورة الإبهام لأجل الانصاف في الكلام، ولذلك لما سمعه الحاضرون قالوا: هذا نصف بيت قالته العرب، فعليك بالانصاف وأمن يهجو: استفهام إنكارى، أى ليس من يهجوه منكم ومن يمدحه وينصره منا مستويين. ويحتمل أن الهمزة للتنبيه، أو للنداء، والمنادى محذوف، أى: يا قوم أبى سفيان إن الذي يهجو رسول الله منكم والذي يمدحه وينصره منكم مستويان في عدم الاكتراث بهما وروى: فمن، ولا بد من تقدير، أى: من يهجوه ويخذله منكم ليقابل الخذلان النصر كالهجو والمدح، ثم إن في هذا دليلا على جواز حذف الموصول، وقد أجازه الكوفيون والأخفش، وتبعهم أبو مالك، وشرط كونه معطوفا على موصول آخر كما هنا. وقوله: ووالده، أى والد أمى. ويروى: ووالدتي. والوقاء: ما يتوقى به المكروه، كالترس وزن الحزام والرباط للمفعول به الفعل، فهو إما بمعنى اسم مفعول أو اسم الآلة، ورأيت في كلام الزمخشري ما يفيد تسمية هذا الوزن باسم المفعول. وفي الهمع ما يفيد أنه جاء شاذا من أوزان الآلة، كأراث لما تؤرث به النار، أى تضرم به، وسراد لما يسرد به، أى يحزز به. ولما سمع صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله «وعند الله في ذلك الجزاء» قال: جزاك الله الجنة بإحسان. ولما سمع قوله «فان أبى» قال: وقال الله حر النار بإحسان. وتقريره صلى الله عليه وسلم على المكافأة بالذم، يدل على الجواز.
30
Q 14:44–47 · Vol. 2, pp. 564–566

Verses 44 to 47

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who wronged will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' [It will be said], 'Had you not sworn before that for you there would be no decline?'" (44) "And you lived among the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it had become clear to you how We dealt with them, and We presented for you the examples." (45) "And they had planned their plan, and with God is their plan, even if their plan were such as to remove the mountains." (46) "So do not think that God will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution." (47)
وَأَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذابُ فَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رَبَّنا أَخِّرْنا إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ نُجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ الرُّسُلَ أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا أَقْسَمْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ زَوالٍ (44) وَسَكَنْتُمْ فِي مَساكِنِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ كَيْفَ فَعَلْنا بِهِمْ وَضَرَبْنا لَكُمُ الْأَمْثالَ (45) وَقَدْ مَكَرُوا مَكْرَهُمْ وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ وَإِنْ كانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبالُ (46) فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انتِقامٍ (47)
Vol. 2, p. 564
"The Day the punishment comes to them" is a second object of "warn," and it is the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of "delay us for a short term" is: return us to the world and give us respite until a limit and bound of time that is near, in which we may make up for what we neglected of answering
يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذابُ مفعول ثان لأنذر وهو يوم القيامة. ومعنى أَخِّرْنا إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ ردّنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا إلى أمد وحدّ من الزمان قريب، نتدارك ما فرطنا فيه من إجابة
Vol. 2, p. 565
Your call and following Your messengers. Or the "day" is meant to be the day of their destruction by swift punishment, or the day of their death, tormented by the severity of the death throes and by meeting the angels without good tidings, and that on that day they will ask that their Lord delay them to a near term, like His saying "if only You would delay me for a short term, so I could give charity." "Had you not sworn": [this is said] on the intent of the saying, and there are two ways [of understanding] it: that they say it out of arrogance and insolence, and because of the habit of ignorance and foolishness that had overtaken them; and that they say it with the tongue of their condition, in that they built solidly and hoped far. "For you [there is no]" is the answer to the oath, and it came in the form of the second person only because of His saying "you swore"; had the wording of those who swore been reported, it would have said: "for us there is no decline." The meaning: you swore that you would remain in the world, not departing through death and annihilation. It is also said: you would not be transferred to another abode, meaning their disbelief in the resurrection, like His saying "And they swear by God their strongest oaths that God will not resurrect one who dies." One says: sakana al-dār and sakana fīhā. From it comes His saying "and you lived among the dwellings of those who wronged themselves," because sukna comes from sukūn, which is staying, and the origin is that it is made transitive with "fī," as you say qarra fī al-dār, ghaniya fīhā, and aqāma fīhā; but when it was transferred to a specific sukūn it was handled freely, so it was said sakana al-dār, as it was said tabawwaʾahā and awṭanahā. It is also possible that it is sakanū (1), from sukūn, that is: they settled in them and were at ease, with contented souls, following the path of those before them in wrongdoing and corruption, not recounting to themselves what the earlier peoples met of the days of God and how the end of their wrongdoing was, so that they might take warning and be deterred. "And it became clear to you" by report and by witnessing "how We destroyed them and took vengeance on them." It has also been read: wa-nubayyina lakum, with nūn. "And We presented for you the examples": that is, the descriptions of what they did and what was done to them, and these are, in their strangeness, like the proverbs coined for every wrongdoer. "And they had planned their plan": that is, their great plan, in which they exhausted their effort. "And with God is their plan": it must be annexed either to the agent, like the first, in the sense: their plan is recorded with God, so He will requite them for it with a plan greater than it; or annexed to the object, in the sense: with God is their plan with which He plans against them (2), which is their punishment that they deserve, which He brings to them from where they do not perceive or reckon. "Even if their plan were such as to remove the mountains": even if their plan were great and extreme in severity, so the removal of the mountains by it is set forth as an illustration of its enormity and severity, that is: even if their plan were fashioned to remove the mountains and prepared for that. It has also been taken that "in" is a negative particle and the lām confirms it, like His saying "and God would not have let your faith be lost." The meaning: it is impossible that the mountains be removed by their plan, with the mountains as a figure for God's signs and laws, because they stand in the position of firm mountains in steadfastness and fixity. This is supported by the reading of Ibn
دعوتك واتباع رسلك. أو أريد باليوم: يوم هلاكهم بالعذاب العاجل، أو يوم موتهم معذبين بشدّة السكرات ولقاء الملائكة بلا بشرى، وأنهم يسألون يومئذ أن يؤخرهم ربهم إلى أجل قريب، كقوله لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ. أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا أَقْسَمْتُمْ على إرادة القول، وفيه وجهان: أن يقولوا ذلك بطرا وأشرا، ولما استولى عليهم من عادة الجهل والسفه، وأن يقولوه بلسان الحال حيث بنوا شديداً وأمّلوا بعيداً. وما لَكُمْ جواب القسم، وإنما جاء بلفظ الخطاب لقوله أَقْسَمْتُمْ ولو حكى لفظ المقسمين لقيل: ما لنا مِنْ زَوالٍ والمعنى أقسمتم أنكم باقون في الدنيا لا تزالون بالموت والفناء. وقيل. لا تنتقلون إلى دار أخرى يعنى كفرهم بالبعث، كقوله وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ يقال: سكن الدار وسكن فيها. ومنه قوله تعالى وَسَكَنْتُمْ فِي مَساكِنِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ لأنّ السكنى من السكون الذي هو اللبث، والأصل تعدّيه بفي، كقولك: قرّ في الدار وغنى فيها وأقام فيها، ولكنه لما نقل إلى سكون خاص تصرف فيه فقيل: سكن الدار كما قيل: تبوّأها وأوطنها. ويجوز أن يكون: سكنوا «1» ، من السكون، أى: قرّوا فيها واطمأنوا طيبي النفوس، سائرين سيرة من قبلهم في الظلم والفساد، لا يحدّثونها بما لقى الأوّلون من أيام الله وكيف كان عاقبة ظلمهم، فيعتبروا ويرتدعوا وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ بالإخبار والمشاهدة كَيْفَ أهلكناهم وانتقمنا منهم. وقرئ: ونبين لكم، بالنون وَضَرَبْنا لَكُمُ الْأَمْثالَ أى صفات ما فعلوا وما فعل بهم، وهي في الغرابة كالأمثال المضروبة لكل ظالم وَقَدْ مَكَرُوا مَكْرَهُمْ أى مكرهم العظيم الذي استفرغوا فيه جهدهم وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ لا يخلوا إمّا أن يكون مضافا إلى الفاعل كالأوّل، على معنى: ومكتوب عند الله مكرهم، فهو مجازيهم عليه بمكر هو أعظم منه، أو يكون مضافا إلى المفعول على معنى: وعند الله مكرهم الذي يمكرهم «2» به، وهو عذابهم الذي يستحقونه يأتيهم به من حيث لا يشعرون ولا يحتسبون وَإِنْ كانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبالُ وإن عظم مكرهم وتبالغ في الشدة، فضرب زوال الجبال منه مثلا لتفاقمه وشدته، أى: وإن كان مكرهم مسوى لإزالة الجبال. معداً لذلك، وقد جعلت إن نافية واللام مؤكدة لها، كقوله تعالى وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمانَكُمْ والمعنى: ومحال أن تزول الجبال بمكرهم، على أنّ الجبال مثل لآيات الله وشرائعه، لأنها بمنزلة الجبال الراسية ثباتاً وتمكناً. وتنصره قراءة ابن
Vol. 2, p. 566
Masʿūd: "and their plan was not." It has also been read: la-tazūlu, with the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ), meaning: even if their plan were of such severity that the mountains would be removed by it and uprooted from their places. ʿAlī and ʿUmar ؓ both, read: wa-in kāda makruhum. "Failing His promise to His messengers": he means His saying "Indeed We will surely support Our messengers," and "God has decreed: I shall surely prevail, I and My messengers."
مسعود: وما كان مكرهم. وقرئ: لتزول، بلام الابتداء، على: وإن كان مكرهم من الشدّة بحيث تزول منه الجبال ونتقلع من أماكنها. وقرأ على وعمر رضى الله عنهما: وإن كاد مكرهم مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ يعنى قوله إِنَّا لَنَنْصُرُ رُسُلَنا، كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي.
Question
If you ask: why was it not said "mukhlifa rusulihi waʿdahu"? And why was the second object put before the first (1)?
فإن قلت: هلا قيل: مخلف رسله وعده؟ ولم قدم المفعول الثاني على الأوّل «1» ؟
Answer
I say: the promise was put first to make known that He does not fail the promise at all, as in His saying "Indeed, God does not fail in the appointment"; then He said "His messengers" to give notice that if He does not fail His promise to anyone, and failing promises is not among His attributes, how could He fail it to His messengers, who are His chosen and elect? It has also been read: mukhlifa waʿdahu rusulihi, with the genitive for "messengers" and the accusative for "promise." This is as weak as the reading of the one who read "qatla awlādahum shurakāʾihim." "Exalted in Might": overcoming, who cannot be out-planned; "Owner of Retribution" for His friends against their enemies.
قلت: قدم الوعد ليعلم أنه لا يخلف الوعد أصلا، كقوله إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعادَ ثم قال رُسُلَهُ ليؤذن أنه إذا لم يخلف وعده أحداً- وليس من شأنه إخلاف المواعيد- كيف يخلفه رسله الذين هم خيرته وصفوته؟ وقرئ: مخلف وعده رسله، بجرّ الرسل ونصب الوعد. وهذه في الضعف كمن قرأ «قتل أولادهم شركائهم» . عَزِيزٌ غالب لا يماكر ذُو انتِقامٍ لأوليائه من أعدائه.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 565
1. (1). His statement "wa-yajūzu an yakūna sakanū": perhaps it should be sakantum. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "wa-ʿinda Allāhi makruhum alladhī yamkuruhum bihi": what is in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-makr is stratagem and deceit, and "makara bihi"; al-makr is also red ochre, and "makarahu fa-mtakara," that is, he dyed him and he was dyed, etc.; and this indicates that makr in the sense of stratagem is not made transitive by itself, so reflect. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «ويجوز أن يكون سكنوا» لعله: سكنتم. (ع)
2. . قوله «وعند الله مكرهم الذي يمكرهم به» الذي في الصحاح المكر: الاحتيال والخديعة، وقد مكر به. والمكر أيضاً: المغرة، وقد مكره فامتكر، أي خضبه فاختضب اه، وهو يفيد أن المكر بمعنى الاحتيال لا يتعدى بنفسه، فتدبر. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 566
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "If you ask: why was the second object put before the first, etc.?" Aḥmad said: There is something to consider in what he said, because when a verb is restricted by an object its absoluteness is cut off, so putting the promise first in the verse is not proof of the absoluteness of the verb with respect to the one promised, such that the mention of the messengers would stand apart, like an outsider, from the first absoluteness; and there is no difference in the meaning he mentioned between putting the mention of the messengers first or last; and putting the second object first does nothing except give notice of care for the speaker's intended aim; and the matter is of this order in the verse, because it was revealed in the context of warning and threatening the wrongdoers with what God, Exalted is He, threatened them through the tongues of the messengers, so what matters in the threat is the mention of the threat. As for its being through the tongues of the messengers, that is a matter on which the intimidation does not necessarily depend, so that even if the threat from God, Exalted is He, were supposed to come through no messenger's tongue, the fear of it would be sufficient on its own. And God knows best.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت لم قدم المفعول الثاني على الأول
…. الخ» ؟ قال أحمد: وفيما قاله نظر، لأن الفعل متى تقيد بمفعول انقطع إطلاقه، فليس تقديم الوعد في الآية دليلا على إطلاق الفعل باعتبار الموعود، حتى يكون ذكر الرسل بائناً كالأجنبى من الإطلاق الأول، ولا فرق في المعنى الذي ذكره بين تقديم ذكر الرسل وتأخيره ولا يفيد تقديم المفعول الثاني إلا الإيذان بالعناية في مقصود المتكلم والأمر بهذه المثابة في الآية، لأنها وردت في سياق الانذار والتهديد للظالمين بما توعدهم الله تعالى به على ألسنة الرسل، فالمهم في التهديد ذكر الوعيد. وأما كونه على ألسنة الرسل فذلك أمر لا يقف التخويف عليه ولا بد، حتى لو فرض التوعد من الله تعالى على غير لسان رسول، لكان الخوف منه حسبياً كافياً، والله أعلم.
31
Q 14:48–51 · Vol. 2, pp. 566–568

Verses 48 to 51

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come out before God, the One, the Prevailing," (48) "and you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles," (49) "their garments of liquid pitch, and their faces will be covered by the Fire," (50) "so that God may recompense every soul for what it earned. Indeed, God is swift in account." (51)
يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّماواتُ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ (48) وَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الْأَصْفادِ (49) سَرابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرانٍ وَتَغْشى وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ (50) لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ ما كَسَبَتْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ (51)
Vol. 2, p. 566
"The Day the earth is replaced": its accusative is as a substitute for "the Day it comes to them," or as an adverb of time for "retribution." The meaning: the day when this earth that you know is replaced by another earth, other than this known one, and likewise the heavens. Tabdīl is change, and it may be in essences, as you say: baddaltu al-darāhim danānīr [I exchanged the dirhams for dīnārs]; and from it comes "We replaced them with other skins" and "We replaced their two gardens with two gardens"; and in attributes, as you say: baddaltu al-ḥalqa khātaman, when you melted the band and fashioned it into a ring, moving it from one shape to another; and from it comes His saying "for those, God will replace their evil deeds with good deeds." There is disagreement about the replacement of the earth and the heavens. It is said: their attributes are replaced, so its mountains are removed from the earth and its seas gush forth, and it is leveled so that no crookedness or unevenness is seen in it. On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās: it is that same earth, but it will be changed, and he recited:
يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ انتصابه على البدل من يوم يأتيهم. أو على الظرف للانتقام. والمعنى: يوم تبدّل هذه الأرض التي تعرفونها أرضاً أخرى غير هذه المعروفة، وكذلك السموات. والتبديل: التغيير، وقد يكون في الذوات كقولك: بدّلت الدراهم دنانير. ومنه بَدَّلْناهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَها وبَدَّلْناهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ وفي الأوصاف، كقولك: بذلت الحلقة خاتماً، إذا أذبتها وسويتها خاتماً، فنقلتها من شكل إلى شكل. ومنه قوله تعالى فَأُوْلئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ واختلف في تبديل الأرض والسموات، فقيل: تبدّل أوصافها فتسير عن الأرض جبالها وتفجر بحارها. وتسوّى فلا يرى فيها عوج ولا أمت. وعن ابن عباس: هي تلك الأرض وإنما تغير، وأنشد:
Vol. 2, p. 567
"And the people are not the people whom you knew, nor is the abode the abode that you used to know (1)." And the heaven is replaced by the scattering of its stars, the eclipse of its sun, the lunar eclipse of its moon, its splitting, and its becoming doors. It is also said: in their place another earth and other heavens will be created. On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd and Anas: people will be gathered on a white earth on which no one has committed a sin. On the authority of ʿAlī ؓ: an earth of silver and heavens of gold will be substituted. On the authority of al-Ḍaḥḥāk: an earth of silver, white like sheets. It has also been read: yawma nubaddilu al-arḍa, with nūn (2).
وَمَا النَّاسُ بِالنَّاسِ الّذِينَ عَهِدْتَهُمْ … وَلَا الدَّارُ بِالدَّارِ الّتِى كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ «1» وتبدّل السماء بانتثار كواكبها، وكسوف شمسها، وخسوف قمرها، وانشقاقها، وكونها أبوابا. وقيل: يخلق بدلها أرض وسموات أخر. وعن ابن مسعود وأنس: يحشر الناس على أرض بيضاء لم يخطئ عليها أحد خطيئة. وعن على رضى الله عنه: تبدّل أرضا من فضة، وسموات من ذهب. وعن الضحاك: أرضاً من فضة بيضاء كالصحائف. وقرئ: يوم نبدّل الأرض، بالنون «2» .
Question
If you ask: how did He say "the One, the Prevailing"?
فإن قلت: كيف قال الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ؟
Answer
I say: it is like His saying "To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To God, the One, the Prevailing," because when dominion belongs to one who is overpowering, who is neither overcome nor resisted, so that no one has a helper to turn to other than Him nor any protector, the matter is of the utmost difficulty and severity. "Bound together": some of them bound to others; or to the devils; or their hands bound to their feet, in fetters. His saying "in shackles" is either connected with "bound together," that is: they are bound together in shackles; or it is not connected with it, so that the meaning is: bound together, shackled. Al-aṣfād: fetters; it is also said: chains; and he recited from Salāma b. Jandal: "And Zayd al-Khayl has met with shackles, biting at the forearm and the bone of the shin (3)." Al-qaṭirān: it has three forms: qaṭirān, qaṭrān and qiṭrān, with fatḥa or kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ [in the latter two]. It is what is drawn from a tree called al-abhal and then boiled, with which mangy camels are smeared, and it burns the mange and the skin by its heat and sharpness, and its heat may reach the inside; it is characteristic of it that fire catches in it quickly, and it may be used as lamp fuel; it is black in color and foul in smell. The skins of the people of the Fire will be smeared with it until its coating becomes for them like garments, that is, shirts, so that four things combine upon them: the sting of the tar, its burning, the fire's swift catching in their skins, and the repulsive color and the stench of its smell. Indeed, the difference between the two tars is like the difference between the two fires, and for everything that God has promised or has been promised in the Hereafter, between it and what we witness of its kind there is a difference beyond measure, and it is as though we have of it only the names, while the things named are there. So by His wide generosity we seek refuge from His wrath, and we ask Him for success in what saves us from His punishment. It has also been read: min qaṭrin ānin; al-qaṭr: copper or molten brass; al-ānī: that whose heat has reached its utmost. "And their faces will be covered by the Fire": like His saying "Then is he who shields with his face the worst of the punishment on the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces
"
قلت: هو كقوله لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ لأنّ الملك إذا كان لواحد غلاب لا يغالب ولا يعازّ فلا مستغاث لأحد إلى غيره ولا مستجار، كان الأمر في غاية الصعوبة والشدّة مُقَرَّنِينَ قرن بعضهم مع بعض. أو مع الشياطين. أو قرنت أيديهم ألى أرجلهم مغللين. وقوله فِي الْأَصْفادِ إمّا أن يتعلق بمقرّنين، أى: يقرنون في الأصفاد. وإمّا أن لا يتعلق به، فيكون المعنى: مقرّنين مصفدين. والأصفاد: القيود: وقيل الأغلال، وأنشد لسلامة بن جندل: وَزَيْدُ الْخَيْلِ قَدْ لَاقَى صِفَاداً … بَعَضُّ بِسَاعِدٍ وَبِعَظْمِ سَاقِ «3» القطران: فيه ثلاثة لغات: قطران، وقطران، وقطران: بفتح القاف وكسرها مع سكون الطاء، وهو ما يتحلب من شجر يسمى الأبهل فيطبخ، فتهنأ به الإبل الجربي، فيحرق الجرب بحرّه وحدّته، والجلد، وقد تبلغ حرارته الجوف، ومن شأنه أن يسرع فيه اشتعال النار، وقد يستسرج به، وهو أسود اللون منتن الريح، فتطلى به جلود أهل النار حتى يعود طلاؤه لهم كالسرابيل وهي القمص، لتجتمع عليهم الأربع: لذع القطران. وحرقته، وإسراع النار في جلودهم، واللون الوحش، ونتن الريح. على أن التفاوت بين القطرانين كالتفاوت بين النارين، وكل ما وعده الله أو وعد به في الآخرة، فبينه وبين ما نشاهد من جنسه من لا يقادر قدره، وكأنه ما عندنا منه إلا الأسامى والمسميات ثمة، فبكرمه الواسع نعوذ من سخطه، ونسأله التوفيق فيما ينجينا من عذابه. وقرئ: من قطران، والقطر: النحاس أو الصفر المذاب. والآنى: المتناهي حرّه وَتَغْشى وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ كقوله تعالى أَفَمَنْ يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ، يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ
Vol. 2, p. 568
because the face is the most precious place in the outward body and its noblest, like the heart in the inward, and for that reason He said "which rises over the hearts." It has also been read: wa-taghshā wujūhahum, in the sense of tataghashshā. That is: what is done to the criminals is done "so that God may recompense every soul" that is criminal "for what it earned," or every soul, criminal and obedient, because when He punishes the criminals for their criminality, [it follows] that He rewards the obedient for their obedience.
لأن الوجه أعز موضع في ظاهر البدن وأشرفه، كالقلب في باطنه، ولذلك قال تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ وقرئ: وتغشى وجوههم، بمعنى تتغشى: أى يفعل بالمجرمين ما يفعل لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ مجرمة ما كَسَبَتْ أو كل نفس من مجرمة ومطيعة لأنه إذا عاقب المجرمين لإجرامهم على أنه يثيب المطيعين لطاعتهم.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 566
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "If you ask: why was the second object put before the first, etc.?" Aḥmad said: There is something to consider in what he said, because when a verb is restricted by an object its absoluteness is cut off, so putting the promise first in the verse is not proof of the absoluteness of the verb with respect to the one promised, such that the mention of the messengers would stand apart, like an outsider, from the first absoluteness; and there is no difference in the meaning he mentioned between putting the mention of the messengers first or last; and putting the second object first does nothing except give notice of care for the speaker's intended aim; and the matter is of this order in the verse, because it was revealed in the context of warning and threatening the wrongdoers with what God, Exalted is He, threatened them through the tongues of the messengers, so what matters in the threat is the mention of the threat. As for its being through the tongues of the messengers, that is a matter on which the intimidation does not necessarily depend, so that even if the threat from God, Exalted is He, were supposed to come through no messenger's tongue, the fear of it would be sufficient on its own. And God knows best.

…. الخ» ؟ قال أحمد: وفيما قاله نظر، لأن الفعل متى تقيد بمفعول انقطع إطلاقه، فليس تقديم الوعد في الآية دليلا على إطلاق الفعل باعتبار الموعود، حتى يكون ذكر الرسل بائناً كالأجنبى من الإطلاق الأول، ولا فرق في المعنى الذي ذكره بين تقديم ذكر الرسل وتأخيره ولا يفيد تقديم المفعول الثاني إلا الإيذان بالعناية في مقصود المتكلم والأمر بهذه المثابة في الآية، لأنها وردت في سياق الانذار والتهديد للظالمين بما توعدهم الله تعالى به على ألسنة الرسل، فالمهم في التهديد ذكر الوعيد. وأما كونه على ألسنة الرسل فذلك أمر لا يقف التخويف عليه ولا بد، حتى لو فرض التوعد من الله تعالى على غير لسان رسول، لكان الخوف منه حسبياً كافياً، والله أعلم.
Vol. 2, p. 567
1. (1). He says: the people today are not the people whom you knew before, because of the passing away of the living among them, and the abode today is not the abode that you knew, because its conditions have been replaced and its attributes changed.
2. . His statement "wa-quriʾa nubaddilu al-arḍa with nūn": perhaps [it should say] "and with the accusative of al-arḍ and al-samāwāt"; so let the reading be verified. (ʿ)
3. . By Salāma b. Jandal. Zayd al-Khayl: he is the one whom the Prophet ﷺ named Zayd al-Khayr. "Qad lāqā": that is, he received from his enemies ṣifād, that is, a fetter and a chain. He borrowed biting for the pinching of the dry, hard fetter, in the manner of the explicit metaphor; the bāʾ is for attachment, and the word "bone" was inserted for exaggeration in the biting, until it reached the bone. [.....]
1. (1) . يقول: ليس الناس اليوم هم الناس الذين عهدتهم سابقا، لفناء الأحياء من بينهم، وليست الدار اليوم هي الدار التي كنت تعلمها، لتبدل أحوالها وتغير أوصافها.
2. . قوله «وقرئ نبدل الأرض بالنون» لعله ونصب الأرض والسماوات، فلتحرر. القراءة. (ع)

Vol. 2, p. 568
1. (1). His statement "from nadhira bihi when he knew it": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "nadhira al-qawm bi-l-ʿaduww," with kasra on the dhāl, when they knew. (ʿ)
2. . Its chain of transmission will come at the end of the book.
1. (1) . قوله «من نذر به إذا علمه» في الصحاح: نذر القوم بالعدو- بكسر الذال- إذا علموا. (ع)
2. . يأتى إسناده في آخر الكتاب.

Q 14:52 · Vol. 2, p. 568

Verse 52

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"This is a notification for the people that they may be warned by it and that they may know that He is but one God and that those of understanding may be reminded." (52)
هذا بَلاغٌ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ وَلِيَذَّكَّرَ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ (52)
Vol. 2, p. 568
"This is a notification for the people": a sufficiency in reminding and exhortation; by "this" He means what He described from His saying "So do not think" to "swift in account." "And that they may be warned": a conjunction upon an omitted element, that is: that they may be advised and that they may be warned "by it," by this notification. It has also been read: wa-li-yandharū, with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from nadhira bihi when he knew it (1) and prepared for it. "And that they may know that He is but one God": because when they fear what they were warned of, the fear calls them to reflection until they arrive at tawḥīd, since fear is the mother of all good. On the authority of the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Sūrat Ibrāhīm will be given a reward of ten good deeds, equal to the number of everyone who worshipped idols and the number of those who did not." (2)
هذا بَلاغٌ لِلنَّاسِ كفاية في التذكير والمواعظة، يعنى بهذا ما وصفه من قوله فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ إلى قوله سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ. وَلِيُنْذَرُوا معطوف على محذوف، أى لينصحوا ولينذروا بِهِ بهذا البلاغ. وقرئ: ولينذروا، بفتح الياء، من نذر به إذا علمه «1» واستعدّ له وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ لأنهم إذا خافوا ما أنذروا به، دعتهم المخافة إلى النظر حتى يتوصلوا إلى التوحيد، لأنّ الخشية أمّ الخير كله. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «من قرأ سورة إبراهيم أُعطى من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد كل من عبد الأصنام وعدد من لم يعبد» «2»
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 568
1. (1). His statement "from nadhira bihi when he knew it": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "nadhira al-qawm bi-l-ʿaduww," with kasra on the dhāl, when they knew. (ʿ)
2. . Its chain of transmission will come at the end of the book.
1. (1) . قوله «من نذر به إذا علمه» في الصحاح: نذر القوم بالعدو- بكسر الذال- إذا علموا. (ع)
2. . يأتى إسناده في آخر الكتاب.
